title: Quality and Reliability Engineer (Advance Packaging & Assembly)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact:
We are seeking a Manufacturing Quality and Reliability Engineer to join the Foundry QnR team at our Penang site, supporting Intel's advanced packaging programs (EMIB, Foveros).


This role spans silicon processing and wafer-level assembly (WLA) flows, and key interfaces with packaging substrates and 2.5D EMIB technology. You will help ensure that products and processes meet rigorous quality and reliability standards from wafer fabrication through packaging and assembly. The position directly influences manufacturing performance, yield, reliability, and customer satisfaction by driving robust quality control, disciplined excursion management, and continuous process improvement. You will also have the opportunity to represent Quality and Reliability in development forums, Silicon and Advanced Packaging factory operations, and Substrate suppliers.


Key Responsibilities

  • Apply Advanced Packaging expertise to assess inline process health, excursion impact, yield risk, defect mechanisms, and downstream packaging implications.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive effective root cause analysis, systemic corrective and prevention actions using 8D and related problem-solving methodologies.
  • Partner with fab manufacturing, substrates assembly, test, process engineering, and quality teams to strengthen early excursion detection, process controls, in-line screens, and outgoing quality.
  • Drive quality control improvements devising incoming/ outgoing quality controls, using statistical process control, defect pareto analysis, control plans, audit learnings, and excursion prevention indicators across fab, substrate manufacturing, and assembly manufacturing steps.

title: E-core CPU Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We created the Intel Atom Processor (E-Core), a disruptive technology that enables a broad range of devices including entry PC's, smartphones, modems, 2 in 1 laptops, micro-servers, and other Internet-of-Things IoT devices. You will be part of a team, participating in the design of a future generation high performance Intel Atom microprocessor. This role requires a engineer with strong analytic and problem solving skill, an ability to communicate well, and willing to share and discuss issues. You will work on implementation of CPU Core blocks from synthesis through post-layout verification and tapeout. You will develop the custom constraints for driving synthesis and Auto-Place and Route APR tools to implement and optimize the design to meet aggressive timing and power goals. You will work closely with micro-architecture, RTL, and custom circuit teams to converge the design to project targets.


The responsibilities will be tailored to the candidate's skills and expertise and will include several of the following, but not be limited to

  • Logic synthesis and place and route for CORE IP blocks.
  • Performing floor-planning and routing studies and implementation
    Block/sub-system level timing analysis.
  • Work on low power techniques and power reduction in sub-system.
  • Physical verification closure of block/sub-system.
  • Scripts writing for data analysis and recipe creation.
  • Strong analytical ability, problem solving and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and at various levels of abstraction.
  • Strong communication and team work skills.
  • Capable of working in a high performing team to deliver the results required from the organization.
  • Ability to work well in at team and be productive under aggressive schedules.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Must have either BS or MS in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering.

Minimum 5 year of experience in:

  • CPU physical design and timing verification.
  • Synthesis/APR flows on multi voltage high frequency designs including custom polygon editing.
  • Tcl scripting.
  • Noise, cross-talk, OCV analysis.
  • Floorplanning and physical design and timing closure.
  • Formal equivalence, DRC/LVS, IR and electro-migration checks.

Preferred qualifications:

  • 6+ years of experience with the above skill sets.
  • Experience with Fusion Compiler, DCT, DCE, ICC2, RedHawk, ICV, Conformal, Calibre, PrimeTime, StarRCXT.

title: Advanced Packaging Module Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Corporation is one of the world's leading semiconductor companies, driving innovation that shapes the future of computing, connectivity, and human progress. With decades of pioneering research and development, Intel is at the forefront of designing and manufacturing the world's most advanced chips and technologies. Our Oregon campus in Hillsboro is one of Intel's largest and most strategically important sites globally, serving as a hub for cutting-edge semiconductor research, development, and high-volume manufacturing. At Intel, we believe in the power of human ingenuity and are committed to creating an inclusive, collaborative environment where brilliant minds come together to solve the world's most complex technological challenges.

We are seeking a highly motivated and technically skilled Process Integration Engineer to join our dynamic team in Hillsboro, Oregon. In this critical role, you will be at the intersection of innovation and manufacturing, driving technology development and enablement for both high-volume manufacturing and next-generation semiconductor technologies. You will lead the design and development of sophisticated manufacturing processes, perform pathfinding activities for future device architectures, and collaborate with world-class suppliers and internal teams to push the boundaries of what's possible in semiconductor technology. This is a unique opportunity to make a meaningful impact on Intel's strategic roadmap and the broader semiconductor industry.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Technology Development & Enablement: Drive technology development for high-volume manufacturing and future technology nodes, providing process integration and equipment solutions to meet desired device specifications.
  • Process Design & Development: Lead the design and development of technically sophisticated manufacturing processes, including material selection, parameter optimization, equipment metrology, and system design to enable new product designs and functional requirements.
  • Pathfinding & Roadmap Development: Perform pathfinding activities in support of process and hardware development, enabling the manufacturing of innovative device architectures, and develop technology roadmaps for future product generations.
  • Manufacturing Optimization: Recommend and implement modifications to operating equipment to improve production efficiency, refine manufacturing techniques, and optimize production output for existing products.
  • Supplier Collaboration: Partner with key equipment and materials suppliers to develop and implement enabling elements of technology, building cost-sensitive roadmaps in collaboration with the vendor ecosystem.
  • Feasibility Studies: Perform process technology feasibility studies through theoretical simulations and practical engineering methods to validate new approaches and technologies.
  • Industry Awareness: Remain current on relevant industrial process and material manufacturing technical trends, developing a forward-looking view of Intel's future process technology needs to push the industry forward.
  • Statistical Analysis & Experimentation: Apply Statistical Process Control (SPC) and Design of Experiments (DOE) principles to drive data-informed decisions and process improvements.
  • Automation & Systems Development: Leverage hands-on experience with robotics, automation systems, vision systems, and image processing to advance manufacturing capabilities.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • A Natural Problem-Solver: You thrive when faced with complex challenges and approach them with creativity, curiosity, and a structured mindset.
  • Adaptable & Resilient: You embrace change and ambiguity, pivoting quickly when priorities shift without losing momentum or focus.
  • A Collaborative Team Player: You build strong relationships across teams, functions, and supplier ecosystems, knowing that the best outcomes come from working together.

  • Self-Motivated & Driven: You take ownership of your work, proactively seek out opportunities to improve processes, and are passionate about making a meaningful impact.
  • Detail-Oriented: You bring precision and rigor to everything you do, understanding that in semiconductor manufacturing, the smallest details can make the biggest difference.
  • Innovative & Forward-Thinking: You are passionate about staying ahead of industry trends and are energized by the opportunity to shape the future of semiconductor technology.

Are you ready to be part of a team that is literally building the future? At Intel's Hillsboro, Oregon campus, you'll have the resources, the talent, and the mission to do work that truly matters — not just for Intel, but for the world.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, or a related field with 4+ years of relevant industry experience; or a PhD degree in the same fields with 3+ years of relevant experience.
  • Relevant experience will be any of the following:
    • Technical expertise in semiconductor processing, system controls, opto-mechanics, or mechanical systems.

Preferred Qualifications:

As a Physical Design Engineer, you will play a critical role in driving the development of cutting-edge technologies at Intel. Your work will directly impact Intel's product innovation, addressing complex challenges in power, performance, and area optimization to shape the future of computing architectures. Collaborating with cross-disciplinary teams, the CTO plays a pivotal role in delivering impactful designs that support Intel's broader mission of creating world-changing technology.

- Drive RTL-to-GDS design convergence using advanced synthesis and place-and-route tools targeting performance, power, and area (PPA) goals.

- Proficiency in scripting languages such as Python, Perl, and TCL for design flow automation and debugging.
- Hands-on experience with debugging functional equivalence verification (FEV) and RV reports, including planning and implementing engineering change orders (ECOs).
- Strong understanding of chiplet integration and advanced packaging techniques.
- Experience leveraging AI tools to set up workflows, streamline debugging, and improve productivity.

Preferred Qualifications
- Expertise in static timing analysis of multiple interfaces (e.g., SerDes, UCIe) and experience with industry-standard EDA tools such as Cadence Virtuoso and Synopsys Fusion Compiler.

- Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across cross-functional teams, providing mentorship and guidance to junior engineers.
- Experience in both power-efficient and high-frequency physical design techniques with advanced tools and methodologies.

Join us in shaping the future of computing architectures. Your expertise and ideas will drive groundbreaking innovations in physical design and high-performance silicon solutions.

title: Senior CPU Architecture and Benchmarking Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role

Join Intel's architecture team as a Senior CPU Architecture and Benchmarking Engineer. You will drive rigorous, low-level investigations into CPU designs, crafting targeted microbenchmarks that expose microarchitectural behavior at fine granularity and translating those findings into actionable architectural guidance. Your work will bridge the gap between silicon measurement, software behavior, and architectural definition, playing a key role in shaping Intel's future CPU roadmap.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, implement, and analyze pinpointed microbenchmarks to explore and characterize low-level microarchitectural behavior including branch prediction, instruction fetch/decode, execution units, memory subsystem, prefetchers, and power delivery interactions
  • Investigate and document microarchitectural details of CPU designs through systematic benchmarking and analysis
  • Evaluate the impact of system software layers — including OS schedulers, runtime libraries, compilers, and firmware — on end-product CPU performance and power efficiency
  • Identify power/performance gaps and propose concrete architectural solutions and mitigations
  • Collaborate with silicon lab, simulation, backend, and RTL teams to correlate benchmarking findings with pre-silicon models and post-silicon measurements
  • Explore and evaluate proposed microarchitectural ideas in CPU performance simulators, providing quantitative measure of value
  • Develop and maintain tooling, test infrastructure, and analysis frameworks to support repeatable and scalable benchmarking workflows
  • Communicate technical findings clearly and persuasively in written reports and presentations to senior engineering and product teams

To Be Successful in This Role, You Should Demonstrate

  • Intellectual curiosity and a systematic mindset when investigating complex microarchitectural behavior, with the rigor to design experiments that yield clear, reproducible conclusions
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across silicon, simulation, and software teams to align findings and drive architectural decisions
  • The ability to communicate complex technical findings with clarity and confidence to both engineering peers and senior leadership audiences

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline with 8+ years of relevant industry experience, OR a Master's Degree in a related discipline with 6+ years of relevant industry experience
  • Deep understanding of out-of-order CPU microarchitecture, including pipeline stages, execution resources, memory hierarchy, and power/performance interactions
  • Demonstrated experience designing and interpreting low-level microbenchmarks for CPU characterization
  • Proficiency in assembly programming and low-level performance tooling (e.g., EMON/PMU counters, VTune, or equivalent)
  • Strong background in performance analysis methodologies, bottleneck identification, and quantitative trade-off evaluation
  • Proficiency in C/C++ and scripting languages (Python or similar) for benchmark development and data analysis

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with cycle-accurate CPU performance simulators and the ability to model and evaluate new microarchitectural features
  • Understanding of software stack impacts on CPU performance, including OS scheduler behavior, memory allocators, compiler code generation, and BIOS/firmware tuning
  • Experience reading or debugging RTL to investigate microarchitectural behavior or validate benchmark hypotheses
  • Track record of translating benchmarking insights into concrete architectural recommendations or published technical contributions

As a Semiconductor Research Engineer, you will drive scientific innovation and research that shapes the future of semiconductor technologies. This role focuses on designing, simulating, and developing novel devices, packages, and interconnects using device physics, electromagnetics, and advanced materials science. You'll lead hands-on experiments to build prototypes that demonstrate groundbreaking concepts and collaborate across teams to establish methodologies that optimize performance, reliability, and cost. Your contributions will directly impact Intel's advancements in assembly packaging platform technologies, ensuring the company remains at the forefront of the industry.

As part of this team, you'll contribute to Intel's mission of transforming technology landscapes and driving industry progress.

title: Senior Signal Integrity Engineer (Hands-on)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Central Engineering Group (CEG) team delivers best-in-class Ethernet products and is at the heart of Intel's transformation from a PC company to a company that powers the cloud and billions of smart, connected computing devices. CEG's compelling Ethernet products move the world's data and are the foundations of cloud service and telecommunications data centers. You will be exposed to High-Speed I/O protocols such as PCIeGen6-7, DDR5-6, and PAM4 Ethernet 224Gb, which are a part of our Ethernet Infrastructure Processing Unit (Intel IPU) and Foundation NIC (FNIC) Ethernet product lines. We propose a dynamic and flexible workplace position, working directly with highly capable design, system, and pre/post-silicon teams within the organization. Most of the team's engineers have 10+ years of experience, and we are looking for a highly skilled multidisciplinary engineer with proven experience in Signal Integrity engineering to lead the hardware design of our next division projects' challenges and be part of Ethernet networking's accelerated growth. In this position, as a signal integrity engineer, you will be responsible for modeling channel elements in 3D and 2D EM simulation tools for pre- and post-layout stages of package and platform design for PCIe, Ethernet, and memory interfaces. You are expected to have a thorough understanding of RF circuits and electromagnetic wave propagation; the role includes learning the specifications of each interface and the required design limitations that should be verified. You will be expected to lead all signal integrity activities related to multiple projects for various high-speed and low-speed interfaces utilizing traditional and automated tools. You will work closely with silicon design teams and Hard IP vendors and will be responsible for the model's correlation based on cross-section and electrical measurements at the post-manufacturing stage and modeling manufacturing variation impact on the channels. You will be responsible for running the sign-off simulation flows for various designs, providing feedback to the design teams, and being hands-on in the lab for experiments when required. You would also be responsible for identifying/qualifying new AI-based automation techniques and solutions and providing technical leadership to working groups/task forces through debugging and reviews.

Qualifications:

Required Skills and Experience
• B.Sc./M.Sc. Electrical Engineer with over 7 years of relevant experience in Signal Integrity
• Proven design experience in the semiconductor ASIC development industry is a MUST
• Proven planning and design flow buildup
• Proven experience with PCB technology and layout techniques (Analog and Digital) including stack-up, routing, and advance SI/PI consideration
• Proven hands-on experience with EDA tools: HFSS, CST, ADS, Simbeor, or equivalent
• Knowledge of CAD tools: Cadence Allegro or Mentor Expedition, or equivalent
• Proven experience with modeling and simulation one of the Ethernet, PCIe, DDR interfaces
• Familiar with layout technics
• Working experience with AI-based tools
• Lab hands-on experience in high-speed, low-speed, and clocks circuitry signals measurement such as high-end Oscilloscopes, VNA, TDR, BERT's, etc.
• Excellent debugging skills, ability to analyze problems, diagnose the root cause and apply corrective actions
• Ability to work as a team player and contribute in a cross-functional product team on a daily basis
• Strong verbal and written communication skills in English for interacting with design, evaluation and production engineers; customers; technical marketing engineers; and program managers

title: SoC Design Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Team:

You will be joining Intel's cutting-edge product development group, a team focused on designing and verifying advanced semiconductor solutions. This group is at the forefront of innovation, delivering high-quality, scalable products that drive Intel's leadership in technology and performance. By contributing your skills here, you will help shape the future of computing and enable groundbreaking advancements in the industry.


Position Overview:

As a SoC Design Verification Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring that Intel's complex System-on-Chip (SoC) designs meet functional specifications and deliver high-quality performance. You will design scalable and reusable verification plans, develop test environments, and execute tests to uncover issues and improve functionality. Your contributions will directly enhance Intel's product quality and ensure optimal performance in presilicon development.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Create and update UVM-based test bench generation and test case creation
  • Define and develop scalable and reusable block, subsystem, and SoC verification plans
  • Create test benches and verification environments that align with microarchitecture specifications
  • Execute verification plans, including emulation and system simulation models, to ensure design functionality and uncover bugs
  • Debug and root cause issues in presilicon environments, implementing corrective measures to address failures
  • Collaborate with architects, RTL developers, postsilicon teams, and physical design teams to improve verification of complex architectural features
  • Document and maintain test plans, driving technical reviews with design and architecture teams
  • Integrate security coverage activities within test plans, including regression and debug tests
  • Maintain and improve existing functional verification infrastructure and methodologies
  • Absorb learnings from postsilicon development and incorporate feedback into improved verification strategies.

To Be Successful, You Should Demonstrate the Following:

  • Ability to work collaboratively across interdisciplinary teams
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to work across interdisciplinary teams
  • Passion for tackling complex problems and delivering innovative solutions.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, with 7+ years of hands-on experience in SoC design verification, including demonstrated expertise in OVM/UVM methodologies, debugging, and test planningOR
  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, with 6+ years of hands-on experience in SoC design verification, including demonstrated expertise in OVM/UVM methodologies, debugging, and test planning.

The experience must include:

  • AMBA protocols such as CHI, AXI, AHB, and APB with industry-standard VIP from various EDA vendors
  • Creation and updating of UVM-based test benches and test case creation

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with postsilicon validation and incorporating feedback into presilicon test plans
  • Familiarity with emulation models and system simulation tools for performance analysis

Job Description: 

The Graphics Research Organization at Intel is seeking a highly motivated Research Scientist Intern to join its world-class team. This role offers an opportunity to help shape next-generation graphics technologies and experiences by conducting cutting-edge research in real-time 3D rendering, machine learning, and highly parallel algorithms. 


As an intern, you will collaborate with industry-leading researchers to develop innovative graphics and AI techniques. Your work may contribute directly to Intel's graphics hardware and software products while advancing the state of the art in both industry and academia through research publications. 


We are looking for curious, collaborative, and technically strong candidates who are passionate about graphics research, possess excellent communication skills, and are eager to explore new ideas that drive innovation.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field with a focus on computer graphics and machine learning.

title: Yield Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.


Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.


Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel


As a Yield Development Engineer, you will play a critical role in advancing Intel's cutting-edge semiconductor technologies. You will be part of a team responsible for driving yield improvement strategies that span the entire lifecycle of a technology node, from research and development through high-volume manufacturing. Your contributions will directly influence Intel's ability to maintain its leadership in the semiconductor industry, ensuring the success of innovative silicon solutions that shape the future of computing. Collaborating with cross-functional teams, you will develop methods and tools to analyze vast data sets, identify yield limiters, and implement process changes that enable Intel to achieve its yield milestones. This role promises an opportunity to shape groundbreaking technologies and generate impactful advancements for the industry and beyond. 


Responsibilities will include but will not be limited to:

  • Perform statistical analysis to construct accurate process development roadmaps and drive technology yield milestones. 
  • Analyze and consolidate diverse data sources to identify defect modes and create yield models. 
  • Develop multivariate algorithms for high-volume data analysis to identify root cause yield limiters. 
  • Extract insights from structured and unstructured data using machine learning, coding techniques, and advanced statistical methods. 
  • Collaborate with process integration, defect engineering, and electrical fault isolation teams to debug yield detractors and propose solutions. 
  • Conduct fault isolation and failure analysis to determine the root cause of yield-impacting issues. 
  • Develop tools and systems that transform manufacturing data into actionable yield improvement strategies. 
  • Work closely with design teams to resolve product-related yield issues and improve manufacturability. 
  • Execute new product introductions and participate in factory task forces to ensure process optimization.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your schoolwork, classes, research and/or relevant previous job and/or internship experiences.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Physical Sciences, Computer Science, or a related field and 3+ years of experience in semiconductor processing, semiconductor devices, or nanotechnology; OR
  • Master's degree in Engineering, Physical Sciences, Computer Science, or a related field and 2+ years of experience in semiconductor processing, semiconductor devices, or nanotechnology; OR
  • PhD in Engineering, Physical Sciences, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • 1+ years of experience in one of the following:
    • Proficiency in data analysis systems, and machine learning techniques.
    • Optical probing or metrology.
    • Expertise in Statistical Process Control (SPC) and Design of Experiments (DOE) principles.
    • Expertise in full-stack application development, software architecture, and cloud-based platforms

Preferred Qualifications:

  • PhD in Engineering, Physical Sciences, Computer Science, or a related field and 2+ years of experience in semiconductor processing, semiconductor devices, or nanotechnology.
  • 1+ years of experience in fault isolation, failure analysis tools, and techniques such as electrical testing, and layout studies.
  • Proven ability to collaborate in cross-functional teams and matrixed organizations.
  • Strong project management skills with demonstrated self-initiative and ability to drive strategic objectives in complex environments.
  • Expertise in semiconductor physics and advanced device interactions modeling.
  • Experience maintaining and troubleshooting semiconductor equipment.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and present yield strategies to technical and business stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in yield modeling methodologies

Take advantage of this opportunity to join Intel and shape the future of engineering. Apply today to be part of a team that drives industry-leading innovation and transformation.

title: Director of Supply Planning - Assembly, Test, and Materials
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role We are seeking a Director of Supply Planning for Assembly, Test and Materials to lead supply planning across our global semiconductor back-end manufacturing network. This leader is responsible for developing and managing the executable supply plan across assembly, test, and associated materials. The role translates end to end supply requirements and business priorities into a capacity, material, qualification, and flow feasible plan for the Assembly and Test network. The Director will lead a planning organization responsible for balancing manufacturing requirements across factories, anticipating constraints, developing recovery scenarios, and ensuring that capacity, materials, and manufacturing capabilities are synchronized to deliver committed supply. This role requires a leader who can operate at both strategic and operational levels. It involves building planning capabilities and processes while also leading the organization through complex supply, capacity, and material constraints. Key Responsibilities Assembly and Test Supply Planning Lead the development and execution of the supply plan across Assembly and Test manufacturing operations. Translate end to end supply requirements into executable stage level plans that optimize manufacturing capacity, cycle time, yield, qualifications, product mix, routing, and other manufacturing constraints. Own planning across the Assembly and Test network, including a worldwide network of internal manufacturing sites Ensure that Assembly and Test plans remain synchronized across with upstream die availability, materials availability, and downstream finished goods requirements. Materials Planning and Readiness Lead materials planning and readiness in support of the Assembly and Test supply plan. Translate manufacturing plans into requirements for materials such as substrates, lead frames, interposers, packaging components, and other critical materials. Partner closely with the procurement team to identify material shortages and supply risks early, quantify their impact to manufacturing and supply commitments, integrate supplier commitments, and develop mitigation and recovery scenarios. Constraint Management and Scenario Planning Identify current and emerging capacity, material, and manufacturing constraints across the Assembly and Test network. Lead scenario analysis to determine the impact of constraints and evaluate alternatives such as product reallocation, alternate manufacturing routes, capacity changes, material prioritization, and changes in production timing. Drive recovery planning when execution deviates from plan, working with the factory to ensure actions are prioritized based on their impact to supply and customer commitments. Stage Planning and Integration Serve as the primary Assembly, Test and Materials planning interface with Central Supply Planning, manufacturing operations, Procurement, engineering, product organizations, and other supply chain functions. Translate end to end requirements and priorities into feasible plans and provide timely feedback when Assembly, Test, or material constraints affect the end to end supply plan. Drive synchronization of capacity and material constraints across multiple manufacturing stages to reduce unnecessary WIP, queue time, expedites, replanning, and other non value added flow. Planning Execution and Performance Establish and manage a disciplined planning cadence that connects long term capacity and materials planning with tactical supply planning and near term manufacturing execution. Maintain clear accountability for planning performance and continuously improve the quality, stability, and executability of the supply plan. Establish and manage key performance indicators including: • Supply and commit performance • Stage plan and schedule performance • Material readiness and commit performance • Inventory and WIP health • Cycle time performance • Plan stability and planning accuracy • Constraint recovery Use performance data to identify systemic planning gaps and drive corrective actions across planning, manufacturing, materials, and business processes. Planning Systems and Capability Development Drive continuous improvement of supply-planning processes, systems, data, and decision-making capabilities. Ensure planning models accurately represent manufacturing capacity, product flows, BOMs, routings, yields, cycle times, lead times, qualifications, and material constraints. Improve advanced planning capabilities, including constraint-based planning, scenario analysis, exception management, and planning automation. Drive adoption and effective utilization of advanced planning platforms, including Blue Yonder or comparable supply planning solutions. Develop a planning organization that increasingly manages by exception and scenario rather than through manual expediting and transactional intervention. Leadership Responsibilities Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of Assembly, Test, and Materials supply-planning professionals. Create clear accountability across stage planning, Central Supply Planning, manufacturing operations, and Procurement. Develop planning talent capable of understanding both semiconductor manufacturing details and the broader supply chain implications of planning decisions. Create a culture of fact based decision making, early risk identification, cross-functional problem solving, and accountability for results. Communicate complex supply situations and tradeoffs clearly to senior executives and cross functional stakeholders. Influence decisions across organizational boundaries where the Director may not have direct authority but is accountable for driving an executable supply outcome. What Success Looks Like Success in this role means that Assembly, Test, and Materials operate from a single, credible, executable supply plan. Constraints are identified early enough to influence decisions. Material shortages are understood before they disrupt manufacturing. Capacity decisions are made based on end-to-end supply requirements rather than local utilization alone. Planning signals are stable and trusted by manufacturing operations. Most importantly, the organization consistently converts Central Supply Planning requirements into executable manufacturing plans that deliver the intended supply while improving flow, inventory, cycle time, and overall planning effectiveness.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Business, or a related discipline. • 12+ years of experience in supply chain management or semiconductor engineering related field with a Bachelor's degree, 8+ years with a Master's degree, or 6+ years with a PhD. • Demonstrated leadership experience managing complex supply-planning or manufacturing-planning organizations. • Deep understanding of constrained manufacturing environments and the interaction between capacity, materials, product mix, cycle time, inventory, and customer requirements. • Experience developing and executing supply plans across multiple manufacturing stages and locations. • Strong analytical and scenario-planning capabilities with demonstrated ability to make decisions under complex supply constraints. • Proven track record in leading diverse and global teams to achieve measurable outcomes. • Demonstrated ability to lead across organizational boundaries and influence senior stakeholders. Preferred Qualifications • Advanced degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or a related field. • Direct experience with semiconductor Assembly and Test manufacturing and planning. • Experience with semiconductor packaging materials, substrates, and associated material-planning constraints. • Experience with advanced planning systems such as Blue Yonder, SAP IBP, or comparable constraint-based planning platforms. • Experience with multi-stage planning, capacity allocation, scenario planning, and optimization. • Demonstrated experience transforming planning organizations from manual or reactive processes toward integrated, exception-based planning.

title: Analog Circuit Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Role Overview
As an Integrated Voltage Regulator (IVR) Design Engineer, you will be responsible for the architecture, design, and implementation of high-performance power management solutions directly integrated onto advanced processors (CPUs, GPUs, or SoCs). You will work at the intersection of Analog/Mixed-Signal IC design and Power Electronics to improve energy efficiency and performance in next-generation computing systems.

Key Responsibilities
Circuit Architecture and Design: Develop and refine analog topologies such as Operational Amplifiers (Op-Amps), Bandgap References, Data Converters (ADC/DAC), and Phase-Locked Loops (PLLs).
Design and Simulation: Perform transistor-level design using industry-standard tools (like Cadence Virtuoso). Conduct extensive Monte Carlo simulations, corner analysis, and noise analysis to ensure high yield and reliability.
Layout Oversight: Collaborate closely with layout engineers to guide critical placement and routing, focusing on matching, shielding, and minimizing parasitic capacitance/resistance.
Verification: Use SPICE-based simulators to verify circuit functionality against rigorous performance specifications (speed, power, gain, etc.).
Post-Silicon Characterization: Bench-test silicon prototypes in the lab to validate performance against pre-silicon models and debug hardware anomalies

Qualifications:

Required Technical Skills
Transistor Fundamentals: Expert knowledge of MOSFET/BJT device physics, small-signal modeling, and aging effects.
EDA Tool Proficiency: Mastery of Cadence (Spectre/Virtuoso), Mentor Graphics, or Synopsys tool suites.
Signal Integrity: Deep understanding of thermal noise, jitter, crosstalk, and power supply rejection ratio (PSRR).
Mixed-Signal Flow: Familiarity with Verilog-A or Verilog-AMS for behavioral modeling of analog blocks.
Qualifications
Education: BS, MS, or PhD in Electrical Engineering (EE) with a concentration in Analog IC Design.
Experience: 3 - 7 years of experience in analog design (FinFET or planar CMOS nodes).
Analytical Mindset: Strong mathematical background for analyzing feedback systems and stability.

title: Sr AI Runtime Architect - Neuromorphic Computing
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Opportunity:

For nearly a decade, Intel's Neuromorphic Computing Lab, together with a global ecosystem of 250+ research groups, has explored architectures, algorithms, and software inspired by the brain's extraordinary efficiency, scalability, and adaptability. Our Loihi series of research chips pioneered event-driven, sparse, and massively parallel neuro-inspired processing, fueling over 100 peer-reviewed publications that validate the promise of this novel approach.

Now, we're entering an exciting new chapter: transforming these breakthroughs into real-world products that will power the coming era of physical AI systems - beyond the reach of GPUs and mainstream AI accelerators.

If you are passionate about pushing the boundaries of computing, from transistor-level innovation to software abstractions, join us. Help define the next wave of AI technology that harnesses the proven advantages of Intel's neuromorphic computing technology with the versatility demanded by modern AI workloads.

Position Overview:

Join the team building Intel's neuromorphic AI execution stack targeting edge and robotic systems. In this role, you will lead the team and technical direction for our next-generation runtime stack, while remaining hands-on in architecture and implementation. You will set the roadmap from the first product generation onward, on a spatial, event-driven architecture that redraws the boundary between compiler and runtime.

Responsibilities:

- Define and drive the technical vision, architecture, and roadmap for the runtime stack, from firmware to framework integration, while contributing hands-on to critical design and implementation.
- Architect and develop the runtime and performance tooling, and define the execution behavior that the firmware and drivers must implement, whether the device is attached to a host or runs standalone.
- Own the contracts between the runtime stack and the compiler, as well as its integration with industry-standard AI and robotics frameworks.
- Own the measurable performance, real-time behavior, and production quality of the stack across silicon and simulators.
- Collaborate with compiler, hardware, and application teams, as well as customers and partners, to translate workload requirements into runtime capabilities and feed performance insights back into compiler and hardware design.
- Provide technical leadership by establishing engineering practices and mentoring engineers.

About the Organization:

As part of Intel's CTO Office, you will join a vertically integrated incubation effort dedicated to bringing Intel's neuromorphic technology innovations to market. Our diverse team of engineers and researchers has pioneered sparse, event-based, neuromorphic architecture over multiple generations and is now focused on commercializing the technology in future Intel and partner products.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications

- BSc, MSc, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
- 5+ years of experience developing and shipping AI runtime software, such as OpenVINO, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, Ryzen AI, or comparable runtimes, for accelerators, GPUs, or other complex hardware, with working knowledge of the underlying drivers and firmware.
- 5+ years of experience leading the architecture of complex software systems, including defining technical direction and the interfaces to adjacent components.
- 5+ years of experience owning the performance and production quality of accelerator software, including profiling, benchmarking, and debugging across hardware and software boundaries.
- 5+ years of experience providing technical leadership to engineering teams, including mentoring engineers and leading cross-functional delivery.
- 10+ years of hands-on experience developing production-grade systems software in C/C++, with proficiency in Python, using disciplined engineering practices such as code reviews, automated testing, and CI/CD.
- 1+ years of hands-on experience with agentic software engineering, routinely using AI agents to design, implement, test, and review production code.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience managing engineering teams, including hiring and developing engineers.
- Experience with the internals of OpenVINO, oneAPI Level Zero, or comparable accelerator software stacks.
- Experience with spatial, dataflow, or statically scheduled accelerators where the compiler determines placement and scheduling.
- Experience with robotics or real-time systems, including deterministic execution and ecosystems such as ROS 2 or Holoscan.
- Experience developing or integrating functional or performance simulators into accelerator software stacks.
- Familiarity with device driver and firmware development for embedded Linux or RTOS-based systems.
- Experience with HW/SW co-design or performance modeling.

title: GPU Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role

Join Intel's graphics software team and help deliver high-quality GPU experiences in AI domain.

As a GPU Software Engineer, you will develop, validate, debug, and optimize graphics software and GPU driver solutions across Intel platforms. You will work at the intersection of software and hardware, partnering with engineering teams to bring new graphics capabilities to market and solve complex system-level issues.


This is an opportunity to develop hands-on expertise across GPU architecture, graphics drivers, validation, debugging, performance, compute, and AI workloads.

 What You’ll Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Develop and execute end-to-end validation solutions for GPU software, graphics drivers, and applications.
  • Debug and resolve complex software, driver, and system-level issues impacting GPU functionality, quality, and performance.
  • Triage defects, perform root-cause analysis, and collaborate with software and hardware engineering teams to drive issues to resolution.
  • Develop and maintain software, automation, and debugging tools that improve validation efficiency and product quality.
  • Analyze cross-component interactions and identify potential quality, performance, and compatibility issues.
  • Perform validation, triage, and debugging of GPU compute drivers, runtime layers, and AI framework integration failures across software and hardware teams.
  • Integrate latest AI features into end-to-end validation flows and analyze cross-component interactions to develop robust test scenarios.
  • Develop and maintain automation tools, benchmarking suites, and frameworks to improve validation and debug efficiency across AI compute and runtime components.
  • Optimize software performance, memory efficiency, and quality for emerging AI workloads, deep learning inference, and agentic applications.
  • Enable and validate forthcoming AI hardware acceleration capabilities for Intel's GPU platforms.
  • Collaborate on cross-OS software development and validation for GPU-accelerated AI and machine learning workloads.

Behavioral traits that we are looking for:

  • Technical curiosity: Motivated to understand how software, GPU hardware, drivers, operating systems, and applications interact.
  • Problem-solving: Uses structured analysis and data to troubleshoot complex technical issues and identify root causes.
  • Proactive ownership: Identifies potential issues or opportunities early, takes initiative, and follows problems through to resolution.
  • Collaboration: Works effectively across software, hardware, validation, and architecture teams to solve cross-functional problems.
  • Communication: Clearly communicates technical findings, risks, and recommendations to technical stakeholders.
  • Learning agility: Quickly learns new GPU architectures, graphics technologies, tools, APIs, and development environments.
  • Quality mindset: Demonstrates attention to detail and considers product quality, reliability, performance, and the end-user experience when making technical decisions.
  • Adaptability: Effectively manages changing requirements and priorities in a fast-paced engineering environment

Intel invests in our people and offers a complete and competitive package of benefits employees and their families through every stage of life. 

  • See  Intel Benefits for more details. 

Qualifications:

 You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. 

Note:

For information on Intel’s immigration sponsorship guidelines, please see

Intel U.S. Immigration Sponsorship Information


Minimum Qualifications and Experience:


Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field with 3+ years of relevant experience; OR
Master's degree in the field with 1+ years of relevant experience.


Your experience described above must be in the following:

  • Software development using C, C++, or Python.
  • Experience with AI validation workloads such as LLM inference evaluation, and agentic framework integration.
  • Hands-on experience with machine learning frameworks and runtimes such as PyTorch, OpenVINO, ONNX Runtime, or TensorFlow.
  • Experience with industry-standard APIs and frameworks such as DirectX, OpenGL, OpenCL, or Vulkan.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience:

  • Experience with validation, triage, or debugging computer graphics hardware and software.
  • Proven expertise in optimizing GPU compute software for throughput and latency (e.g., operator fusion, KV-cache optimization, low-bit quantization like INT4/INT8/FP8).
  • Familiarity with cross-OS profiling and debug tools such as WinDbg, GPUView, GDB, Intel VTune, emulators, or JTAG-debuggers.
  • Experience with CI/CD practices, automated validation frameworks, and containerized cross-platform testing environments.
  • Strong collaboration skills and passion for staying updated on emerging AI algorithms and hardware acceleration technologies.

Why Join Intel?
Help shape the future of GPU computing by developing and validating graphics technologies that power gaming, content creation, media, and emerging AI experiences. You'll solve challenging problems across hardware and software while working with engineers bringing next-generation Intel graphics capabilities from development to real-world products.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel's APTM organization is seeking a highly driven Staff Technology Development Substrate Yield Lead to drive supplier yield, defect reduction, technical issue closure, and process-control maturity supporting next-generation EMIB-T substrates across Japan suppliers. The team will be chartered to lead yield performance for next-generation advanced packaging technologies, including EMIB-T (Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge with TSV), Intel's most advanced platform for heterogeneous integration partnering with substrate suppliers locally at the HVM factories. This is a high-visibility, high-accountability role with significant responsibility for enabling successful technology development and manufacturing readiness across both Intel Foundry Services (IFS) and Intel Product Groups (IPG).

The ideal candidate is a self-starter who thrives in ambiguous and fast-paced environments, proactively drives issues to closure, and requires minimal supervision. Success in this role requires strong technical depth, urgency in execution, the ability to influence cross-functional teams and suppliers, and a relentless focus on delivering yield and program milestones.


This position requires an Expat assignment in Japan.

Key responsibilities

  • Own day-to-day yield performance and issue closure for assigned supplier lines, modules, products, or process areas.
  • Lead structured investigations from containment and hypothesis development through experiments, failure analysis, corrective action, and sustainment.
  • Use statistical and spatial analytics to identify signatures by line, tool, material, panel position, geometry, product, and time.
  • Establish clear supplier actions, owners, completion criteria, control limits, and verification plans.
  • Support DFM/DFY, qualification, ramp readiness, change control, and deployment of dashboards or automated analytics.
  • Capture reusable learning and communicate facts, hypotheses, decisions, and residual risks clearly.

Behavioral traits

  • Experience working across multiple organizations and influencing stakeholders to achieve results.

title: Staff EMIB-T Substrate Yield Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel's APTM organization is seeking a highly driven Staff Technology Development Substrate Yield Lead to drive supplier yield, defect reduction, technical issue closure, and process-control maturity supporting next-generation EMIB-T substrates across Japan suppliers.  The team will be chartered to lead yield performance for next-generation advanced packaging technologies, including EMIB-T (Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge with TSV), Intel's most advanced platform for heterogeneous integration partnering with substrate suppliers locally at the HVM factories. 


This is a high-visibility, high-accountability role with significant responsibility for enabling successful technology development and manufacturing readiness across both Intel Foundry Services (IFS) and Intel Product Groups (IPG).


The ideal candidate is a self-starter who thrives in ambiguous and fast-paced environments, proactively drives issues to closure, and requires minimal supervision. Success in this role requires strong technical depth, urgency in execution, the ability to influence cross-functional teams and suppliers, and a relentless focus on delivering yield and program milestones. 


This position requires an Expat assignment in Japan.


Key responsibilities

  • Own day-to-day yield performance and issue closure for assigned supplier lines, modules, products, or process areas.
  • Lead structured investigations from containment and hypothesis development through experiments, failure analysis, corrective action, and sustainment.
  • Use statistical and spatial analytics to identify signatures by line, tool, material, panel position, geometry, product, and time.
  • Establish clear supplier actions, owners, completion criteria, control limits, and verification plans.
  • Support DFM/DFY, qualification, ramp readiness, change control, and deployment of dashboards or automated analytics.
  • Capture reusable learning and communicate facts, hypotheses, decisions, and residual risks clearly.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications

  • Masters degree with 6+years or PhD with 4+years in Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Chemistry, Data Science, or a related technical discipline.
  • 5+ years of experience in semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, substrate technology, yield engineering, process engineering, or a closely related field.
  • Hands-on experience in substrate, advanced packaging, or semiconductor yield engineering, including statistical analysis, defect reduction, process optimization, SPC, DFM/DFY, defect metrology, failure analysis, and HVM execution.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to make data-driven decisions in complex environments.
  • Experience working across multiple organizations and influencing stakeholders to achieve results.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage complex technical issues, execute with urgency, and drive actions to closure.
  • Experience developing or deploying yield monitoring systems, automated analytics, dashboards, image analytics, computer vision, AI/ML-based defect detection, or automated defect classification systems.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience working directly with substrate suppliers and external manufacturing partners.
  • Demonstrated program leadership experience, including coordinating cross-functional technical teams and driving execution in high-visibility, high-impact environments.
  • Experience with semi-additive processing, build-up films, microvias, copper plating, lithography, lamination, embedded silicon, TSV, 2.5D/3D packaging, or heterogeneous integration.
  • Prior experience supporting technology development, qualification, and manufacturing ramp of advanced semiconductor technologies.
  • Experience with automated data pipelines, dashboards, image analytics, computer vision, AI/ML defect detection, or automated defect classification.

title: Logistics Operations Manager
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Logistics Operations Manager, you will oversee and drive logistics operations for inbound, interplant, and outbound materials, equipment, and finished goods. You will play a key role in ensuring operational excellence by managing critical logistics processes, optimizing solutions, and driving compliance across Intel's supply chain. Your contributions will directly enhance cost efficiency, delivery reliability, and performance standards, making a lasting impact on Intel's global logistics operations.

Business group
The Logistics Operations Manager role belongs to Intel Foundry's Logistics organization, which focuses on efficiently moving materials, equipment, and finished goods to support manufacturing processes and global customer delivery. This team is dedicated to driving operational excellence through process optimization, supplier collaboration, and innovative solutions, helping Intel deliver world-class products and meet customer expectations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage logistics operations for inbound, interplant, and outbound shipments of materials, equipment, and finished goods.
  • Own dock operations to support site start-up, ramp, and steady-state logistics execution.
  • Monitor and drive performance against logistics KPIs, compliance requirements, and operational standards.
  • Analyze logistics processes and data to identify inefficiencies, defects, and opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Track, escalate, and resolve shipping, warehouse, carrier, and execution exceptions to maintain delivery continuity.
  • Lead critical logistics escalations, minimizing disruptions to operations and ensuring customer satisfaction.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams and external logistics providers to optimize supply chain execution.
  • Leverage analytical tools and digital solutions to enhance cost efficiency, speed, quality, and reliability.
  • Deliver regular updates to senior leaders on logistics performance, risk assessments, and operational readiness.
  • Prepare and support logistics readiness for ongoing capacity growth, customer ramps, and strategic initiatives.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Logistics, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, or a related field.
  • Minimum 4 years of experience in logistics operations or third-party logistics (3PL) management with a Bachelor's degree, or 3 years with a Master's degree.
  • Expertise in warehouse operations, compliance protocols, and supplier governance, with a proven ability to manage execution end-to-end.
  • Strong analytical skills, with experience translating data into actionable decisions and sustained operational improvements.
  • Technical proficiency in monitoring logistics KPIs and driving operational excellence.
  • Experience managing EHS risks within warehouse, logistics, manufacturing, or industrial operations, particularly involving chemical handling, scheduled waste or high-value scrap, hazardous materials,.
  • Working knowledge of warehouse chemical-management requirements, including Safety Data Sheets, chemical compatibility, labeling, segregation, secondary containment, spill response, and emergency preparedness.
  • Demonstrated experience in operational risk assessment, control design, incident investigation, corrective action, and compliance management.
  • Experience developing and governing business processes, SOPs, control plans, and performance-management mechanisms.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Proven ability to thrive in dynamic, fast-paced operational environments.
  • Demonstrated initiative, ownership, and the ability to lead independently through ambiguity.
  • Experience supporting customer ramps, operational transformations, or large-scale logistics readiness initiatives.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence outcomes effectively.
  • Proven experience leading logistics quality programs, risk assessments, operational controls, and corrective/preventive action initiatives to ensure compliance, business continuity, and operational excellence.
  • Strong knowledge of logistics security, safety, regulatory compliance, and risk management frameworks, with the ability to identify vulnerabilities and implement sustainable mitigation plans.
  • Professional training or certification in EHS, chemical safety, scheduled-waste management, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, business process management, or risk management would be an advantage.
  • Experience supporting EHS and chemical-management controls in a semiconductor, electronics, manufacturing, or other high-technology environment.
  • Knowledge of Malaysian requirements relevant to warehouse operations, including the Occupational Safety and Health Act, Environmental Quality Regulations, and scheduled-waste management requirements.
  • Familiarity with structured risk and control methods such as HIRARC, FMEA, Management of Change, control self-assessments, and CAPA.
  • Experience managing third-party warehouse, scrap, recycling, waste-disposal, or chemical-handling service providers.

This is an exceptionally exciting moment to enter the semiconductor manufacturing industry. Global demand for advanced computing - driven by AI, automation, cloud infrastructure, and digital transformation - is fueling the largest period of growth and reinvestment the sector has seen in decades. Semiconductors are now recognized as critical to economic resilience, national security, and technological leadership, leading to unprecedented expansion in manufacturing capacity and innovation. For professionals in the field, this translates to rare opportunities to shape breakthrough technologies, contribute to globally significant projects, and be part of arguably the most rapidly evolving and impactful industry ever.

Intel's Global Construction Engineering (GCE) organization is responsible for the design and engineering of Intel's major manufacturing and cleanroom facilities worldwide. Our organization consists of highly specialized, in-house architects and engineers working in a deeply collaborative environment. Together with our factory, operations, and supply chain partners, we deliver some of the most technically complex construction programs in the industry - projects that demand precision, speed, and disciplined cost management.

Our vision is to be the world leader in semiconductor foundry construction engineering, and we are expanding our team to support the acceleration of Intel Foundry's manufacturing roadmap. We are seeking exceptional technical talent to join our organization who will thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy working with leading-edge technology, and be motivated by opportunities to innovate and make meaningful business impact.

This is a hybrid Contract position in Penang, Malaysia.

As a Construction Project Design Manager - Global Construction Engineering, your responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
• Develop discipline scope and engineering solutions for construction projects.
• Interface and coordinate with contract design, construction, scheduling, and estimating resources.
• Interface with facilities staff and project managers, factory partners, particularly the Industrial Engineering team, to determine the optimal facility design scope and engineering solutions that support evolving factory requirements and business needs
• Define design criteria, lead scope definition and justification, develop design concepts, and oversee completion of positioning, programming, and detailed design.
• Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary design activities to ensure alignment with project objectives, schedule, budget, and constructability requirements.
• Work with estimators to ensure costs are captured and project budgets are met.
• Have strong knowledge of Intel's master specifications and standards, while utilizing established change processes to improve standards and drive innovative solutions.
• Collaborate and share learnings with counterparts at other sites across the globe.
• Build and drive a safety culture of caring in every business environment, from offices to construction sites, and from front-end planning through construction execution.
• Candidates with experience as a Design Manager on semiconductor manufacturing or advanced technology facility construction projects are highly encouraged to apply. Such experience may include leading architect-engineer (A/E) firms, managing design execution, coordinating multidisciplinary engineering teams, and driving design quality, cost, and schedule performance through project delivery.

The successful candidate should exhibit the following behavioural traits:
• Strong written, visual, and verbal communication skills for technical and business topics.
• Ability to communicate strategic and tactical concepts across a wide range of employees and management levels.
• Ability to influence and drive alignment in a highly matrixed, cross-functional environment.
• Strong collaboration skills across engineering disciplines, organizations, external architect-engineer (A/E) partners, and global teams.
• Strong orientation toward teamwork, customer service, and quality.
• Excellent organizational, planning, and workload management skills, with the ability to lead multiple projects of varying complexity.
• Strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities, including the ability to resolve complex technical and project delivery challenges.
• Proficiency in reading, interpreting, and coordinating construction contract documents and engineering deliverables.
• Working knowledge of office productivity and computer applications.
• Commitment to continuous improvement, innovation, and the adoption of new technologies and best practices.
• High attention to detail, accountability, and ownership in delivering commitments.
• Commitment to championing and sustaining a strong safety culture throughout the project lifecycle.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Minimum Qualifications: • Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related technical field. • 5+ years of relevant industry experience in facilities engineering, project engineering, design engineering, or design management roles supporting semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, or similar industrial facility projects. Preferred Qualifications: • Master's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related technical field and 4+ years of relevant industry experience. • Experience as a Design Manager, Engineering Manager, or Lead Discipline Engineer supporting semiconductor facility design and construction projects. • Demonstrated experience managing external architect-engineer (A/E) firms and coordinating multidisciplinary design deliverables from concept through construction. • Familiarity with AutoCAD, P/IDs PipeFlo (for Mechanical and Chemical Engineering candidates), ETAP/SKM and power system studies (for Electrical Engineering candidates), and BIM. • For Mechanical and Chemical Engineering candidates, experience with utility and process systems commonly used in semiconductor or advanced manufacturing facilities, including HVAC, chilled water, process cooling water, exhaust, vacuum, compressed dry air, specialty gas, chemical distribution, wastewater treatment, and related safety systems. • Working knowledge of process hazard analysis (PHA), HAZOP reviews, pressure relief and piping system design principles, equipment specification and selection, and engineering codes and standards applicable to industrial facilities. • Basic knowledge of control methods for process systems and/or electrical power distribution systems. • Registration as a Professional Engineer • Experience with: - Construction, start-up, and commissioning/turnover of facility systems - Building and fire codes, hazardous occupancies, and related codes and standards to the field of expertise - Semiconductor manufacturing facilities, cleanrooms, and related infrastructure systems.

title: Reliability Lab Shock and Vibration Testing Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Stress Test and Reliability Laboratory organization is looking for a dynamic, hands-on engineer to join their environmental stress tool engineering team in Chandler, AZ. The lab engineering team develops and maintains a fleet of equipment which is used to evaluate Intel's silicon, package, and assembly technologies under simulated field use including heat, humidity, temperature change, and dynamic stresses such as shock and vibration.

This role will focus on supporting our dynamics stress capability. In this role, you will be responsible for developing, executing, and analyzing mechanical reliability and environmental stress testing programs for semiconductor devices, boards, and assemblies. The role requires expertise in shock, vibration, and dynamic mechanical loading methodologies with a strong emphasis on industry-standard test requirements and a deep knowledge of the physics of failure.


Responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

  • Develop, plan, and execute dynamic stress tests, including shock, vibration, and other test methods in compliance with JEDEC, IPC, and/or customer requirements
  • Develop test fixtures, instrumentation strategies, and data acquisition systems to support mechanical reliability evaluations.
  • Working with the operations team, perform testing on devices
  • Analyze test data using statistical and engineering methods to identify failure modes, performance limits, and reliability risks.
  • Correlate test data to mechanical models to validate and improve simulation results
  • Generate detailed test plans, procedures, reports, and qualification documentation.
  • Drive continuous improvement of laboratory capabilities, test automation, and best practices for dynamic stress testing.
  • Ensure laboratory operations comply with applicable safety, quality, and calibration requirements.
  • Provide technical guidance regarding shock and vibration requirements throughout the product development lifecycle.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.  Requirements listed would be obtained through a combination of industry relevant job experience, internship experiences and or schoolwork/classes/research. 


Minimum Requirements

Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Engineering, or similar STEM related degree:

  • BS with 4+ years of experience in shock and vibration stress testing/methods
  • -OR- MS with 1+ years of experience in shock and vibration stress testing/methods
  • - OR- PhD with 6 months+ of experience in shock and vibration stress testing/methods

Experience can come from a combination of educational and work experience and may include:

  • Hands-on experience conducting shock and vibration testing using electrodynamic shakers and mechanical shock equipment.
  • Working knowledge of JEDEC and/or IPC standards related to board-level reliability and mechanical stress testing.
  • Experience developing test plans, procedures, and qualification reports.
  • Proficiency with data acquisition systems, accelerometers, strain gauges, and vibration control software.
  • Experience analyzing vibration and shock response data and interpreting failure mechanisms.
  • Understanding of finite element analysis (FEA) results and correlation to physical testing.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep expertise with JEDEC standards such as JESD22-B103, JESD22-B110, JESD22-B111, and other relevant mechanical reliability requirements.
  • Experience interpreting and applying IPC standards including IPC-9703 and related solder joint reliability specifications.
  • Familiarity with military, aerospace, or transportation standards such as MIL-STD-810, ASTM, and IEC environmental test methods
  • Advanced knowledge of vibration analysis, modal analysis, frequency response functions (FRFs), and resonance characterization.
  • Proficiency with FEA tools such as Comsol Multiphysics, ANSYS, Abaqus, or Nastran.
  • Experience with standard and high-speed data acquisition systems (including DMM) and automated test scripting using Python, MATLAB, or LabVIEW.
  • Laboratory leadership experience, including test equipment specification, procurement, calibration management, and mentoring junior engineers.
  • Proficiency in electrical measurements, calibration, and troubleshooting programmable DC power supplies, multimeters, and other instrumentation.
  • Experience with data acquisition systems, instrumentation communication protocols (e.g., Ethernet, RS-232, GPIB), and automated test equipment.
  • Knowledge of design of experiments, statistical process control, and measurement system analysis.
  • Strong troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in cross-functional engineering environments.

Your expertise and enthusiasm for engineering excellence can help shape the future of semiconductor innovation. Join our team and contribute to groundbreaking technological advancements by applying today.

Job Description:

This position is in the Logic Technology Development (LTD) team, working in one of the most advanced semiconductor development facilities in the world.

The LTD Resolution Enhancement Technology (RET) team is extending the limits of feature sizes that are patternable on Intel's devices, using current and future lithography manufacturing tooling. The team works closely with fab integrated lithography process and mask manufacturing teams using computational lithography tooling to optimize mask patterns and maximize manufacturing process capability. The RET team also works closely with the design rule definition teams, using lithography and patterning simulation capabilities to determine design rules for future Intel process nodes.

We foster a collaborative, supportive, and exciting environment where the brightest minds in the world come together to achieve exceptional results. We give you opportunities to transform technology and create a better future, by delivering products that make the world a better place.

  • Development, and implementation of Resolution Enhancement Techniques (RET) for existing and novel process technologies
  • Define and selects new approaches and implementation of RET
  • OPC recipe code optimization and validation
  • Algorithmic design pattern layout manipulation
  • Use predictive modeling, statistics, machine learning, and other data analysis techniques to collect, explore, visualize fab process data, and develop RET software algorithms and applications to compensate for physical effects in photolithography imaging and the etch pattern transfer process

title: Senior Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact 

You will be part of a highly skilled, agile design/verification team developing cutting-edge hardware for the NIC, IPU and AI domains. 

As a senior IP Design Verification Engineer, you will play a crucial role in ensuring the functionality and reliability of complex designs. You will technically lead teams in developing verification plans, creating test benches, and building environments to thoroughly validate meaningful parts of the chip — complex IPs and subsystems. 

Your work will directly contribute to identifying and resolving bugs in the pre-silicon environment using simulation and/or Formal Property Verification techniques, ensuring robust designs that meet high-performance standards. 

We are intentional, fast adopters of AI as a working tool. We bring modern AI assistants and automation into every part of the verification flow — planning, stimulus and checker development, coverage analysis, debug and more. 

 
 
Business group  
You will be joining Intel's Central Engineering Group (CEG), a global organization responsible for designing and verifying industry-leading IPs and architectures that power Intel's NIC, IPU and ASIC products. The group produces innovative technologies and solutions for hyperscalers, cloud providers, networking, AI and other specialized workloads. 

As part of this dynamic team, you will contribute to Intel's commitment to advancing silicon and system innovation.  
 
Key Responsibilities 

  • Own verification planning and execution for key IP features across IP and subsystem integration points 
  • Build scalable verification environments and targeted test plans with reusable test benches, checkers, VIPs, and behavioral models 
  • Collaborate closely with architecture, design, and software teams from specification through bringup; contribute across role boundaries when needed to unblock progress and maintain execution quality 
  • Drive ownership of multiple critical blocks and verification components; take full responsibility for functional signoffs and achievement of performance and power metrics 
  • Lead IP delivery to multiple customers while ensuring technical excellence; balance competing requirements, schedules, and resources across teams 
  • Drive convergence of simulation and formal verification into unified bug hunting and coverage closure strategies; evaluate and adopt emerging methodologies including ML-driven verification flows 
  • Mentor and develop verification engineers; establish verification best practices and raise team-level execution quality 
  • Comfortable using AI-assisted development tools as part of everyday workflow; track record of delivering reusable, configurable verification collateral 

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications  

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.  
  • 10+ years of experience in functional design verification of ASIC, SOC or FPGA designs with expertise in System Verilog, OVM/UVM, and debugging tools.  
  • Proficiency in creating IP test environments and/or using formal verification methods
