title: CPU Power Management and Performance Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is shaping the future of technology to help create a better future for the entire world. Our work in pushing forward fields like AI, analytics, and cloud-to-edge technology is at the heart of countless innovations. With a career at Intel, you'll have the opportunity to use technology to power major breakthroughs and create enhancements that improve our everyday quality of life. Join us and help make the future more wonderful for everyone. Want to learn more? Visit our YouTube Channel or the link below.


Life at Intel

We are seeking an experienced SoC CPU power-management professional to define and drive the power-management architecture for next-generation mobile and desktop client processors. In this role, you will own end-to-end CPU power and performance requirements within the broader SoC, define differentiated architectural features and control mechanisms, and guide their implementation from early product definition through post-silicon validation. You will work closely with CPU microarchitecture, SoC integration, silicon design, firmware, operating system, validation, thermal, and product teams to deliver industry-leading performance, energy efficiency, and user experiences.


Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Own the power-management and performance architecture for mobile and desktop CPUs as part of the CPU architecture team. Define architectural capabilities, develop innovative techniques, guide implementation, and drive energy efficiency across operating conditions and product segments.
  • Define and analyze CPU power and performance requirements, budgets, and interfaces within the SoC, working across CPU cores, shared caches, interconnects, memory, accelerators, and platform IP.
  • Create and maintain workload-based CPU and SoC power and performance models and targets; correlate predictions with pre- and post-silicon data; and apply the results to improve current implementations and future architectures across idle, sustained, burst, and peak workloads.
  • Partner with firmware and operating system teams to define end-to-end CPU and platform power-management capabilities, including DVFS policies, clock and power gating, idle-state management, telemetry, residency, latency, and quality-of-service tradeoffs.
  • Influence CPU microarchitecture and SoC fabric, memory, and I/O architecture to optimize power efficiency, performance, throughput, latency, and quality of service under representative real-world workloads.
  • Lead cross-functional architecture and design reviews, drive tradeoff decisions across power, performance, area, cost, thermals, and product experience, and align CPU, SoC integration, validation, firmware, operating system, and product teams.
  • Translate product usage models and competitive insights into clear architectural requirements, feature specifications, and measurable success criteria; track execution and communicate risks, decisions, and progress to technical and product leadership.
  • The architect role may involve technical and managerial leadership of a team or group.

A successful candidate will also demonstrate:

  • System-level thinking and the ability to connect detailed design decisions to CPU, SoC, and product-level outcomes.
  • Strong analytical problem-solving skills, with an emphasis on innovation, feasibility assessment, and disciplined exploration of architectural tradeoffs.
  • Technical leadership and communication skills to influence CPU architecture, SoC design, firmware, validation, and product roadmaps across organizational boundaries.
  • Curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to expand deep technical expertise into broader architecture ownership while advancing energy-efficient computing.

Qualifications:

The minimum qualifications below are required for consideration. Preferred qualifications are additional attributes that may help candidates succeed in the role. Relevant experience may be gained through architecture, design, modeling, validation, firmware, or other closely related engineering roles.


What We Need to See (Minimum Qualifications):

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with 6+ years of relevant experience; master’s degree with 4+ years; or PhD with 2+ years. The specialized experience described below may be included within this overall experience.
  • Within that experience, 4+ years in SoC or IP architecture, CPU or SoC design, microarchitecture, power and performance engineering, or a closely related technical field.

How to Stand Out (Preferred Qualifications):

  • Extensive experience in CPU or SoC design, microarchitecture, architecture, or power and performance engineering; candidates with deep design expertise and demonstrated system-level leadership who are ready to grow into an architecture role are encouraged to apply. 
  • Proven experience designing, integrating, or architecting compute SoCs, CPUs, or complex silicon IP, with an understanding of how local design decisions affect system-level power, performance, and product behavior.
  • Knowledge of CPU or SoC power-management concepts such as DVFS, clock and power gating, idle states, telemetry, thermal constraints, or firmware and operating system interactions; direct ownership in all areas is not required.
  • Advanced knowledge of computer architecture, CPU microarchitecture, system-level design, and the interactions among cores, caches, interconnects, memory, accelerators, and platform IP.
  • Experience with performance or power modeling, benchmarking, workload analysis, functional modeling, statistical analysis, or correlation of model predictions with silicon measurements.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical tradeoffs, communicate across design, architecture, firmware, validation, and product teams, and expand from detailed design ownership to broader architectural decision-making.

Bring your technical depth, system-level perspective, and passion for energy-efficient computing to Intel. Join us in developing CPU power-management innovations that shape the performance, efficiency, and user experience of future client products.


Benefits at Intel

Our total rewards package goes above and beyond just a paycheck. Whether you're looking to build your career, improve your health, or protect your wealth, we offer generous benefits to help you achieve your goals. Go to Intel Benefits | Intel Careers for details of benefits available to you. Intel reserves the right to modify, change or discontinue benefit plans at any time in its sole discretion.

title: Chassis IP Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As an IP Logic Design Engineer, you will be instrumental in developing and optimizing logic designs for high-performance IP blocks that drive Intel's cutting-edge SoC solutions. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include writing register transfer level (RTL) code, conducting simulations, and ensuring designs meet stringent power, performance, area, and timing goals. You'll play a pivotal role in delivering quality IPs while collaborating across architecture, verification, and SoC integration teams to ensure seamless handoffs and impactful results.

Business group
The Central Engineering Group (CEG) is Intel's leading innovation hub, focused on designing foundational technologies for integration across Intel's product portfolio. Within this team, the UIC Fabric Design organization specializes in developing reusable IP blocks and subsystems that enhance system-level capabilities. This group contributes to Intel's broader mission of delivering world-class solutions to revolutionize computing across industries.

Key Responsibilities
- Design and develop RTL code for IP blocks, ensuring functionality, quality, and scalability.
- Optimize logic designs to meet power, performance, area, and timing objectives.
- Collaborate with architecture teams to define microarchitecture features of IP designs.
- Participate in verification plan reviews and implement corrective measures for failing RTL tests.
- Support SoC integration teams to ensure high-quality integration and verification of IP blocks.
- Work with physical design teams to address timing and implementation challenges.
- Drive compliance with quality assurance standards for seamless IP-SoC handoff.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with 4+ years of experience in state-of-the-art SoC or IP design OR Master's degree with 3+ years of experience.
- Proficiency in Verilog/System Verilog, including Lint/CDC/RDC tools and methodologies.
- Demonstrated ability to optimize designs for power, performance, and area trade-offs (PPA).

Preferred Qualifications
- Familiarity with AMBA (CHI, AXI, AHB, APB) and PCIe/CXL protocols.
- Experience in designing IP subsystems, including protocol conversion bridges and debug/trace components.
- Understanding of concepts such as QoS, access control, flow control, RAS, and security/error handling.
- Proven ability to collaborate across architecture, verification, and SoC integration teams effectively.
- Familiarity with using AI tools to assist logic design.
- Strong communication skills and experience working with globally distributed teams across time zones.

We invite you to join our team, where you'll be empowered to innovate, collaborate, and leave a lasting impact on the future of computing.

title: Compiler Engineering Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Us in Shaping the Future


At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software.


As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.


The Team


The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.


Position Overview


We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack.


You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on a scoped project that may involve compiler features, MLIR-based intermediate representations, Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), optimization, code generation, runtime or offload support, debug information, testing infrastructure, performance analysis, or developer tools.


Projects may involve connecting software capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for an undergraduate student who wants to build practical compiler-engineering experience and apply foundational computer science concepts to production software.


Responsibilities


• Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies.
• Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase.
• Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions.
• Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project.
• Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members.
• Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team.
• Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications


• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or a Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Informatics, or a related technical discipline (able to maintain student status for at least 1 year).
• Coursework or project experience in data structures, algorithms, computer architecture, operating systems, programming languages, or compiler construction.
• Experience programming in C or C++ through coursework, research, personal projects, or prior internships.
• Experience using software development and debugging tools in a Linux or similar development environment.


Preferred Qualifications


• Compiler-related coursework or project experience, including parsing, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, or runtimes.
• Familiarity with LLVM, MLIR, Clang, Flang, SYCL/DPC++, Triton, OpenMP, CUDA, or another compiler or parallel-programming ecosystem.
• Knowledge of CPU or GPU architecture, heterogeneous computing, or systems programming.
• Familiarity with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi.
• Tile-base programming model knowledge
• GPU Compute kernel writing experience
• Experience with Git, automated testing, continuous integration, performance analysis, or open-source development.
• Technical contributions such as code, patches, reviews, research, publications, or substantial academic projects.


Success in This Role


• Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.
• Clear written and verbal communication.
• Ability to work independently on scoped tasks while seeking guidance when needed.
• Collaborative mindset and commitment to high-quality engineering.


Bring your passion, curiosity, and your engineering drive to Intel, and help shape how the next generation of AI workloads runs on Intel hardware.

title: E-core Senior CPU Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We created the Intel Atom Processor (E-Core), a disruptive technology that enables a broad range of devices including entry PC's, smartphones, modems, 2 in 1 laptops, micro-servers, and other Internet-of-Things IoT devices. You will be part of a team, participating in the design of a future generation high performance Intel Atom microprocessor.


This role requires an engineer with strong analytic and problem solving skill, an ability to communicate well, and willing to share and discuss issues. You will work on implementation of CPU Core blocks from synthesis through post-layout verification and tapeout. You will develop the custom constraints for driving synthesis and Auto-Place and Route APR tools to implement and optimize the design to meet aggressive timing and power goals. You will work closely with micro-architecture, RTL, and custom circuit teams to converge the design to project targets.

The responsibilities will be tailored to the candidate's skills and expertise and will include several of the following, but not be limited to:

  • Logic synthesis and place and route for CORE IP blocks.
  • Performing floor-planning and routing studies and implementation
    Block/sub-system level timing analysis.
  • Work on low power techniques and power reduction in sub-system.
  • Physical verification closure of block/sub-system.
  • Scripts writing for data analysis and recipe creation.
  • Strong analytical ability, problem solving and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and at various levels of abstraction.
  • Strong communication and team work skills.
  • Capable of working in a high performing team to deliver the results required from the organization.
  • Ability to work well in at team and be productive under aggressive schedules.
  • Ability to contribute as technical leader to resolve problems and provide mentorship.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications:
Must have either BS or MS in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering.

Minimum 10 year of experience in:

  • CPU physical design and timing verification.
  • Synthesis/APR flows on multi voltage high frequency designs including custom polygon editing.
  • Tcl scripting.
  • Noise, cross-talk, OCV analysis.
  • Floorplanning and physical design and timing closure.
  • Formal equivalence, DRC/LVS, IR and electro-migration checks.

Preferred qualifications:

  • 12+ years of experience with the above skill sets.
  • Experience with Fusion Compiler, DCT, DCE, ICC2, RedHawk, ICV, Conformal, Calibre, PrimeTime, StarRCXT.
  • Cadence Tools Experience Not a Must But Preferred.

title: Graduate Talent (E-core CPU Physical Design)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We created the Intel Atom Processor (E-Core), a disruptive technology that enables a broad range of devices including entry PC's, smartphones, modems, 2 in 1 laptops, micro-servers, and other Internet-of-Things IoT devices. You will be part of a team, participating in the design of a future generation high performance Intel Atom microprocessor. This role requires a engineer with strong analytic and problem solving skill, an ability to communicate well, and willing to share and discuss issues. You will work on implementation of CPU Core blocks from synthesis through post-layout verification and tapeout. You will develop the custom constraints for driving synthesis and Auto-Place and Route APR tools to implement and optimize the design to meet aggressive timing and power goals. You will work closely with micro-architecture, RTL, and custom circuit teams to converge the design to project targets.

  • Logic synthesis and place and route for CORE IP blocks.

  • Work on low power techniques and power reduction in sub-system.

title: Compiler Engineering Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software.

As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.

About the Team

The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs.

The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models.

You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.

Position Overview

We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on a scoped project that may involve:

  • Compiler features or MLIR-based intermediate representations
  • Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs)
  • Optimization, code generation, runtime, or offload support
  • Debug information or testing infrastructure
  • Performance analysis or developer tools

Projects may involve connecting software capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning models such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Kimi.

You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for an undergraduate student who wants to build practical compiler-engineering experience and apply foundational computer science concepts to production software.

Key Responsibilities

  • Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies
  • Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase
  • Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions
  • Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project
  • Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members
  • Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team
  • Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work

To Be Successful in This Role

You should demonstrate the following professional traits:

  • Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills
  • Clear written and verbal communication

Qualifications:

This position is not eligible for intel immigration sponsorship.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Informatics, or a related technical discipline
  • 3+ months of coursework or project experience in data structures, algorithms, computer architecture, operating systems, programming languages, or compiler construction
  • Experience programming in C++ through coursework, research, personal projects, or prior internships
  • Experience using software development and debugging tools in a Linux or similar development environment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Compiler-related coursework or project experience, including parsing, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, or runtimes
  • Hands-on compiler development experience with LLVM, MLIR, Triton, GCC, Clang, or similar compiler frameworks
  • Experience with GPU programming models such as CUDA, SYCL, OpenMP, or HIP
  • Knowledge of CPU or GPU architecture, heterogeneous computing, or systems programming
  • Familiarity with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi
  • Tile-based programming model knowledge
  • GPU compute kernel writing experience
  • Experience with Git, automated testing, continuous integration, performance analysis, or open-source development
  • Technical contributions such as code, patches, reviews, research, publications, or substantial academic projects

title: Compiler Engineering Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Us in Shaping the Future
At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.
The Team
The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.
Position Overview
We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on an engineering or research project that may involve compiler features, MLIR-based intermediate representations, Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), optimization, code generation, runtime or offload support, debug information, testing infrastructure, performance analysis, or developer tools. Projects may connect hardware capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for a graduate student who can apply deeper technical expertise to an ambiguous engineering or research problem, evaluate alternatives, and deliver a well-supported solution or prototype.
Responsibilities
• Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies.
• Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase.
• Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions.
• Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project.
• Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members.
• Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team.
• Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
• Currently pursuing a Bachelor or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical discipline.
• Graduate-level coursework, research, or project experience in compilers, programming languages, computer architecture, parallel computing, systems software, or a closely related area.
• Experience programming in C or C++ and working with complex software systems.
• Experience designing experiments, analyzing technical results, and communicating conclusions.
Preferred Qualifications
• Hands-on experience with LLVM or related compiler infrastructure, including front-end development, intermediate representations, optimization passes, code generation, runtimes, or debug information.
• Research or development experience involving CPU/GPU architectures, heterogeneous computing, AI/ML compilation, HPC, parallel programming, or performance optimization.
• Familiarity with LLVM, MLIR, Clang, Flang, SYCL/DPC++, Triton, OpenMP, CUDA, or another compiler or parallel-programming ecosystem.
• Experience with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi.
• Tile-base programming model knowledge
• GPU Compute kernel writing experience
• Experience contributing to open-source software or working in a large collaborative codebase.
• Publications, technical reports, patents, open-source contributions, or other evidence of advanced technical work.
Success in This Role
• Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.
• Clear written and verbal communication.
• Ability to work independently on scoped tasks while seeking guidance when needed.
• Collaborative mindset and commitment to high-quality engineering.

title: AI Frameworks Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact


Intel is building the open software stack that makes large language models run fast on Intel GPUs. You will join the engineering team that develops and optimizes LLM inference frameworks - working directly in vLLM and in the SW stack beneath it and in the upstream. You will write and tune compute kernels, reshape execution paths, hunt performance bottlenecks and submit your changes into widely used open-source projects. If you want to optimize how fast AI workloads run, this is that role.

Business group


The Data Center Group (DCG) is at the forefront of delivering cutting-edge technologies to power the world's data centers, enabling advanced computing solutions that drive innovation across industries. Within this group, our team is dedicated to developing AI frameworks and workloads that empower researchers and developers to create high-performance, scalable solutions for complex AI challenges. We aim to build tools and technologies that accelerate progress in AI, aligning with Intel's mission to advance global technology.

Key Responsibilities


- Design, develop, and optimize AI framework software for LLM inference on Intel GPUs, contributing upstream to external open-source frameworks such as vLLM and PyTorch.
- Develop and optimize compute kernels for transformer inference.
- Implement and tune distributed execution paths - tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism, collective communication, and asynchronous data movement within deep learning frameworks.
- Transform and optimize the computational-graph representation of neural network models, and develop machine learning primitives in mathematical and kernel libraries.
- Profile inference workloads to identify performance bottlenecks across the stack, quantify them, and propose and drive solutions together with the individual component teams that own each layer.
- Optimize code for a range of computing hardware backends, adapting implementations to the memory hierarchy, instruction set, and execution model of each target.
- Build and extend unit tests, correctness checks, and performance regression coverage so that framework and kernel work stays reliable as upstream moves.
- Collaborate with framework, compiler, and machine learning engineers across global teams, and engage with the open-source community through code review and technical discussion.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications


- Bachelor's degree in AI, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or a related field.
- 4+ years of relevant experience with a Bachelor's degree, or 3+ years with a Master's degree.
- Advanced expertise in Python programming.
- Hands-on experience with AI inference and large language models (LLMs).
- Demonstrated proficiency in PyTorch.
- Solid foundation in AI frameworks, machine learning algorithms, and software engineering practices.
- Strong problem-solving skills with experience in debugging and designing optimized software and algorithms.
- Proficiency in Linux environments from a user perspective.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in performance profiling and optimization for AI workloads, including reading and interpreting hardware-level profiles.
- Familiarity with parallel and distributed computing concepts and collective communication libraries.
- Familiarity with vLLM or another LLM inference serving framework.
- Track record of accepted contributions to a major open-source AI project.
- Understanding of numerical precision and quantization formats (FP8, INT8, INT4) and their accuracy implications.
- Knowledge of writing/optimizing GPU compute kernels is a plus.
- Creativity and innovative thinking in solving technical and system-level challenges.
- Strong communication skills and ability to work across global teams.

title: AI Frameworks Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact


Intel is building the open software stack that makes large language models run fast on Intel GPUs. You will join the engineering team that develops and optimizes LLM inference frameworks - working directly in vLLM and in the GPU kernel libraries beneath it, upstream and in the open.


This is a deeply technical, inward-facing engineering role: your work is the framework itself. You will write and tune compute kernels, reshape execution paths, hunt performance bottlenecks down to the hardware, and land your changes in widely used open-source projects. If you want your code to decide how fast an entire class of AI workloads runs, this is that role.

Business group


The Data Center Group (DCG) is at the forefront of delivering cutting-edge technologies to power the world's data centers, enabling advanced computing solutions that drive innovation across industries. Within this group, our team is dedicated to developing AI frameworks and workloads that empower researchers and developers to create high-performance, scalable solutions for complex AI challenges. We aim to build tools and technologies that accelerate progress in AI, aligning with Intel's mission to advance global technology.

Key Responsibilities


- Design, develop, and optimize AI framework software for LLM inference on Intel GPUs, contributing upstream to external open-source frameworks such as vLLM and PyTorch.
- Develop and optimize compute kernels (e.g., Triton, SYCL) for attention, mixture-of-experts, quantization, normalization, and other core building blocks of transformer inference.
- Implement and tune distributed execution paths - tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism, collective communication, and asynchronous data movement within deep learning frameworks.
- Transform and optimize the computational-graph representation of neural network models, and develop machine learning primitives in mathematical and kernel libraries.
- Profile inference workloads to identify performance bottlenecks across the stack, quantify them, and propose and drive solutions together with the individual component teams that own each layer.
- Optimize code for a range of computing hardware backends, adapting implementations to the memory hierarchy, instruction set, and execution model of each target.
- Build and extend unit tests, correctness checks, and performance regression coverage so that framework and kernel work stays reliable as upstream moves.
- Collaborate with framework, compiler, and machine learning engineers across global teams, and engage with the open-source community through code review and technical discussion.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications


- Bachelor's degree in AI, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or a related field.
- At least 2-3 years of relevant experience with a Bachelor's degree, or 1+ year with a Master's degree.
- Advanced expertise in Python programming.
- Demonstrated proficiency in PyTorch, including its internals or extension mechanisms.
- Hands-on experience with AI inference and large language models (LLMs).
- Strong problem-solving skills with experience in debugging and designing optimized software and algorithms.
- Proficiency in Linux environments from a user perspective.
- Solid foundation in AI frameworks, machine learning algorithms, and software engineering practices.

Preferred Qualification


- Experience writing or optimizing GPU compute kernels (Triton, CUDA, SYCL, OpenCL, or similar).
- Experience in performance profiling and optimization for AI workloads, including reading and interpreting hardware-level profiles.
- Familiarity with parallel and distributed computing concepts and collective communication libraries.
- Familiarity with vLLM or another LLM inference serving framework.
- Track record of accepted contributions to a major open-source AI project.
- Understanding of numerical precision and quantization formats (FP8, INT8, INT4) and their accuracy implications.
- Creativity and innovative thinking in solving technical and system-level challenges.
- Strong communication skills and ability to work across global teams.

Bring your passion for AI, innovative thinking, and technical expertise to Intel, where you will contribute to groundbreaking advancements that impact the world for years to come.

title: Power Delivery Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Are you passionate about computing and AI accelerators?

Do you thrive on innovation and want to disrupt the industry? Are you eager to work with leading AI hardware engineers on Intel's latest architecture? If you love collaborating with diverse teams to create best-in-class AI compute platforms, Intel's GPE department has exciting opportunities for you.

As a member of the GPE team, you will develop hardware and platform solutions for Intel products, including the newest IPs targeted at next-generation GPUs and AI accelerators.


You will have the opportunity to engage in enabling technologies in PCB design, manufacturing, testing, and debugging. We are a winning team with a clear vision of delivering competitive and cutting-edge products, and we are committed to building the best products and developing the best skills for our team.


Key Responsibilities:


  • Work on end-to-end power delivery design and development, from initial concept to implementation of power delivery requirements and ecosystem enabling power integrated circuits.
  • Own power integrity simulation for the platform power delivery network: build and correlate VRM-to-die PDN models, run DC IR-drop and AC target-impedance analysis, and perform transient droop and Ldi/dt studies across die, package, and PCB to set the decoupling and stack up strategy before layout is committed.
  • Apply knowledge of power conversion topologies, including components, compensation circuits/stability analysis, drop/droop analysis, simulation tools, and techniques, as well as PCB layout and design tools, to characterize performance and validate correlation of simulation modeling and results.
  • Design and validate platform power conversion and management solutions, including energy management, and perform simulation and optimization for package and PCB, including stack up, power/ground noise plane assignment, decoupling solutions, and/or power sequencing requirements.
  • Design for debug: architect observability into the board from the start, including per-rail voltage and current sense points, Kelvin-sense and probe landing points, telemetry and current-monitor access (SVID/PMBus/IMON), rail-level isolation and enable control, and voltage-margining , so power-on and post-silicon issues can be isolated on the first board instead of a respin.
  • Design for flexibility: build configurability into the power delivery solution so a single board can support multiple SKUs and derivatives, using stuffing options for phase count and decoupling, pin-compatible dual-source regulator footprints, rail split/merge and current headroom for higher-power SKUs, and programmable load line, compensation, and VID range.
  • Create and execute test plans to validate and characterize power delivery solutions.
  • Correlate bench and VR test tool measurements with simulation results to improve simulation model accuracy and close the loop on power integrity assumptions.
  • Conduct failure analysis and root cause investigations for power delivery issues, implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
  • Collaborate with silicon and platform architects to generate solutions and analyses, delivering content into platform design guides as solution collaterals for end customers.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including board design, SW/FW, and systems validation, to ensure seamless integration of power delivery solutions.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications, you must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position.

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in:
    • Designing low voltage, high current, multi-phase DC-DC switching regulators (buck, boost, etc.) to meet stringent targets, optimizing the design for transient response and conversion efficiency.
    • Working with signal/power integrity and power delivery network simulation tools such as Cadence Sigrity PowerDC/PowerSI, Ansys SIwave etc. to develop accurate models of circuit design 
    • Design and optimize accurate power delivery simulation models using SPICE and time-based simulation tools (LTSpice, SIMPLIS etc.) based on SOC design power requirements.
    • Power delivery network modeling across die, package, and PCB, including stackup, plane assignment, decoupling network design, and S-parameter extraction and correlation.
    • Experience using oscilloscopes and DAQ for hardware troubleshooting and debugging.
    • Interacting with Signal Integrity, Layout, and Mechanical engineers, with working knowledge of SI/PI, PCB layout, and mechanical aspects of board designs.

Preferred Qualifications, are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

  • Experience designing for debug and testability on power delivery hardware, including sense and telemetry instrumentation, voltage margining, and rail isolation for post-silicon bring-up.
  • Experience designing configurable power delivery solutions that support multiple SKUs and derivative products from a single board design.
  • Identify new technologies/interfaces and develop board power delivery architecture.
  • Experience in project management, including leading projects and manage timelines and resources effectively.
  • Familiarity with emerging technologies such as GaN power devices, switched capacitor topology, etc.
  • Experience delivering products for high-volume production and cost optimization.
  • Knowledge of board and power management (HW/SW/FW) debugging.
  • Willing to provide hardware technical support to ODM/OEM board vendors.
  • Willingness to travel globally to meet internal teams and external customers.

title: Sort/Test Quality & Reliability Engineer (QRE)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.


Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.


Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel


As a Sort/Test Quality & Reliability Engineer, you will lead quality and reliability readiness for tester hardware, test modules, test processes, manufacturing systems, and supplier-developed solutions used in semiconductor development and high-volume manufacturing. Drive shift-left risk prevention, qualification rigor, test process certification, and disciplined HVM transfer through cross-functional execution with Test Development, Product Engineering, Manufacturing QnR, ATM, factories, suppliers, and ODM partners.


Your responsibilities may include but not limited to:

  • Test Process Definition and Certification: Lead pathfinding, test process development, qualification, certification, and HVM ramp across products, architectures, Sort, and back-end test.
  • QnR Requirements and Risk Prevention: Define requirements, readiness criteria, acceptance plans, FMEA, and mitigation closure for tester platforms, modules, interface hardware, burn-in, wafer/die sort, metrology, and supplier hardware.
  • Qualification Strategy: Lead Installation Qualification, Module Operational Qualification, Measurement System Analysis, HVM and Transfer Qualification, Reliability Validation, Change Qualification, and production release reviews.
  • Module Manufacturing Qualification: Ensure test processes achieve quality, yield, miscorrelation, gain, capability, stability, cost, and customer-risk objectives before transfer and during ramp.
  • Technology Transfer and Factory Support: Enable successful and timely transfer to ATM factories; provide effective IPG QRE support for engineering, qualification, pilot, and revenue production.
  • Methodology Ownership: Own, define, and update Test Process Certification methods, specifications, critical success indicators, qualification templates, and release criteria.
  • QMS Deployment: Establish and maintain FMEA, Control Plans, MSA, SPC, OCAP, calibration, traceability, data integrity, change control, work instructions, and audit-ready evidence.
  • Excursion and Corrective Action Leadership: Lead MQE, excursion, yield, hardware, and reliability investigations using 8D, 5 Why, fault isolation, DOE, and model-based problem solving; verify corrective action effectiveness and recurrence prevention.
  • Analytics and Continuous Improvement: Use statistical analysis and manufacturing data to monitor process health, predict emerging risk, reduce escapes, improve qualification efficiency, and strengthen certification decisions.

Qualifications:

Candidates must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. The experience listed below may be obtained through schoolwork, research, classes and project work, internships, military training, and/or work experience.


Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree with 4+ years of relevant experience, OR Master's degree with 3+ years of relevant experience, OR PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, Metallurgy, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, Reliability Engineering, or a related technical field.


Relevant Experiences Include:

  • Experience in one or more of the following: test process development, product development, HVM factory operations, semiconductor manufacturing, product test methodology and standards, die preparation, SORT/SDx, hardware development, reliability engineering, failure analysis, or process certification.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead risk assessments, qualification plans, corrective actions, readiness reviews, technical decisions, and cross-functional execution.
  • Strong statistical, analytical, written, and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical risk into clear actions and decisions.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Semiconductor Test and Flow
  • Wafer sort, die sort, final test, burn-in, SLT, HDMT/AHMT, V93K/Advantest
  • Die prep, probing, package assembly, back-end test, and end-to-end material flow from silicon fab to customer
  • Test Process Definition, Test Process Certification, ATTD development, HVM transfer, and ATM excursion management
  • Identify electrical, thermal, mechanical, contamination, ESD, and test-induced product risks.
  • Define mitigation plans and closure criteria.
  • Ensure risks are tracked through development, qualification, and production ramp.

Quality, Reliability and Analytics:

  • FMEA, Control Plan, SPC, OCAP, 8D, DOE, reliability validation, and change control
  • Electrical, thermal, mechanical, contamination, ESD, and test-induced product risk assessment
  • JMP/JSL, SQL, statistical modeling, process capability, correlation, and predictive monitoring
  • Advanced packaging, foundry manufacturing, supplier quality, and ODM manufacturing systems

Take advantage of this opportunity to join Intel and shape the future of engineering. Apply today to be part of a team that drives industry-leading innovation and transformation.

title: Yield Product Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role

As a Yield Product Development Engineer, you will be at the forefront of advancing Intel's cutting-edge process technologies within our Manufacturing Development and Customer Engineering (MDCE) organization. This pivotal role involves identifying root cause yield limiters and driving solutions that enhance manufacturability and yield across technology nodes. You will work within a dynamic, fast-paced environment to ensure the successful introduction of new products, process improvements, and robust methodologies to meet manufacturing goals. Your expertise will directly contribute to Intel's ability to deliver world-class semiconductor solutions and advance the future of computing.

Your responsibilities as a Yield Product Development Engineer will include but not be limited to:

  • Develop methods, processes, and systems to consolidate and analyze diverse big data sources for defect mode understanding and yield modeling.
  • Perform statistical analysis, create visualizations, and construct process development roadmaps that drive technology yield milestones.
  • Extract insights from structured and unstructured data using advanced statistics, machine learning, and coding techniques.
  • Organize, interpret, and structure insights from fab process, defect, and electrical data while identifying anomalies to drive process changes for yield enhancement.
  • Develop multivariate algorithms and tools to identify root cause yield limiters and recommend process changes for yield improvement.
  • Collaborate with design teams to resolve yield issues, ensuring manufacturability across process and product specifications before ramping production.
  • Execute new product introductions, enable design-technology co-optimization, and participate in design of experiments with factory task forces.
  • Develop measurement recipes for rapid feedback on product integrity and address issues impacting yield or product quality.
  • Create and harden systems capable of meeting operational needs for leading-edge logic nodes, working with equipment vendors and internal collaborators.
  • Develop AI/ML applications and computational tools to bridge the gap between design and manufacturing, improve design efficiency, and reduce debug time.
  • Document technical procedures, train colleagues, and debug equipment, software, and procedural failures in production environments when required.

title: Manufacturing Equipment Technician (MTE) - Front End Nights Shift - Shift 4
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Corporation is one of the world's leading semiconductor companies, driving innovation that shapes the future of technology. With a legacy of over 50 years of engineering excellence, Intel is at the forefront of developing cutting-edge solutions in computing, connectivity, and advanced manufacturing. Our Advanced Packaging Technology Development – Substrate and Wafer Assembly (ATPD: SWA) organization is a global leader in delivering innovative, cost-effective substrate packaging solutions that power the devices and infrastructure of tomorrow. At Intel Arizona, we are proud to be part of a thriving technology hub where world-class talent comes together to solve some of the most complex challenges in semiconductor manufacturing.

Are you passionate about hands-on technical work and eager to be part of a team that is shaping the future of semiconductor manufacturing? Intel is seeking a Manufacturing Equipment Technician (MTE) - Front End Nights Shift - Shift 4 to join our Advanced Packaging Technology Development team in Chandler, Arizona. In this role, you will be at the heart of our manufacturing operations, ensuring the reliability and performance of advanced electromechanical systems used in semiconductor production. You will perform critical maintenance, troubleshooting, and calibration activities that directly impact Intel's production efficiency and technological advancement. This is an exciting opportunity to grow your technical career within a world-class organization that values innovation, continuous learning, and collaboration.

Shift Hours: Employees working Shift 4 (Sun-Tues and alternating Saturday nights) start their shift at 6:00 PM and finish at 6:30 AM.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Perform electrical and mechanical troubleshooting to diagnose and resolve issues with advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
  • Execute setup, calibration, corrective, and preventative maintenance on production equipment, including wet chemistry, plating, and dry high-vacuum toolsets.
  • Monitor tool performance and analyze equipment data to proactively identify and address issues before they impact production.
  • Collaborate with engineering and cross-functional support teams to improve equipment reliability, reduce downtime, and drive operational excellence.
  • Document maintenance activities, repair findings, and parts usage accurately using established systems and procedures.
  • Lead or contribute to continuous improvement projects, focusing on equipment optimization, yield enhancements, and process efficiency.
  • Support cleanroom operations while strictly adhering to safety protocols and maintaining full cleanroom attire at all times.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • Collaborative Spirit – You thrive in team environments and build strong working relationships across engineering and operations teams.
  • Analytical Thinking – You approach problems with curiosity and a methodical mindset, always seeking the root cause.
  • Clear Communication – You express ideas confidently, both verbally and in writing, ensuring alignment across teams.
  • Adaptability – You embrace change and remain effective in a fast-paced, evolving manufacturing environment.
  • Attention to Detail – You take pride in precision and accuracy, whether documenting findings or executing maintenance procedures.
  • Growth Mindset – You are committed to continuous learning and actively seek opportunities to develop your skills and knowledge.
  • Time Management – You prioritize effectively, managing multiple tasks without compromising quality or safety.

Ready to make your mark on the future of semiconductor technology? Apply today and join a team of innovators at Intel's Arizona campus who are passionate about pushing the boundaries of what's possible. Whether you're just starting your career or bringing years of technical expertise, Intel offers a place where your contributions matter and your career can flourish.

    • Bachelor’s degree in a STEM field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics) with 2+ years of experience.

    • HS/GED or higher non-semi degree AND 4+ years Field Service Engineer (2) level semiconductor maintenance experience

The Role and Impact


As a Module Engineering PhD Intern, you will play a key role in developing and sustaining semiconductor manufacturing processes for a specific module. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include supporting equipment troubleshooting, performing maintenance and qualification activities, and collaborating with engineering teams to optimize process control methodologies. This role offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in semiconductor manufacturing while building essential skills for a future career in engineering.

The team focuses on advancing semiconductor fabrication processes in areas such as Diffusion, Dielectrics, Implant, EPI, and FE Metals. As part of this group, you will contribute to Intel's mission of creating world-changing technology that enables global progress and enriches lives.

As members of the Manufacturing Development and Customer Engineering (MDCE) team, we are responsible for improving process capability for multiple technology nodes (Intel 18A, Intel 3, Intel 12nm and upcoming technologies) from initial product qualification through high volume manufacturing. The focus will be on delivering yield improvement, performance enhancement, variation and cost reduction.

title: NPI Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

We are seeking experienced and highly driven individuals to support the Kulim Assembly and Test Manufacturing facility as a New Product Integrator. This role is responsible for coordinating and executing New Product Introduction (NPI) activities to ensure successful product startup from engineering builds through high volume manufacturing (HVM). Responsibilities / Expectations: • Plan and manage NPI execution activities as a product integrator, supporting the development, implementation, and ramp of new technologies or products for external customers. • Act as the primary coordination point for NPI build execution, engaging cross functional teams across engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supply chain to enable successful product startup. • Develop and manage detailed NPI execution plans, including task identification, dependency definition, effort and duration estimation, and project schedule tracking. • Track and publish Performance Against Schedule, ensuring achievement of Critical Success Indicators (CSIs) across key NPI milestones, including: o Recipe Check Out o Power On o Engineering Sample o Quality Sample o Factory Certification o Manufacturing Validation • Ensure manufacturing readiness by coordinating system setup, process flow definition, material readiness, and capacity availability to support NPI builds and data collection. • Understand product and process challenges and work closely with technical experts across multiple groups to identify solutions and drive Design for Manufacturability (DFM) alignment during NPI execution. • Proactively identify improvement opportunities and support improvement actions to enhance NPI delivery effectiveness, predictability, and quality. • Lead investigation of issues impacting NPI deliverables, perform structured root cause analysis, align risk mitigation actions, and coordinate resolution with responsible functional owners. • Follow up on recovery actions to ensure NPI schedules and sample volume commitments are met with acceptable quality. • Document NPI readiness and deliverables, including process flow, build routing, BOM, and qualification artifacts, and support preparation of factory certification qualification documentation.

title: AI Model Optimization Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact

Intel is seeking an AI Model Performance Optimization Engineer to help deliver high-performance AI solutions that enable the next generation of client computing experiences. In this role, you will enable, validate, benchmark, optimize, and debug AI models to ensure they run efficiently and accurately across Intel hardware platforms.

Working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, machine learning frameworks, software engineering, and hardware acceleration, you will collaborate with engineers across Intel to improve AI model performance, scalability, and adoption by customers and partners worldwide.

This is an exciting opportunity for engineers passionate about Generative AI, machine learning systems, model optimization, and performance engineering who want to influence technologies used by millions of people globally.

What You Will Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Enable, validate, benchmark, and optimize AI models on Intel platforms to address customer and market segment needs.
  • Analyze model performance and identify optimization opportunities.
  • Debug issues across AI frameworks, software stacks, and hardware platforms.
  • Develop and execute tests to ensure model functionality, accuracy, and performance.
  • Collaborate with software, hardware, compiler, and architecture teams to solve technical challenges.
  • Utilize AI-assisted development tools to improve engineering productivity.
  • Contribute code, bug fixes, documentation, and test coverage to internal and open-source projects.
  • Work effectively with globally distributed engineering teams.
  • Mentor junior engineers and share technical expertise across the team.

Behavioral traits that we are looking for:

  • Curiosity and Learning Agility: Demonstrates a passion for learning emerging AI technologies, frameworks, and development methodologies.
  • Problem Solving: Approaches complex technical challenges with structured analysis and creative thinking.
  • Ownership: Takes initiative, drives issues to resolution, and delivers high-quality results with accountability.
  • Collaboration: Works effectively across software, hardware, architecture, and product teams to achieve shared objectives.
  • Adaptability: Thrives in fast-paced environments where priorities and technologies evolve rapidly.
  • Communication: Communicates complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Global Teamwork: Works effectively across geographically distributed teams and diverse perspectives.

Intel invests in our people and offers a complete and competitive package of benefits employees and their families through every stage of life. 

  • See  Intel Benefits for more details.

Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in a Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related technical discipline with 3+ years of hands-on experience in AI frameworks, algorithms, and programming OR Master's degree in the same field with 2+ years of experience.

Your experience described above must be in the following

  • Programming in Python and/or C++.
  • Experience with machine learning or deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.

At Intel, you'll help shape the future of AI by developing technologies that improve the performance and efficiency of AI applications used worldwide. Performs integration of all dies in a package and completes the relevant checks before tape out. Creates and physical database for the IP. Collaborates with architects to optimize the placement of IPs for latency as well as die area/aspect ratio. Creates specifications and collaterals for the IP blocks to execute the floorplan and automatic place and route (APR) at subsequent hierarchies. Collaborates with the clock design and logic design teams to deliver the physical block level floorplans for APR. Collaborates with the power delivery team on tradeoffs for metal allocation for signal and power. Business group You will join Intel Corporation's team focused on CPU design and development, contributing to the creation of groundbreaking technologies that enable world-class computing solutions. This group thrives on innovation, delivering high-performance designs that support Intel's mission to shape the future of technology through the creation of industry-leading products. Key Responsibilities In this role you will be responsible for all the aspects of Floorplan and pin placement activities. You will engage with Architecture, DFT and package to arrive at optimal chip planning early in the design cycle. You will work closely with physical design cluster leads to comprehend design challenges and arrive at optimal floorplan. You will play critical role in die size estimation and in evaluating Floorplan tools, methods and flows. Planning boundaries and pin densities to facilitate high confidence timing closure and routability. With your broad understanding of physical design you will play a critical role in identifying and solving multitude design issues at partition/cluster and full chip. Expertise with multiple aspects of ASIC integration including Floorplanning, Clock and Power distribution, global signal planning, IO planning and hard IP integration.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or equivalent education, with 4+ years of hands-on experience OR Master's degree in a relevant field with 3+ years of hands-on experience. - Proven expertise in using Floor planning, APR flows, Physical Design Verification Flows using Synopsys or Cadence tools. - Proficiency in hierarchical design approach, top-down design, budgeting, timing and physical convergence. - Strong knowledge of submicron process nodes and layout verification methodologies such as LVS and DRC. - Experience at handling IP/partition/block with multiple voltage and clock domains, ESD strategies, mixed signal block integration, and advanced package technologies. Preferred Qualifications - Familiarity with scripting languages such as Tcl, Perl, or Python for automation in physical design workflows. - Strong collaboration and communication skills to work effectively in cross-functional teams. - Proven ability to work in dynamic and cross-geographical environments. - Knowledge of feature feasibility studies and advanced design flow methodologies. We're excited to welcome passionate engineers who thrive in innovative environments and are eager to contribute to shaping the future of computing. Join us and make an impact by designing world-class CPUs that power cutting-edge technologies.

title: Yield Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact As a Yield Development Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in advancing technology node lifecycle and enhancing manufacturing yield performance. You will analyze complex data sets, develop methodologies, and collaborate across organizations to identify and resolve yield limiters. Your contributions will directly impact manufacturing process optimization, product quality, and Intel's ability to deliver cutting-edge solutions to the market. Business group The Intel Foundry group is dedicated to delivering innovative manufacturing solutions that enable industry-leading products and technologies. Focused on process development and yield enhancement, this team collaborates across design, test, and manufacturing domains to drive continuous improvement. By joining our team, you will contribute to shaping Intel's manufacturing capabilities and supporting our mission to deliver world-class semiconductor technologies. Key Responsibilities - Perform statistical analysis and create visualizations to identify yield limiters and construct accurate process development roadmaps. - Develop methods and systems to analyze big data sources, establishing optimal defect-mode understanding and yield modeling methodologies. - Analyze fab process, defect, and electrical data to detect anomalies and drive process changes for yield improvement. - Synthesize large volumes of data using statistics, machine learning, and coding techniques to extract actionable insights. - Collaborate across design, test, and manufacturing teams to debug yield limiters and implement process changes. - Conduct fault isolation and failure analyses using tools such as ATE testing, optical probing, circuit simulation, and emulation techniques. - Design measurement recipes for quick feedback on product integrity and implement solutions to address yield or quality issues. - Develop equipment and methodologies to support operational needs and enable leading-edge logic node capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications - Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities. - Effective communication skills to collaborate across multidisciplinary teams. - Ability to work in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment. - A passion for learning and adapting in a fast-paced technical environment. title: Manufacturing Equipment Technician (MTE) - Days Backend Shift - Shift 7
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is one of the world's leading semiconductor companies, driving innovation across computing, connectivity, and manufacturing. With a legacy of technological excellence and a bold vision for the future, Intel is committed to pushing the boundaries of what's possible — from the chip to the cloud. Our Advanced Packaging Technology Development – Substrate and Wafer Assembly (ATPD: SWA) organization is at the forefront of delivering innovative, cost-effective packaging solutions that power the next generation of technology. At Intel, we believe in investing in our people, fostering a culture of continuous learning, and empowering every team member to make a meaningful impact.

We are looking for a skilled and motivated Manufacturing Equipment Technician to join our ATPD: SWA team in Arizona. In this role, you will be responsible for maintaining, troubleshooting, and optimizing advanced electromechanical equipment that is critical to Intel's semiconductor manufacturing operations. Your work will directly contribute to Intel's manufacturing innovation, production efficiency, and global competitiveness. This is an exciting opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology in a world-class cleanroom environment while growing your technical career at one of the most recognized names in the semiconductor industry.

Shift Information

This role operates on Shift 7: 6:00 AM – 6:18 PM on an alternating weekly schedule:

Alternating 3-Day (Thu/Fri/Sat) and 4-Day (Wed/Thu/Fri/Sat) work weeks

Key Responsibilities:

  • Troubleshoot and resolve electrical and mechanical issues across a range of advanced manufacturing equipment.
  • Perform equipment setup, calibration, and both corrective and preventive maintenance, with a focus on wet chemistry, plating, and dry high-vacuum toolsets.
  • Analyze tool performance data to proactively identify and address reliability issues, ensuring minimal production downtime.
  • Collaborate closely with engineering and cross-functional support teams to enhance equipment functionality and streamline manufacturing processes.
  • Accurately document maintenance activities, repair findings, and parts usage in accordance with established systems and protocols.
  • Lead or actively support continuous improvement projects, including root cause analysis and equipment optimization initiatives.
  • Operate safely and effectively within a cleanroom environment, adhering to all cleanroom attire requirements and safety protocols.

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • Strong communicator — You express ideas clearly and confidently, both verbally and in writing, and can work effectively with peers and engineering teams.
  • Collaborative mindset — You thrive in team environments and build strong working relationships across functions.
  • Problem-solving orientation — You approach challenges with curiosity and persistence, always looking for the root cause.
  • Attention to detail — You take pride in accuracy, whether documenting maintenance records or calibrating sensitive equipment.
  • Adaptability — You are comfortable working in a dynamic, fast-paced manufacturing environment and embrace change.
  • Continuous improvement mindset — You are proactive in identifying opportunities to improve processes and equipment performance.
  • Accountability — You take ownership of your work and follow through on commitments.

Are you ready to be part of a team that is shaping the future of semiconductor manufacturing? At Intel in Arizona, you'll have the opportunity to work on some of the most advanced manufacturing technologies in the world, grow your skills, and make a real impact every day.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience would be obtained through a combination of prior education level classes, and current level school classes, projects, research and relevant previous job and/or internship experience. This Position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.


Minimum Qualifications:

Candidates must meet at least one of the following:

  • Bachelor's degree in a STEM field OR
  • Associate degree in a technical field with 2+ years of preventive and corrective equipment maintenance experience OR
  • High School Diploma/GED with:
    • 2.5+ years of preventive and corrective Equipment Maintenance Experience

descriptionHtml:

Intel Corporation is one of the world's leading semiconductor companies, driving innovation that shapes the future of computing, connectivity, and intelligence. With decades of engineering excellence and a commitment to pushing the boundaries of what's possible, Intel develops the technologies that power everything from personal devices to data centers and AI systems. At Intel, we believe in the power of human ingenuity — and we're looking for bold, curious minds to help us build what's next.

Are you passionate about semiconductor innovation and ready to make a real impact from day one? Intel's Epoxy MEOS team in Arizona is looking for a Packaging Module Development Engineer to join our growing team of packaging technology experts. In this role, you will be at the forefront of developing and optimizing cutting-edge assembly and packaging processes that directly influence the quality, reliability, and performance of Intel's next-generation semiconductor products.

This is an exciting opportunity for an early-career engineer who is eager to apply their academic knowledge in a world-class manufacturing and engineering environment, contribute to meaningful projects, and grow alongside some of the brightest minds in the semiconductor industry.
