title: AI Silicon Performance Modeling and Analysis Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role and Team


The AI Silicon Architecture and Performance Engineering team is responsible for developing and maintaining performance models that enable architecture exploration, design evaluation, scalability analysis, and performance projection for next-generation AI silicon products. These models are a critical component of the product development process, providing early visibility into architectural tradeoffs, bottlenecks, and optimization opportunities long before silicon availability.


We are seeking a highly experienced and motivated engineer to drive AI silicon performance modeling, validation, architectural analysis, and stakeholder engagement activities. The candidate will work closely with architects, performance stimulus generation teams, silicon design teams, and product stakeholders to evaluate and optimize key AI silicon subsystems that determine overall platform scalability and performance.


The role focuses on performance modeling and analysis of AI SoC communication fabrics, memory subsystems, scale-up and scale-out interconnects, host-device memory paths, and end-to-end data movement infrastructure. The successful candidate will leverage SystemC/TLM-based modeling methodologies to generate actionable insights that directly influence architecture and product decisions.


This position requires a unique combination of software development expertise, architecture understanding, analytical problem solving, and cross-functional technical leadership. The engineer will be expected to independently drive complex technical initiatives while serving as a trusted performance expert across multiple organizations.



Key Responsibilities:

AI Silicon Performance Model Development

  • Implement new architectural features and capabilities based on evolving product requirements.
  • Improve model fidelity, scalability, maintainability, and simulation performance.
  • Perform detailed debugging and root-cause analysis of model issues and performance anomalies.
  • Contribute to the evolution of modeling infrastructure, methodologies, and best practices.
  • Develop, maintain, and enhance SystemC/TLM-based performance models representing critical AI silicon subsystems.
    • Drive modeling of key architectural components including:
    • SoC fabrics and on-chip communication networks
    • Memory controllers and memory subsystem behavior
    • Scale-up controllers and fabrics enabling accelerator-to-accelerator communication within a node, tray, or pod
    • Scale-out controllers and fabrics enabling communication across nodes, racks, and larger AI clusters
    • Host CPU to accelerator memory paths
    • Local, host, and remote memory access paths
    • End-to-end data movement architectures

Functional Validation and Model Correlation:

  • Define and execute comprehensive validation strategies to ensure correctness and architectural accuracy of performance models.
  • Develop validation plans, regression suites, coverage methodologies, and quality metrics.
  • Correlate modeled behavior against architectural expectations, reference simulations, performance projections, and available hardware measurements.
  • Investigate and resolve discrepancies between expected and observed behavior.
  • Establish robust validation frameworks that improve stakeholder confidence in model-generated performance projections.
  • Continuously improve validation methodologies and model quality.

AI Silicon Performance Characterization and Architectural Analysis:

  • Design and execute performance studies covering a wide range of workloads, traffic patterns, and system configurations.
  • Analyze performance of communication fabrics, memory systems, and data movement paths under representative AI workloads.
  • Evaluate bandwidth utilization, latency characteristics, congestion behavior, traffic distribution, buffering efficiency, and resource utilization.
  • Characterize interactions across local memory, host memory, and remote memory domains.
  • Assess scalability of scale-up and scale-out architectures across increasingly larger deployment footprints.
  • Identify performance bottlenecks and quantify their impact on overall system throughput and efficiency.
  • Conduct architectural tradeoff studies to evaluate alternative design approaches.
  • Provide performance-driven recommendations that influence architecture and product decisions.

Performance Data Generation, Analytics and Visualization:

  • Develop frameworks and methodologies for large-scale performance data generation and analysis.
  • Create automated workflows for data collection, processing, correlation, and reporting.
  • Develop performance dashboards and visualization tools that simplify interpretation of complex performance data.
  • Define and track meaningful performance KPIs and architectural metrics.
  • Utilize Python-based analysis frameworks to process large datasets and generate actionable insights.
  • Enable efficient consumption of performance information by architects, designers, and engineering leadership.

Cross-Functional Technical Leadership and Stakeholder Engagement:

  • Partner closely with architecture teams, performance stimulus generation teams, silicon design teams, and product stakeholders.
  • Drive technical discussions related to performance methodology, architectural assumptions, workload behavior, scalability analysis, and bottleneck identification.
  • Review architectural proposals and provide performance-driven feedback.
  • Present performance studies, technical findings, and architectural recommendations to engineering leadership.
  • Influence product and architecture decisions through data-backed analysis and sound engineering judgment.
  • Act as a key technical bridge between architecture, modeling, and performance analysis organizations.

Methodology Development and Team Growth:

  • Drive improvements in modeling methodologies, simulation efficiency, and analysis workflows.
  • Identify opportunities for automation across modeling, validation, performance analysis, and reporting activities.
  • Establish best practices for model quality, performance characterization, and architectural analysis.
  • Contribute to technical mentoring and knowledge sharing across the team.
  • Support the development of junior engineers and future team growth initiatives.
  • Help cultivate a culture of technical excellence and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate should show the following behavioral traits:

  • Strong quantitative reasoning and data-driven decision-making skills.
    Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • Presentation (technical) and stakeholder management skills.
  • Influence engineering decisions through rigorous analysis and technical credibility.
  • Operate independently and deliver results in ambiguous problem spaces.
  • Independently solve complex technical problems.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications, you must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position.

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Electronics Engineering.

  • 6+ years of industry experience in:

    • Performance modeling, AI silicon architecture, SoC architecture, computer architecture, performance engineering, or related domains.
    • SoC architecture, including on-chip communication fabrics, NoC concepts, high-speed interconnects, and scale-up/scale-out communication architectures.
    • Memory subsystem architecture, including memory controllers, cache hierarchies, data movement, and latency/bandwidth characterization and performance bottleneck analysis.
    • Software development experience in C++.
    • Working proficiency in Python for automation, performance analysis, data processing, and visualization.
    • Hands-on experience with SystemC and Transaction-Level Modeling (TLM) methodologies.
    • Experience developing or validating performance models for AI accelerators, SoCs, CPUs, GPUs, networking products, or complex hardware systems.
    • Performing architectural tradeoff analysis and performance debug and characterization studies.

This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.


Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

  • Deep understanding of AI accelerator architectures and modern AI infrastructure.
  • Experience modeling memory, communication, interconnect, or scalability-related subsystems.
  • Experience with Network-on-Chip (NoC) architecture and interconnect performance analysis.
  • Understanding of scale-up and scale-out architectures used in modern AI computing platforms.
  • Familiarity with AI/ML workloads, large language models, distributed training, and inference environments.
  • Experience with performance stimulus generation methodologies and workload characterization.
  • Experience building automated dashboards and reporting solutions using Power BI, Tableau, Grafana, Plotly, or similar technologies.
  • Experience evaluating large-scale distributed AI systems and accelerator clusters.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and providing technical leadership in cross-functional environments.

title: DevOps Engineering Intern
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join the DevOpsAI Integration and Distribution organization and gain hands-on experience operating the continuous integration infrastructure behind large-scale driver and platform validation.

Our CI systems run validation around the clock on a large fleet of physical test machines. Today the bulk of that is Linux graphics driver testing, and the scope is expanding to other platforms and products. At this scale, hardware failures are a daily occurrence, and they surface as reports from developers whose tests failed on a machine they suspect is faulty.

As an intern on this team, you will be the first line of triage for those reports. You will confirm what actually happened, determine whether the fault lies in the machine or in the software under test, and route it to the right owner - a lab support request for a physical repair, or back to the development team when a test left the system in a state that only looks like a hardware fault. Distinguishing between the two is the core skill of this role and the one you will develop fastest.

The work is primarily analytical and log-driven: reading system logs, debug output, and monitoring dashboards, and recognizing the detail that does not fit. We value curiosity highly here - the instinct to keep investigating until the cause is understood - and we care more about how you approach a problem than about the length of your CV.

There is also scope to apply AI in this role, and we encourage it: helpers that summarize or classify large volumes of log data, and monitoring tools that use AI to surface anomalies worth a human review. This is both a practical way to accelerate your own work and a direction that matters to the wider organization.

The team and how we work

The team is based in Poland and works in a hybrid model. Because a significant part of this work involves physical test systems in the lab, regular on-site presence is required; this is not a fully remote position. We are a small, fast-moving team with an informal and collaborative culture.

Key Responsibilities

- Triage incoming infrastructure failure reports: review logs and test artifacts, assess the state of the machine, and determine whether the fault originates in the hardware or in the software under test.
- Raise lab support requests for confirmed hardware faults, documenting the affected component, the symptoms observed, and the causes already ruled out.
- Return software-induced failures to the owning team, identifying the test or change that left the system in a faulty state.
- Monitor the health of the test fleet across our dashboards - machine availability, device detection, storage and network errors - and escalate anomalies before they lead to widespread test failures.
- Collect diagnostics on demand: system and kernel logs, console output, device and firmware state, and artifacts from specific CI runs.
- Work directly with test systems in the lab: verify connections and peripherals, confirm component replacements, and validate that a machine is ready to return to production.
- Track recurring failures so the team can identify the least reliable components and platforms, and feed those findings into how the environment is built.
- Automate recurring checks, including with AI-assisted tooling, turning manual dashboard reviews and log analysis into repeatable processes.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

The candidate must be pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electronics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
- Curiosity and persistence in investigating technical problems, with the patience to work through logs and evidence.
- Working knowledge of the Linux command line and the ability to read system and kernel logs.
- Basic scripting ability in Python or shell.
- A methodical, evidence-based approach to troubleshooting, including the ability to state clearly what has been ruled out.
- Clear written communication in English, as much of this work involves handing findings to others in an actionable form.
- Availability to work on site in the lab on a regular basis, within a hybrid arrangement.

Preferred Qualifications
- Exposure to CI/CD systems, monitoring, or observability tooling.
- Interest in applying AI and large language models to practical problems such as log analysis, failure classification, or anomaly detection.
- Practical PC hardware experience, including assembling systems, replacing components, and diagnosing faults.
- Familiarity with containers and automation tooling such as Docker, Jenkins, or Ansible.
- Experience with log or data analysis and with presenting findings clearly.
- Familiarity with Git and pull request workflows.
- Interest in open source and in the operation of large-scale validation infrastructure.

title: GPU Validation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is shaping the future of technology to help create a better future for the entire world. Our work in pushing forward fields like AI, analytics, and cloud-to-edge technology is at the heart of countless innovations. With a career at Intel, you'll have the opportunity to use technology to power major breakthroughs and create enhancements that improve our everyday quality of life. Join us and help make the future more wonderful for everyone. Want to learn more? Visit our YouTube Channel or the link below.


Life at Intel


The Role and Impact
As a GPU Validation Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability and performance of Intel's industry-leading graphics processing units (GPUs). Your day-to-day responsibilities will involve defining and executing validation methodologies, debugging, and optimizing GPU features. By contributing to the development of cutting-edge validation infrastructure, you will help deliver products that meet rigorous performance, power, and quality standards. This position offers an exciting opportunity to innovate and make a tangible impact on Intel's graphics technology.

Business group
You will be part of Intel's Data Center Group (DCG), a team dedicated to delivering world-class GPU solutions for diverse applications such as gaming, AI, and high-performance computing. DCG focuses on driving innovation and supporting Intel's mission to shape the future of technology by creating advanced graphics architectures that power systems across desktop, mobile, server, and edge environments.

Key Responsibilities
- Define, develop, and execute validation methodologies for GPUs, focusing on interaction between media, display, and system-level features.

- Build and test emulation and prototyping models for GPU.
- Perform silicon debug to identify root causes and resolve functional and triage failures for GPU-related issues.
- Develop and maintain post-silicon validation infrastructure, including performance monitors, behavioral checkers, and test environments.
- Conduct validation testing to ensure performance, power, and area goals are met, leveraging hardware and software tools.
- Review design changes to assess their impact on validation plans, timelines, and tasks.
- Test interactions between GPU features using validation tools and infrastructure.
- Collaborate with architecture, design, board, platform, and manufacturing teams to optimize validation methodologies.
- Publish comprehensive GPU validation reports, summarize results, and communicate findings to relevant teams.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your school work/classes/research and/or relevant previous job and/or internship experiences.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field with 4+ years of industry experience OR Master's degree in a relevant field with 3+ years of experience.
  • 4+ years' experience in pre-silicon validation techniques, tools, and debugging.
  • 4+ years' experience in C, C++, Python, and scripting for automation and validation tasks.
  • 4+ years' experience in computer architecture and microarchitecture fundamentals.
  • 4+ years' experience with emulation (preferably ZeBu/Palladium).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with PCIe standards and compliance processes.
  • Knowledge of GPU architecture.
  • Experience with FPGA prototyping, or acceleration platforms.
  • Experience developing validation protocols and strategies.
  • Experience with hardware debug tools such as logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, and in-circuit emulators.
  • Exposure to Design for Debug (DFD) tools and methodologies.
  • Familiarity with GPU artificial intelligence benchmarks, rendering concepts, and industry-standard APIs.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills with cross-functional teams.

Join Intel's GPU Validation team and contribute to shaping the future of graphics technology through innovation and excellence. Apply now and take the next step in advancing your career.

Project Context
Generative AI is rapidly transforming enterprise applications, with organizations increasingly deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) for conversational AI, knowledge retrieval, software development, content generation, and intelligent automation. As model sizes and user adoption continue to grow, delivering low-latency, cost-efficient, and scalable AI inference becomes a critical challenge.
Modern AI serving stacks combine model serving frameworks, optimized inference engines, cloud infrastructure, and observability platforms to deliver production-ready AI services. Organizations must balance performance metrics such as throughput, Time to First Token (TTFT), Time per Output Token (TPOT), latency, scalability, and total cost of ownership (TCO) while supporting a diverse range of deployment environments spanning on-premises datacenters, private clouds, and public cloud platforms.
This internship focuses on developing and validating modern AI inference solutions using technologies such as vLLM, SGLang, and OpenVINO. The work will involve deploying and benchmarking state-of-the-art LLMs, analyzing inference performance across Intel platforms, automating testing and deployment workflows, and evaluating cloud-native AI architectures. The objective is to help build scalable, efficient, and production-ready AI serving solutions that enable customers to maximize the value of Generative AI deployments.

What You'll Work On
You will explore the design, deployment, and optimization of Generative AI infrastructure, including:
- LLM deployment and serving: Deploy and evaluate large language models using frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, and OpenVINO
- Performance analysis: Measure and optimize serving metrics including throughput, latency, TTFT, TPOT, concurrency, and resource utilization
- AI benchmarking: Develop automated benchmarking workflows to characterize model performance across different hardware and software configurations
- Cloud infrastructure: Deploy and evaluate AI workloads in AWS and Google Cloud Platform environments
- DevOps and automation: Build CI/CD pipelines, test automation, and infrastructure tooling using Jenkins, Python, and Linux-based environments
- Data management: Design and maintain systems for storing, querying, and analyzing benchmarking and telemetry data using PostgreSQL and related technologies
- Solution validation: Investigate trade-offs between performance, scalability, accuracy, and cost across various deployment scenarios

Why This Internship?
- Cutting-edge AI engineering: Work on real-world Generative AI deployment and inference optimization challenges
- Industry impact: Contribute to technologies that help customers deploy and scale AI solutions on Intel platforms
- Hands-on experience: Gain practical expertise with LLM serving frameworks, cloud infrastructure and execution
- Mentorship: Learn from experts in AI systems, performance engineering, cloud computing, and software development
- Broad technical exposure: Develop skills across AI, Linux, DevOps, cloud computing, databases, and infrastructure automation
- Intel ecosystem: Build deep knowledge of AI deployment and optimization on Intel Xeon processors and Intel AI software solutions

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications:
- Strong background in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Science, or related field
- Programming skills: Proficiency in Python and experience developing software applications and automation tools
- LLM knowledge: Understanding of transformer-based generative AI models, inference workflows, tokenization, quantization, and serving architectures
- Linux proficiency: Experience working in Linux environments, shell scripting, system monitoring, and troubleshooting
- Academic standing: Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD program in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering or related field

Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience with one of LLM serving frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, TGI, or similar
- Experience benchmarking and performance tuning AI inference workloads

- Cloud fundamentals: Experience with AWS and/or Google Cloud Platform services
- DevOps knowledge: Understanding of CI/CD concepts and tools such as Jenkins, Git, and containerized workflows
- Knowledge of model optimization techniques including quantization, pruning, KV-cache optimization, and speculative decoding
- Experience working with container orchestration technologies such as Kubernetes and Docker
- Experience building APIs and services using Python frameworks such as FastAPI
- Personal or academic projects involving LLM deployment, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, or inference optimization

Take the next step in your career by joining a team passionate about advancing the future of AI software. This internship offers a unique opportunity to develop your skills, contribute to impactful projects, and grow alongside industry-leading experts.

Responsibilities include capturing user stories/requirements, writing both functional and test code, automating build and deployment, and/or performing unit, integration, and end to end testing of the software tools. Designs and builds web-based interfaces to configure launch and control tools - including frontends, backends, databases and APIs.  

The Frame is a critical component of every wafer that is manufactured by Intel. The frame contains silicon structures that are needed by various metrology and lithographic tools.  Intel's Frame Automation Team is responsible for developing automation and specifications to support the Frame.  To keep the process going, we work closely with engineers from Lithography, Process Integration, Device Physics, Circuit Design, and RET (Resolution Enhancement Technology) teams to understand and establish frame structures. We design frame structures so that the next generation of Intel products are the best they can be.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop, test, and debug software tools and methodologies for design automation
  • Capture user stories and requirements to inform tool design and functionality
  • Write functional and test code to ensure software performance and reliability
  • Automate build and deployment processes to optimize development workflows
  • Conduct unit, integration, and end-to-end testing of software tools for quality assurance
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align tool functionality with business needs

OR

As a Facilities Water/Waste Treatment Technician, you will play a critical role in the operation and maintenance of Intel's industrial water and wastewater systems. title: Gases Technician
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role

Intel Foundry is seeking a skilled Gases Technician to support the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of gas delivery systems that enable advanced semiconductor manufacturing. In this role, you will operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and continuously improve critical gas distribution infrastructure that directly impacts manufacturing performance, product quality, and

operational reliability.

As a member of the Facilities team, you will partner with engineers, manufacturing teams, suppliers, and fellow technicians to ensure uninterrupted delivery of high-purity gases while maintaining Intel's world-class standards for safety, quality, and environmental stewardship.

What You'll Do


Operations & Maintenance

  • Operate, monitor, maintain, and troubleshoot gas delivery systems supporting high-volume semiconductor manufacturing.
  • Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on gas distribution equipment and associated facility systems.
  • Conduct inspections, repairs, equipment changeovers, and system restorations while ensuring compliance with established procedures.
  • Coordinate gas deliveries, vendor activities, and operational transitions to maintain uninterrupted manufacturing support.

Monitoring & Troubleshooting

  • Monitor SCADA/Cimplicity and related control systems to evaluate alarms, trends, and system performance.
  • Diagnose equipment and process issues using operational data, analytical instrumentation, and technical expertise.
  • Respond to equipment alarms and abnormal operating conditions, minimizing manufacturing impacts and restoring safe operations.
  • Lead structured troubleshooting and root-cause analysis efforts to resolve recurring reliability, process, and gas-quality issues.

Quality & Continuous Improvement

  • Perform gas sampling and analytical testing while maintaining contamination control and sample integrity requirements.
  • Support semiconductor purity standards through knowledge of gas compatibility, materials of construction, and process controls.
  • Identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities that enhance reliability, reduce operational risk, and prevent future failures.
  • Review performance trends and equipment history to proactively address emerging issues before they affect manufacturing.

Documentation & Collaboration

  • Maintain accurate maintenance, operational, sampling, and shift-turnover records.
  • Utilize computerized maintenance management systems and digital tools to document work and track asset performance.
  • Support the development and revision of operating procedures, job plans, risk assessments, and change-control documentation.
  • Share technical knowledge and assist with training and qualification of technicians.

Job Requirements

Candidates must be able to:

  • Work a compressed 12-hour night-shift schedule, rotating between three and four days per week.
  • Work in cleanroom and industrial environments while wearing required personal protective equipment.
  • Lift and carry up to 30 pounds and move heavier materials using approved handling equipment.
  • Walk several miles per shift and work in physically demanding environments.
  • Support weekend, holiday, overtime, and on-call operational requirements as needed.
  • Work at heights, climb ladders, and operate powered industrial equipment after certification.

What Makes You Successful

The ideal candidate demonstrates:

  • An unwavering commitment to safety and quality.
  • Strong mechanical and technical troubleshooting skills.
  • Sound judgment in dynamic operational environments.
  • The ability to communicate effectively across technicians, engineers, suppliers, and manufacturing stakeholders.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • A continuous improvement mindset focused on reliability, efficiency, and operational excellence.
  • The ability to thrive in a fast-paced, team-oriented manufacturing environment.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.

This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.

    • -or-Relevant military training and technical experience.
  • Experience supporting hazardous production materials (HPM), bulk gas systems, industrial controls, or semiconductor manufacturing facilities.
  • Experience in high-purity process environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in gas delivery systems, semiconductor facilities, industrial maintenance, or related technical operations.
  • Associate or bachelor's degree in a technical field and 4 + years of technical experience.
  • Proven ability to collaborate across cross-functional teams and drive operational improvements.

Why Intel Foundry

At Intel Foundry, you'll help support the infrastructure behind some of the world's most advanced semiconductor manufacturing technologies. descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.

Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel

Intel's Foundry Automation (IFA) group is seeking an experienced Infrastructure Storage Engineer.

In this role, you will lead the architecture, deployment, optimization, and lifecycle management of NetApp storage platforms supporting engineering, cloud, virtualization, OpenShift, and AI infrastructure environments. You will be responsible for delivering scalable NAS, object, and data protection solutions while also supporting enterprise SAN services and storage integration across virtualized and platform services environments.
This role is central to designing, implementing, maintaining, and scaling high-performance storage platforms that support Intel Foundry's critical infrastructure. You will collaborate closely with platform engineering, cloud, DevOps, virtualization, and software engineering teams to build reliable, automated, and highly available storage services.
The ideal candidate combines deep NetApp expertise with storage engineering, automation, and operational excellence. Experience with enterprise SAN technologies, Fibre Channel fabrics, block storage provisioning, and storage networking concepts is highly desirable to support mixed storage environments and infrastructure modernization initiatives.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Plan, manage, and optimize installation, configuration, and tuning of NetApp NAS platforms, SAN, SDS, object storage, and backup solutions.
  • Design and implement scalable storage solutions supporting bare metal, virtualized, containerized, and cloud environments.
  • Manage storage provisioning, replication, data protection, performance optimization, capacity management, and lifecycle activities.
  • Lead storage modernization, migration, and automation initiatives while maintaining operational standards and documentation.
  • Monitor performance and utilization, troubleshoot storage issues, and ensure high availability and data integrity across the environment.
  • Partner with infrastructure, virtualization, networking, cloud, and software engineering teams to deliver reliable and scalable storage services.

  • In-depth knowledge of NAS, SAN, SDS, and Object Storage technologies, including configuration, performance tuning, capacity planning, and troubleshooting.
  • Experience with storage protocols including NFS, SMB/CIFS, S3, Fibre Channel (FC), and iSCSI.
  • Experience with NetApp technologies such as SnapMirror, SnapVault, Snapshot, FlexVol, FlexGroup, and Storage Virtual Machines (SVMs).
  • Familiarity with enterprise SAN platforms such as PowerMax or similar enterprise storage arrays.
  • Hands-on experience with enterprise backup and disaster recovery solutions such as Veeam and SnapVault.
  • Strong background supporting on-premises storage infrastructure in physical and virtualized environments, with familiarity in hybrid cloud integration.
  • Experience with automation tools such as Ansible, Python, PowerShell, and REST APIs to improve operational efficiency and scalability.
  • Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills with the ability to resolve storage, performance, replication, and capacity-related issues.

This position requires regular onsite presence at our Chandler, Arizona facility.

title: E-core CPU Full Chip Physical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Become a key member of a team participating in the physical design construction and integration and verification of a future Intel CPU. This position requires an engineer with broad physical design and STA skills, coupled with leadership skills necessary to drive methodology and to collaborate effectively with multiple functional teams within the CPU design team. We are looking for a talented individual to drive the physical convergence of a Full-Chip (FC) assembly of partitions.

As a Full Chip design engineer, you will perform floorplanning, pin and feedthrough planning, repeater insertion, power grid generation and assembly of partitions. Given the need for executing multiple projects in parallel, you will be responsible for driving efficiency and quality improvements to the overall FC methodology - including floorplan optimization for better utilization/QoR/runtime and timing and physical aware feedthrough/pin placement. You will also be responsible for coordinating collateral handoffs between the FC Design team and other functions within back-end design such as Clocking, Power Delivery and Partition synthesis/APR. You will drive physical design and timing closure including FEV, LVS, DRC, and reliability verification (IR drop / EM analysis).

The ideal candidate should have an aptitude to work effectively with EDA tools and exhibit behavioral traits that indicate:

  • Ability to work well in a team and be productive under aggressive schedules
  • Excellent written and verbal communications skills
  • Self-motivation and well organized

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.

Minimum qualifications:
Must have either BS or MS in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering
Minimum 7 years of experience in


  • CPU physical design and timing verification
  • Synthesis/APR flows on multi voltage high frequency designs including custom polygon editing
  • Tcl scripting
  • Noise, cross-talk, OCV analysis.
  • Floorplanning and physical design and timing closure.
  • Formal equivalence, DRC/LVS, IR and electro-migration checks

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is transforming its global Assembly and Test manufacturing network to support the next generation of advanced packaging, AI products, and high-volume semiconductor production. To achieve this, we are seeking an Engineering Director, Automated Material Handling Systems, to define, develop, and execute the roadmap for automated material handling systems (AMHS), factory automation, and autonomous logistics solutions across both greenfield and brownfield Assembly and Test factories.

The ideal leader has experience with fully automating high-tech manufacturing factories in Semiconductor Advanced Packaging.  They can combine their operational experience in semiconductor manufacturing, large-scale factory transformation, and strong knowledge of emerging automation technologies. The successful candidate must be able to hit the ground running as the role involves strategic direction setting as well as driving execution.

Responsibilities:

  • Create and execute a comprehensive automation strategy that drives productivity, scalability, safety, flexibility, and cost competitiveness across Intel’s global manufacturing footprint.
  • Serve as the senior program leader responsible for defining future-state factory architectures, aligning major capital investments, and leading complex factory conversion programs that modernize existing operations while enabling next-generation manufacturing capabilities.
  • Rapidly assess current factory operations, identify and prioritize near-term automation opportunities, implement practical solutions that generate measurable business value, and simultaneously build the long-term automation vision for Intel’s Assembly and Test manufacturing factories.
  • Define the Assembly & Test roadmap for automated material handling systems, autonomous logistics, robotics, digital manufacturing systems, and smart factory technologies.

  • Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering or related field
  • 10+ yrs of leading the deployment of factory automation and material handling systems in the semiconductor industry
  • Experience deploying material transport and storage in advanced package assembly and test high volume manufacturing.

title: Platform Hardware design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Position Overview: As a Platform Hardware Design Engineer, you will contribute to the end-to-end development of advanced platform hardware, translating platform level requirements into circuit and component level specifications and ultimately into high quality board designs. You will work across the hardware development lifecycle, including architecture and requirements definition, component selection, schematic design, PCB implementation, design reviews, board fabrication and assembly support, power-on, bring-up, debug, validation, and delivery. This is a hands-on engineering role for candidates who enjoy solving complex hardware problems and working across disciplines to turn system requirements into reliable, manufacturable hardware. Our Business Group You will be joining the Silicon and Platform Engineering Group (SPE), an organization at Intel committed to advancing Intel's mission of delivering world class silicon and platform solutions. The group focuses on developing integrated systems that align with customer needs and support Intel's broader goals of leadership in technology innovation. SPE collaborates across diverse domains to ensure Intel platforms meet performance, reliability, and scalability requirements. Our work sits at the intersection of silicon, board hardware, firmware, validation, signal and power integrity, mechanical and thermal engineering, PCB technology, manufacturing, and system integration. Our hardware engineers have a broader responsibility than executing an individual design. They help establish platform architecture, guide implementation, identify and qualify appropriate hardware solutions, provide technical leadership during board power-on and debug, and lead resolution of schematic, layout, SI/PI, and hardware issues. Key Responsibilities Platform and Board Design • Translate platform level requirements into circuit level, component level, and PCB design requirements. • Design and develop complex platform boards incorporating high speed digital, analog and mixed-signal circuitry considering board/system-level design tradeoffs during development. • Own schematic development for assigned boards, subsystems, and functional blocks, including component definition and selection. • Develop electrical solutions associated with processors/SoCs, FPGAs, memory, high-speed interfaces, voltage regulators, clocks, resets, control interfaces, and platform-management functions. PCB Design and Implementation • Define PCB implementation requirements, including component placement, critical interfaces, routing rules, stack-up considerations, and other layout constraints. • Work closely with PCB layout engineers and guide board implementation from feasibility through design release/tape-out while meeting multidisciplinary platform requirements. • Review complex multilayer PCB designs for electrical performance, signal integrity, power integrity, manufacturability, and system requirements. • Apply high speed transmission-line and layout principles to critical interfaces. Power, Signal Integrity and Platform Considerations • Apply signal integrity and power integrity principles during board architecture, schematic design, component selection, and PCB implementation. • Design and review power delivery architectures, voltage regulation, sequencing, power budgeting, and platform power distribution. • Work with SI/PI specialists to analyze critical high speed interfaces and power delivery networks and incorporate analysis results into board design. • Understand platform level trade-offs involving electrical performance, power, thermal constraints, PCB implementation, component availability, and manufacturability. Board Bring-up, Validation and Debug • Develop and execute board power-on, bring-up, validation, and characterization plans. • Collaborate with architects, hardware engineers, validation engineers, firmware engineers, technicians, and other specialists during platform power-on and debug. • Troubleshoot board and system level problems and perform systematic root cause analysis. • Use laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, logic analyzers, and other measurement equipment for electrical characterization and debug. Analyze failures, determine root causes, implement corrective actions, and drive issues to technical closure. Cross-functional Execution • Collaborate with silicon, firmware, validation, SI/PI, mechanical, thermal, PCB layout, manufacturing, supplier, and program teams. • Incorporate feedback from verification, validation, manufacturing, and other stakeholders into hardware development and design improvements. • Support PCB fabrication, assembly, design-for-manufacturability, design-for-test, and hardware readiness. • Create and maintain design specifications, schematics, review documentation, design checklists, bring-up plans, validation reports, and other technical collateral. • Own assigned hardware deliverables and proactively identify technical, component, manufacturing, and schedule risks.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline.
• 6+ years relevant hands-on industry experience in platform hardware, boar -level product development, PCB design, or related hardware engineering.
• Demonstrated hands-on experience with PCB design, schematic capture, component definition/selection, and interaction with PCB layout teams.
• Strong fundamentals in digital and analog board design, electrical interfaces, mixed-signal design, and platform power-on.
• Experience with high density, multilayer board design and high speed PCB implementation.
• Understanding of high speed interfaces, transmission line fundamentals, signal integrity, and power integrity.
• Knowledge of voltage regulation, power delivery, clocking, resets, and sequencing.
• Experience with industry standard schematic capture and PCB design/review tools like Cadence environments including Allegro and Concept HDL alongside other industry-standard design environments.
• Hands-on experience with board power-on, bring-up, electrical measurement, hardware debugging, and root-cause analysis.
• Strong problem solving, communication, technical documentation, and cross functional collaboration skills.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience designing complex compute, server, client, validation, FPGA based, or semiconductor development platforms.
• Experience with high speed I/O and memory interfaces such as PCIe, DDR/LPDDR, USB, Ethernet, or comparable technologies.
• Working knowledge of signal integrity, power integrity, transmission line theory, impedance control, crosstalk, PCB stack-up, and power distribution networks.
• Experience with SI/PI, circuit, or power simulation tools.
• Experience with board-level power delivery, basic Verilog coding, power budgeting, voltage regulation, sequencing, and power integrity.
• Knowledge of PCB fabrication, board assembly, DFM/DFT, manufacturing flows, and component/BOM management.
• Experience taking hardware through multiple stages of the lifecycle from design through PCB implementation, fabrication, assembly, bring-up, validation, and deployment.
• Working experience in integrating the AI-based tools and agents in regular workflow
• Familiarity with scripting or automation, such as Python, for hardware development, validation, or debug is an added advantage.
• Experience working effectively with geographically distributed engineering teams, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description:

As a Mechanical Design Engineer, you will design and develop mechanical devices, systems, equipment, and packaging that are practical, sustainable, and manufacturable. You will play a key role in creating mechanical and thermal solutions from concept through high-volume manufacturing, ensuring functionality, reliability, and safety. title: Intel Foundry Module Development Engineer - CMP
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Join Intel - and build a better tomorrow. Intel is in the midst of an exciting transformation, with a vision to create and extend computing technology to connect and enrich the lives of every person on Earth. So join us, and help us create the next generation of technologies that will shape the future for decades to come.

As the world's largest chip manufacturer, Intel strives to make every facet of semiconductor manufacturing state-of-the-art -- from semiconductor process development and manufacturing, through yield improvement to packaging, final test and optimization, and world class Supply Chain and facilities support. Employees in the Technology and Manufacturing Group are part of a worldwide network of design, development, manufacturing, and assembly/test facilities, all focused on utilizing the power of Moore's Law to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth.


Engineers within Intel's Logic Technology Development (LTD) organization are chartered with continuing to meet the challenge of Moore's Law in the 21st century. We innovate leading edge fabrication processes and continue to overcome seemingly impossible barriers as tolerances and specifications for building best-in-class computing devices become increasingly rigorous.


The role of a Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) Process Development Engineer in LTD encompasses developing and sustaining planarization techniques for a variety of materials and architectures, enabling rapid miniaturization in the semiconductor industry and the mass production of integrated circuits. CMP techniques leverage physics, chemistry, materials science and surface science concepts, and exist at the intersection of these disciplines. As a result, our team has a diverse set of scientific backgrounds that relies on strong collaboration and shared learning.


Responsibilities:

  • Designing, executing, and analyzing experiments necessary to meet engineering specifications for the process
  • Participating in the development of intellectual property
  • Developing the equipment and components necessary to leverage understanding gained in research (in collaboration with suppliers), identifying shortcomings, and proposing and evaluating modifications to mitigate issues or enable new capabilities
  • Overseeing unique CMP steps in a manufacturing line which integrates thousands of steps necessary for the manufacture of complex microprocessors, while simultaneously transferring the technology to counterparts in manufacturing sites across the globe

What We Offer:

  • The opportunity to participate in and lead Intel's state-of-the-art engineering process in the realization of our IDM 2.0 vision
  • As a global leader in innovation and new technology, we foster a collaborative, supportive, and exciting environment where the brightest minds in the world come together to achieve exceptional results
  • We offer a competitive salary and financial benefits such as bonuses, life and disability insurance, opportunities to buy Intel stock at a discounted rate, and Intel stock awards (eligibility at the discretion of Intel Corporation)
  • We provide benefits that promote a healthy, enjoyable life: excellent medical plans, wellness programs, and amenities, time off, recreational activities, discounts on various products and services, and many more creative perks that make Intel a Great Place to Work

We're constantly working on making a more connected and intelligent future, and we need your help. Change tomorrow. Start today.

OR

  • Masters degree in Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related Scientific STEM field of study with 3+ years of Semiconductor Industry experience (semiconductor processing and semiconductor fabrication)

OR

title: Defect Review Technician
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Be a part of Intel's Advanced Packaging Command Center (APCC), the global command center for Advanced Packaging that provides remote capabilities, follow-on engineering, and operational support across Wafer Packaging Manufacturing (WPM). Through APCC, engineering expertise is focused to improve coordination across regions, drive standardization, and improve responsiveness, while strengthening end-to-end operational execution across regions and delivering consistent, high-quality execution at scale.

As the defect review technician, you will be instrumental in supporting global defect review activities, including defect classification, validation, and hold lot disposition. You will help maintain quality excellence while contributing to APCC's mission of delivering standardized, high-quality execution at scale. Your primary focus will be the accurate classification of defects captured by multiple inspection systems. Through precise defect classification, you will play a vital role in minimizing defect noise, driving systematic defect reduction initiatives, and maintaining the optimal balance between quality control and manufacturing efficiency.

Responsibilities will include but are not limited to
Defect Classification and Analysis:
• Review and Analyze defect images captured by diverse metrology tools.
• Accurately classify defects based on documented defect specification.
• Distinguish between true defects requiring disposition action and false positives or nuisance defects.
• Maintain proficiency across multiple inspection platforms and adapt classification criteria to different tool capabilities and imaging conditions

Defect Validation:
• Verify defect classifications against established criteria and specifications
• Partner with Layer Owner to ensure consistent defect categorization approaches
• Prevent over-rejection scenarios by accurately identifying non-critical defects and cosmetic variations that do not impact product performance.
• Avoid under-rejection situations by ensuring killed defects are properly identified and flagged for disposition.

Hold Lot Disposition:
• Ensure strict compliance in review and disposition of hold lots based on documented Out-of-Control Action Plans (OCAP)
• Ensure proper documentation and traceability of all disposition decisions.
• Collaborate with Layer Owner to update and refine OCAP procedures based on emerging defect patterns
• First Level Defect Analysis

• Document initial findings and recommendations to support Layer Owner analysis and decision-making processes.

• Proficiency in computer-based work and ability to maintain focus and accuracy while reviewing large volumes of inspection images.

• Willingness to learn new technologies, inspection platforms, and manufacturing processes.

title: Compiler Performance Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Compiler Engineering team within Intel's Data Center Group is seeking talented and passionate compiler engineers to help shape the future of software development.

At Intel, we are building next-generation software technologies that unlock the full potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies enable developers to efficiently leverage CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. Our mission is to design, innovate, and deliver industry-leading compilers and development tools that maximize hardware performance across Intel platforms. By advancing performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity, we empower AI, HPC, and other compute-intensive workloads while maintaining a strong commitment to open-source collaboration and innovation.

Our team develops LLVM-based compiler technologies for C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, domain-specific languages (DSLs), and Fortran, targeting Intel CPUs and GPUs. We work across the entire compiler stack, including language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization frameworks, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality engineering, and developer tooling.


This role provides exceptional opportunities for technical growth and career development through hands-on work with cutting-edge compiler technologies, mentorship from experienced engineers and technical leaders, and collaboration with world-class engineering teams across the globe.


Responsibilities

As part of the compiler performance and optimization team, you will gain firsthand experience in the technologies that transform source code into highly optimized machine code. Your responsibilities will include:

  • Analyzing performance issues in compiler-generated code and identifying root causes within optimization and code generation stages.
  • Measuring and tuning application performance on Intel CPUs and GPUs while tracking regressions and identifying optimization opportunities.
  • Designing and implementing automated testing solutions to continuously monitor compiler performance and quality.
  • Bridging Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI and HPC software ecosystems, including PyTorch, inference frameworks, and machine learning workloads.
  • Contributing to open-source compiler communities through issue reporting, patch development, code reviews, and technical discussions.
  • Developing and enhancing compiler components, including optimization passes, code generation features, runtime systems, and offload technologies under the guidance of senior engineers.

As a Process Integration Development Engineer, you will drive revolutionary advancements in substrate manufacturing technologies, ensuring smooth and efficient integration processes for next-generation packaging solutions. title: Sort Interface Pathfinding and Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel Corporation is one of the world's leading semiconductor companies, driving innovation across computing, connectivity, and artificial intelligence. With a bold vision to shape the future of technology, Intel is transforming how the world processes, stores, and communicates data. Our Advanced Packaging ,Test and Manufacturing (APTM) organization is at the forefront of this transformation, delivering industry-leading packaging and test technologies that power products across Client, Data Center, AI, Networking, and External Foundry markets. At Intel, we believe the next big thing starts with you.

We are seeking a talented and driven Sort Interface Pathfinding and Development Engineer to join our Sort Interface Development team in Oregon. In this high-impact role, you will pioneer breakthrough silicon interface probing & test solutions that enable best-in-class die and wafer sort capabilities across leading-edge process nodes and advanced heterogeneous packaging platforms — including EMIB, EMIB-T, Foveros, and Foveros Direct.

As Intel scales its Open System Foundry and OSAT (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test) business model, you will play an instrumental role in establishing world-class, customer-ready sort interface capabilities. You will lead electro-mechanical pathfinding, test hardware development, customer and supplier technical co-design, and probing process qualification to support both Intel's internal product roadmap and external Foundry customers.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Formulate and execute rigorous Design of Experiments (DOE) to optimize and qualify next-generation probing technologies and contact architectures for wafer and die sort operations
  • Serve as the lead technical liaison for Foundry and OSAT customers, translating complex chiplet and package requirements into scalable sort interface specifications
  • Author industry-standard sort design rules and Interface Design Kits (IDKs) to streamline ecosystem integration for external fabless customers and design partners
  • Collaborate with customer design and DFT teams to architect test interface hardware, resolve technical gaps, and synchronize testability roadmaps
  • Partner with global Test Solution vendors and PCB suppliers to pioneer state-of-the-art probing capabilities
  • Direct supplier and pathfinding initiatives to align vendor roadmaps with internal efficiency and performance goals
  • Drive supplier accountability and manufacturing readiness to guarantee on-time hardware delivery for critical New Product Introductions (NPI)

As a Successful Candidate, You Will Bring:

  • Collaborative mindset — you thrive working across cross-functional teams, customers, and global suppliers
  • Strong communicator — you can translate highly technical concepts into clear, actionable specifications for diverse audiences
  • Analytical thinker — you approach complex problems with curiosity, structure, and data-driven decision-making
  • Self-starter — you take initiative, drive projects forward, and hold yourself and others accountable
  • Customer-focused — you understand the importance of building trust and delivering value to external partners
  • Adaptable — you are comfortable navigating ambiguity and evolving priorities in a fast-paced, cutting-edge environment
  • Continuous learner — you stay current with emerging technologies and proactively seek opportunities to grow

If you are passionate about pushing the boundaries of advanced packaging and test technology, and you want to make a meaningful impact on products that power the world's most advanced computing systems, we want to hear from you.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related STEM field with 6+ years of industry experience OR Master's degree in the same fields with 4+ years of industry experience OR Ph.D. in the same fields with 2+ year of relevant post-graduate or industry experience
  • Relevant industry experience can be any of the following:
    • Experience with wafer/die sort Technology, prober-tester cell integration, and qualification of advanced probe card technologies
    • Structure and execute DOEs to evaluate probing margins, yield, and process health
    • Direct experience in ATE test hardware/methodology, Sort/Class product development, or PCB/space transformer/substrate design rules and stackup architectures

Preferred Qualifications:

    • Experience qualifying probe technologies for fine-pitch micro-bumps, 2.5D/3D architectures (EMIB, EMIB-T, silicon bridges), or wafer-level chip-scale probing

The Role and Impact

As an Electrical Validation Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability and performance of Intel's next-generation silicon products. You will actively validate circuit analog performance, analyze electrical signal integrity compliance, and ensure system-level margins for stable operation. This hands-on role directly contributes to the development of high-quality products that delight customers while meeting production and industry standards.


Business group

The Electrical Validation team is part of Intel Corporation, supporting Intel's commitment to delivering innovative and high-performing silicon solutions. Their focus on multidisciplinary research and collaboration plays a vital role in supporting Intel's broader mission to deliver cutting-edge technology.

title: Senior Product Failure Analysis Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role


Intel Foundry is seeking a highly skilled Senior Product Failure Analysis Engineer to lead complex failure investigations that drive product quality, manufacturing excellence, and technology development across advanced semiconductor technologies.

In this role, you will leverage deep expertise in semiconductor devices, electrical characterization, physical failure analysis, and root cause investigation to identify and solve challenging product and process issues. You will partner across engineering, manufacturing, yield, process integration, quality, reliability, and design teams to develop corrective actions that improve technology robustness and accelerate product success.

This position offers the opportunity to influence the development of future technologies while advancing Intel Foundry's commitment to delivering world-class semiconductor solutions.

What You Will Do

Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Lead complex failure analysis investigations involving semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, packages, and manufacturing processes.
  • Develop and execute comprehensive failure analysis strategies using electrical, physical, material, and structural characterization techniques.
  • Perform root cause analysis of yield, reliability, performance, and customer-return failures.
  • Utilize fault isolation and failure localization methodologies to identify defect mechanisms and process interactions.
  • Drive corrective and preventive actions through collaboration with manufacturing, process engineering, design, product engineering, quality, and reliability organizations.
  • Define and implement advanced methodologies, tools, and workflows that improve failure analysis effectiveness and throughput.
  • Provide technical leadership during technology transfers, manufacturing ramps, process qualifications, and new product introductions.
  • Analyze large datasets and laboratory findings to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Document findings and present technical recommendations to senior engineering and business stakeholders.
  • Mentor junior engineers and contribute to the development of organizational failure analysis expertise.
  • Leverage data analytics and AI-enabled tools to improve investigation efficiency, knowledge sharing, and decision-making.

Behavioral Traits that we are looking for:


  • Strong analytical thinking and structured problem-solving skills.
  • Intellectual curiosity and a passion for understanding complex failure mechanisms.
  • Technical leadership and ability to influence without direct authority.
  • Ownership mindset with accountability for delivering results.
  • Effective communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Collaboration and partnership across global, cross-functional teams.
  • Adaptability and resilience in fast-paced, highly technical environments.
  • Continuous learning mindset and willingness to embrace emerging technologies and methodologies.
  • Attention to detail while maintaining focus on broader business objectives.
  • Customer-focused approach to quality, reliability, and operational excellence.

title: AMHS Intelligent Systems Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Drive the Automated Circulatory Engine of Intel Foundry

At Intel Foundry Technology & Manufacturing, we design, build, and scale the physical and digital infrastructure that powers the future of computing. Automated Material Handling Systems (AMHS) serve as the circulatory system of Intel’s high-volume manufacturing facilities, enabling continuous 24x7 wafer transport and reticle delivery across our Gordon Moore Park at Ronler Acres and Aloha campuses.


We are seeking an experienced Manufacturing Systems Software Development Engineer to take ownership of real-time cleanroom automation architectures, high-availability control software, and data-driven factory throughput. Operating at the convergence of distributed software systems, factory physics, and advanced cleanroom operations, you will directly influence wafer cycle times, tool availability, and operational yield for next-generation process nodes.


What You Will Do

  • AMHS Equipment Ownership: Serve as the technical expert responsible for ensuring optimal performance, reliability, and continuous improvement of the AMHS within the manufacturing environment. Maintain system uptime targets based on organizational goals, through proactive monitoring, preventive maintenance execution, and rapid response to Major Impacts (MI), while simultaneously driving innovation through the evaluation and implementation of new technologies.   Flexibility to participate in an operational on-call rotation to support 24x7 manufacturing escalations.
  • Architect & Deliver Factory Automation Software Integration: Design, integrate, and deploy robust end-to-end software solutions for 300mm wafer transport, reticle management, and automated stocker systems across high-volume cleanroom environments
  • Optimize Distributed Control Systems: Debug, tune, and sustain multi-tier automation platforms—spanning low-level firmware, OS configurations, database interfaces, and real-time scheduling algorithms—to maximize tool availability and eliminate dispatch bottlenecks.
  • Lead New Product Introductions (NPI): Partner cross-functionally with IT Platforms, Networks, Middleware, and Module Equipment Engineering to qualify and integrate new automation capabilities with zero operational disruption to high-volume manufacturing line balance.
  • Own Complex Escalations & Root Cause Analysis: Function as the module technical authority for system excursions; drive structured Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and implement robust permanent corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
  • Champion Fab Data Intelligence: Develop performant SQL queries, Python automation routines, and PowerBI dashboards to monitor fleet health, analyze telemetry logs, and proactively eliminate systemic failures before they manifest as tool downtime.
  • Continuous Improvement: Strive to improve corrective and preventive maintenance overload from maintenance by continually looking for opportunities to improve maintenance through innovative ideas and enhancements. All improvements need to be driven through the DPO and DPG to ensure all sites benefit through these CIPs.
  • Project Management: Complete equipment qualification in accordance with the appropriate qual specifications, contribute to global knowledge revisions based on ongoing learning and lessons learned during system qualifications. Willingness to work in a cleanroom environment (including walking long fab distances and working at heights around automated track superstructures).
  • Execute Global Standards: Collaborate with Intel’s worldwide AMHS engineering network to maintain alignment with Copy Exactly! (CE!) protocols and industry SEMI standards.

Why Join Intel Foundry?

  • Direct Impact at Global Scale: Your code directly governs real-time wafer movement and operational KPIs across one of the most sophisticated semiconductor manufacturing ecosystems on earth.
  • World-Class Automation Ecosystem: Direct, hands-on access to multi-million-dollar automated storage, overhead transport (OHT), and robotics infrastructure engineered alongside premier global equipment partners.
  • Accelerated Technical Leadership: Direct mentorship and collaboration with Intel Fellows and Senior Principal Engineers on an accelerated path toward technical distinction.

title: Strategic / Development Industrial Engineer (Senior Individual Contributor)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Foundry Capacity Optimization (FCO) and Strategic Planning organization is seeking a visionary, high-impact Grade 10 Strategic / Development Industrial Engineer to lead the next era of operational transformation across our planning and capacity ecosystems.

As a senior individual contributor reporting directly to the VP/GM of Foundry Capacity Optimization, you will partner closely with Staff Area Managers (AMs), Principal Engineers, and senior FCSP stakeholders to architect and execute a multi-year digital and operational transformation roadmap.

Your charter is clear: radically increase the strategic impact, velocity, and analytical depth of the organization without expanding headcount. You will eliminate manual data manipulation, disparate spreadsheet modeling, and repetitive reconciliation, enabling FCO engineers to focus on solving high-value, complex semiconductor capacity and customer delivery challenges.

Core Responsibilities

1. Transformation Roadmap and Systems Architecture

• Define, architect, and deliver the end-to-end Foundry Capacity Optimization (FCO) Digital Transformation Roadmap, aligning long-range planning (LRP), capacity modeling, tool allocation, and operational execution systems.

• Translate complex foundry operational workflows into automated, scalable, and resilient enterprise system requirements.

• Establish quantifiable efficiency and productivity metrics to track manual labor reduction, cycle-time compression, and decision-velocity improvements across planning cycles.

2. AI, Machine Learning, and Automation Implementation

• Spearhead the adoption of modern Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Generative AI technologies to automate complex decision-support pipelines, including automated tool mismatch identification, capacity balancing, and yield/mix scenario modeling.

• Partner directly with Foundry Automation, Enterprise IT, software development groups, and specialized third-party technology consultants to rapidly prototype, validate, and deploy production-grade solutions.

• Drive the transition from fragmented desktop spreadsheets and static databases to unified, low-latency, automated enterprise planning engines.

3. Data Integration and Elimination of Manual Reconciliation

• Eliminate the time engineers spend manually mapping, transforming, stitching, and reconciling disparate fab, demand, and tool datasets.

• Partner with data engineering and business intelligence teams to establish a robust single source of truth for fab capacity, equipment lines, capital planning, and customer allocations.

• Institutionalize automated exception handling, data anomaly detection, and self-healing data pipelines across critical planning feeds.

4. Industry Benchmarking and External Innovation

• Actively benchmark peer semiconductor foundries and adjacent hyper-capital-intensive industries, including advanced aerospace, automotive, display, and energy, for state-of-the-art planning systems, algorithmic optimization, and operational efficiency methodologies.

• Evaluate commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) platforms versus proprietary internal builds and develop disciplined business cases, ROI models, and technology roadmaps for executive review.

• Bring external best practices into Foundry Capacity Optimization (FCO), fostering a culture of continuous modernization, technological curiosity, and systems thinking.

5. Stakeholder Alignment and Change Leadership

• Function as a trusted technical advisor and thought partner to Staff AMs, Principal Engineers, and executive management.

• Drive operational change management across diverse engineering disciplines, ensuring seamless adoption of new digital tools, automated interfaces, and standardized workflows.

• Mentor and upskill the broader engineering cohort in modern analytical tools, automation scripts, and systems-level problem solving.


Required Skills and Experience

• Proficiency with data analysis and automation tools such as SQL, Python, Excel, business intelligence platforms, or similar technologies.

• Experience developing capacity models, facility layouts, or manufacturing systems.

• Knowledge of supply chain processes, production systems, or factory operations.

• Familiarity with forecasting methodologies and statistical techniques.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Experience within high-volume semiconductor manufacturing, semiconductor foundry operations, or complex wafer fab supply chains, including familiarity with fab toolsets, lithography/etch/thin-film constraints, cycle-time dynamics, and capacity models.

• Familiarity with commercial supply chain/capacity planning suites such as Kinaxis, Anaplan, SAP IBP, and Blue Yonder, as well as modern business intelligence architectures.

• Experience engaging with and directing external technology vendors, systems integrators, and management consultants to execute technology pilots and full-scale rollouts.

• Demonstrated expertise in Lean, Six Sigma, Design for Excellence, or formal Business Process Re-engineering (BPR).

Qualifications:

• Bachelor's/BS degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Research, or a related field.

• 12+ years of experience with a Bachelor's degree, 8+ years with a Master's degree, or 6+ years with a PhD in a relevant domain.

We invite you to bring your expertise, vision, and creativity to make a meaningful impact on Intel's manufacturing future. Join us in shaping the next generation of technology solutions.

You will work across process development, device engineering, product engineering, design technology co-optimization (DTCO), and foundry customer teams to ensure memory technologies meet quality, reliability, and technology readiness objectives.
