title: Process Integration Development Engineer - Defect Metrology
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.

Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel

At Intel's Logic Technology Development (LTD) we have continued to extend Moore's law to be world leaders in computing technology. To achieve the necessary scaling of our semiconductor manufacturing process, we have led the industry in developing enhancements such as strained silicon for carrier transport enhancement, high-k metal gates, and FINFETs. LTD has been at the center of every new development that has kept Moore's Law moving forward. Defect Metrology plays a key role in the development of every new silicon process development. Our analysis builds the plan that allows LTD to take technology from the research phase to the high-volume manufacturing phase while maintaining high-quality standards. In the MIE organization, we engineer world-class yields on F25 processes by driving defects down to Best-in-Class targets.

As a Defect Metrology engineer, you will be responsible for identifying all defects that impact yield and performance in an advanced silicon process technology. You will characterize the process using cutting-edge metrology tools. With this characterization, you will be responsible for investigating and identifying the root cause owners and developing defect reduction roadmaps to achieve program milestone commitments to our customers. You will then work directly with the process modules and integration teams to drive that roadmap by developing and qualifying process fixes through Model-Based Problem Solving (MBPS). You will also respond to exclusionary baseline shifts in defect trends to isolate the root cause and implement preventative actions consistent with 8D methodology. This role provides an opportunity to influence Intel's future process technologies that will keep Moore's Law moving forward.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Owning a segment of the process to ensure adequate metrology is placed to detect and respond to all yield-limiting defects prior to reaching end-of-line sort
  • Manage data collection strategies, data integrity and quality for the metrology scans in the segment
  • Investigate and respond to exclusionary baseline shifts to ensure segment defect health is restored to capable, demonstrated baseline
  • Develop new recipes and response action plans as part of New Product Introduction (NPI)
  • Provide navigation and leadership to meet Intel's yield objectives, utilizing state-of-the-art metrology tools and test vehicles (QTM, Short Loop, etc.)
  • Organizing and presenting defect summaries to F25, LTD, MDCE engineering teams.
  • Partnering with Intel Integration, Yield, and failure analysis labs to identify root cause for all defect issues.
  • Hold the team and collaborators accountable for quality through Integrated Module Team (IMT) and Focus Team (FT) forums.
  • Work collaboratively as a part of the overall LTD Defect metrology group.
  • Role-model and establish a team culture of trust, collaboration, safety, accountability, and sustaining excellence.
  • Build strong relationships with other LTD teams based on mutual trust and respect.

The Ideal Candidate Must Demonstrate:

  • Strong data analysis and problem-solving skills
  • Team player with flexibility and adaptability to changing business needs
  • Strong ownership mindset and driving closure - see the problem, own the problem
  • Excellent communication and navigation skills to larger audiences
  • Understand and adhere to Intel cultural values such as Customer First, Fearless Innovation, Results Driven, One Intel, Integrity, Quality, Inclusion

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. Experience would be obtained through a combination of prior education level classes, and current level school classes, projects, research, and relevant previous job and internship experience.

Minimum qualifications:


  • Must possess a Master's degree with 3+ years of experience, or PhD with 1+ years of experience in Computer Science, Physics, Material Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear engineering, Optics, or Chemistry (with focus on hands on experimental research)
  • Must have at least 1+ years of experience with each of the following:
    • Experimental research - designing and conducting experiments, operating equipment (characterization, fabrication, synthesis), analyzing statistical data
    • Materials characterization (SEM, TEM, etc.), materials fabrication, synthesis, metrology, statistical or data analysis (MATLAB, Excel, JMP, etc.)
    • Semiconductor processing fundamentals (lithography, wet etch, dry etch, chemical and/or mechanical polishing, etc.), semiconductor and/or transistor device physics, and design of experiments.
    • Complex problem-solving methodologies - root cause analysis, model-based problem solving (MBPS), 5 Why, Fishbone, etc.

Preferred qualifications:


At least 1+ years’ experience with one or more of the following:

  • Defect metrology, defect improvement, yield improvement, or process integration
  • Demonstrate experience of Statistical Process Control (SPC), or Design of Experiments (DOE) principles
  • Expertise on semiconductor physics or semiconductor processing
  • Expertise with defect metrology tools such as brightfield, darkfield, or voltage contrast (VC)

We welcome motivated professionals to bring their expertise and enthusiasm to Intel, where you will have the opportunity to grow your career while helping to shape the future of technology in a collaborative and forward-thinking environment. Shape the Future of Intel Foundry

Are you passionate about connecting strategy, operations, technology, and customer success? Do you thrive in complex environments where collaboration, innovation, and execution drive business outcomes?

title: Central Document Control Manager
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
Join Intel Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS) in building the world's largest semiconductor manufacturing facilities across the globe. As a Construction Central Document Control Manager, you will play a pivotal role in executing a new document control and records management strategy, ensuring consistent, efficient document control processes across all Intel Foundry construction projects. You will own the standards, operating model and oversight required to ensure project and business records are complete, secure, compliant and retrievable throughout their lifecycle.

Business Group
Within the Foundry Construction and Sourcing (FCS) organization in Intel Foundry, the FCS Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) team operates to ensure that Intel Foundry compliantly operates free from construction and supply risk disruption. We do this by relentlessly delivering agile and reliable oversight with an Intel Foundry governance, risk, and compliance framework that minimizes foundry risks and business impacts for our customers. Within the FCS GRC team, the Central Document Control Manager governs the FCS enterprise document and records management strategy, enabling compliant, efficient and scalable information management across FCS.

This individual will play a critical, forward-looking role in modernizing document control and records management practices across all sites, including executing a new, holistic cross-FCS records management strategy and evaluating processes for efficiency, standardization, automation and appropriate use of AI-enabled capabilities. This role will closely partner with construction project teams, project controls teams, design teams, sourcing teams, CW workgroups and other stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

  • Owns and governs the centralized enterprise document control framework used across all FCS Construction projects.
  • Executes the updated global FCS Construction Document Control and Records Management strategy, operationalizing centralized improvements for process simplification, automation, AI enablement, Project File Index (PFI) modernization and operating model optimization.
  • Streamlines, maintains and enforces Construction Document Control standards, processes and controls to ensure consistent execution by project teams and Local Document Control resources.
  • Ensures the Construction Document Control system protects Intel intellectual property, supports contractual, legal, audit and claims defense requirements, maintains complete, accurate and retrievable project records and serves as the single source of truth for project documentation.
  • Defines, maintains and governs the standard Project File Index (PFI), approving updates, deviations or exceptions, ensuring contractual deliverables are properly stored and searchable in accordance with PFI requirements and overseeing deployment of the PFI structure within approved project platforms (e.g., BIM360).
  • Manages Construction Document Control platform administration and access governance, overseeing implementation of permissions and role alignment by Local Document Control teams and ensuring access audits are conducted in accordance with Intel policy.
  • Ensures contractual deliverables are transmitted through Intel Document Control in accordance with contract requirements.
  • Governs FCS records management practices to support traceability, audit readiness and claims defense.
  • Partners with Program and Project Managers to align Construction Document Control services with project needs, recommending opportunities for reducing document control cost footprint across sites.
  • Manage Construction Document Control requirements from project initiation through project closeout, ensuring document control standards are applied consistently throughout projects at all sites and aligned with Intel Records Retention Policy.
  • Ability to lead cross-functional teams and align stakeholders in matrixed organizations.

Qualifications:

Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Business, Engineering, Information Management or related field.
  • 4+ years of experience in document control, records management, or information governance across multi-site or enterprise environments.
  • Experience with process improvements and operational efficiencies through standardization, automation, AI or digital transformation.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in the following:

  • Business processes and construction or engineering environments.
    Management platforms such as Hexagon SDx, BIM360 / ACC, or equivalent systems.
  • Legal, audit or claims-driven document requirements.
    Recordkeeping and retention environments.
  • Semiconductor construction and progressive build practices in advanced manufacturing facilities.
  • Compliance or Governance.

title: Process Integration Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.


Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel

At Intel's Logic Technology Development (LTD) we have continued to extend Moore's law to be world leaders in computing technology. To achieve the necessary scaling of our semiconductor manufacturing process, we have led the industry in developing enhancements such as strained silicon for carrier transport enhancement, high-k metal gates, and FINFETs. LTD has been at the center of every new development that has kept Moore's Law moving forward. TMI Integration plays a key role in the development of every new silicon process development. Our analysis builds the plan that allows LTD to take technology from the research phase to the high-volume manufacturing phase while maintaining high-quality standards. In the MIE organization, we engineer world-class yields on D1 processes by driving critical Fab and E-Test parameters to Best-in-Class targets. As a TMI Integration engineer, you will be responsible for identifying all the process parameters that impact yield and performance in an advanced silicon process technology. You will characterize the process using cutting-edge metrology tools. With this characterization, you will be responsible for creating a yield cliff parameter improvement roadmap. You will then work directly with modules and TD integration to drive that roadmap by developing and qualifying process fixes. This role provides an opportunity to influence Intel's future process technologies that will keep Moore's Law moving forward. 

Responsibilities will include but will not be limited to:

title: Supply Chain Planning and Operations (SCPO) AI Lead
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Supply Chain Planning Operations (SCPO) organization is seeking an AI Software Architect to serve as the SCPO AI Lead.

This is a founding technical leadership role embedded within supply planning operations. The role will define and execute the AI strategy for connecting planning and execution data, detecting emerging supply, flagging demand and product risks, and enabling planners and leaders to act on trusted, explainable insights.

The Supply Chain Planning Operations (SCPO) AI Lead will architect and build the intelligent stitching and alerting layer across Plan of Record (POR), Long Range Planning (LRP), Sales and Operations Planning (SnOP), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and other supply chain related data.


The role will convert fragmented data from multiple sources and manual reconciliation into production capabilities that continuously monitor supply execution, identify likely failures, explain the drivers, and guide timely intervention.


The successful candidate will deliver production solutions used in operational decisions, work directly with planners, and establish the technical foundation and engineering practices for SCPO. Please note that this is not a research-only or advisory role.

The SCPO AI Lead is responsible for, but not limited to:


  • Define the SCPO AI and data intelligence strategy, architecture, roadmap, and standards in alignment with supply-chain priorities and measurable business outcomes.
  • Architect and operationalize a trusted data stitching layer across POR, LRP, SnOP, ERP, and other planning data sources, including lineage, controls, reconciliation, and data-quality monitoring and governance.
  • Develop production machine-learning and AI capabilities for time-series analysis, anomaly detection, root-cause identification, supply-risk sensing, and early warning of execution failures.
  • Integrate AI outputs with enterprise planning systems and operational workflows using reliable APIs, data pipelines, monitoring, access controls, and override mechanisms.
  • Build agentic workflows that automate recurring analyses, evidence gathering, exception triage, and narrative generation while maintaining human-in-the-loop controls, auditability, and appropriate governance.
  • Develop scenario and sensitivity capabilities that evaluate supply disruptions, demand changes, yield shifts, capacity reallocations, material constraints, and other operational decisions across planning horizons.
  • Create explainable alerts and decision-support experiences that show what changed, why it matters, the level of confidence, and the recommended next action.
  • Map the planning-system ecosystem, data flows, manual intervention points, process breakpoints, dependencies, and failure modes; prioritize automation and guardrails based on business risk and value.
  • Partner with supply planning, demand planning, manufacturing, foundry, procurement, finance, data engineering, information technology, and business teams to translate operational problems into scalable technical solutions.
  • Establish MLOps and software-engineering practices for model versioning, testing, deployment, observability, retraining, documentation, security, and responsible AI governance.
  • Communicate technical findings, model limitations, risk signals, architecture decisions, and business recommendations clearly to planners, technical partners, senior managers, and executives.
  • Operate with intellectual rigor in ambiguous environments where data, systems, and requirements are incomplete or evolving.
  • Commitment to explainability, responsible AI, human oversight, security, and governance for decisions with material financial or operational consequences.

Initial success measures include:


  • Within 90 days: define the target stitching architecture, data ownership model, prioritized use-case roadmap, and deploy an initial live reconciliation capability.
  • Within 6 months: deploy an explainable alert that detects a material supply-execution risk early enough to support intervention.
  • Within 12 months: demonstrate sustained planner adoption, measurable reduction in manual reconciliation, and operational decisions informed by trusted alerts and scenarios.

The ideal candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:


  • Advanced communication skills to tailor complex technical content for engineering, planning, and executive audiences.
  • Tolerance for responsible experimentation, including disciplined learning from approaches that do not succeed.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications, you must possess the minimum qualifications below to be initially considered for this position.


  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Industrial Engineering, Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.
  • 8+ years of experience in:

    • Machine-learning engineering, AI engineering, data science, data engineering, optimization, or related technical roles, including leadership of complex production deployments.
    • Architecting, deploying, and operating machine-learning solutions in production on complex enterprise data.
    • Programming experience in Python and strong SQL skills, with practical experience in modern machine-learning, data-processing, and software-engineering frameworks.
    • Designing data pipelines, APIs, and integrations across enterprise applications, data platforms, and operational systems.
    • Leading cross-functional technical work and influencing architecture and delivery decisions without relying solely on direct authority.

This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.


Preferred Qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.


  • Master's degree in relevant technical or quantitative discipline.
  • Experience in semiconductors, electronics, or comparable high-volume manufacturing environments, including wafer starts and outs, yield, substrate and long-lead materials, new-product-introduction gates, and capacity commitments.
  • Working knowledge of supply planning, demand planning, SnOP or integrated business planning, capacity planning, inventory optimization, procurement, and order management.
  • Experience with enterprise planning and manufacturing platforms such as SAP, Kinaxis Rapid Response, Oracle, manufacturing execution systems, or equivalent technologies.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud data and AI platforms, distributed data processing, and enterprise-grade observability and security.
  • Experience with large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic frameworks, and evaluation and governance of generative AI solutions.
  • Experience building interactive scenario-modeling or decision-support applications used by operational teams.
  • Experience hiring, mentoring, and technically leading AI, machine-learning, or data-engineering talent in a new or rapidly scaling capability.
  • APICS CPIM, CSCP, or equivalent supply-chain certification.

title: Silicon Domain Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the Role and Team The AI Silicon Architecture and Performance Engineering team is responsible for developing and maintaining performance models that enable architecture exploration, design evaluation, scalability analysis, and performance projection for next-generation AI silicon products. These models are a critical component of the product development process, providing early visibility into architectural tradeoffs, bottlenecks, and optimization opportunities long before silicon availability. We are seeking a highly experienced and motivated engineer to drive AI silicon performance modeling, validation, architectural analysis, and stakeholder engagement activities. The candidate will work closely with architects, performance stimulus generation teams, silicon design teams, and product stakeholders to evaluate and optimize key AI silicon subsystems that determine overall platform scalability and performance. The role focuses on performance modeling and analysis of AI SoC communication fabrics, memory subsystems, scale-up and scale-out interconnects, host-device memory paths, and end-to-end data movement infrastructure. The successful candidate will leverage SystemC/TLM-based modeling methodologies to generate actionable insights that directly influence architecture and product decisions. This position requires a unique combination of software development expertise, architecture understanding, analytical problem solving, and cross-functional technical leadership. The engineer will be expected to independently drive complex technical initiatives while serving as a trusted performance expert across multiple organizations. ________________________________________ Key Responsibilities 1. AI Silicon Performance Model Development • Develop, maintain, and enhance SystemC/TLM-based performance models representing critical AI silicon subsystems. • Drive modeling of key architectural components including: o SoC fabrics and on-chip communication networks o Memory controllers and memory subsystem behavior o Scale-up controllers and fabrics enabling accelerator-to-accelerator communication within a node, tray, or pod o Scale-out controllers and fabrics enabling communication across nodes, racks, and larger AI clusters o Host CPU to accelerator memory paths o Local, host, and remote memory access paths o End-to-end data movement architectures • Implement new architectural features and capabilities based on evolving product requirements. • Improve model fidelity, scalability, maintainability, and simulation performance. • Perform detailed debugging and root-cause analysis of model issues and performance anomalies. • Contribute to the evolution of modeling infrastructure, methodologies, and best practices. ________________________________________ 2. Functional Validation and Model Correlation • Define and execute comprehensive validation strategies to ensure correctness and architectural accuracy of performance models. • Develop validation plans, regression suites, coverage methodologies, and quality metrics. • Correlate modeled behavior against architectural expectations, reference simulations, performance projections, and available hardware measurements. • Investigate and resolve discrepancies between expected and observed behavior. • Establish robust validation frameworks that improve stakeholder confidence in model-generated performance projections. • Continuously improve validation methodologies and model quality. ________________________________________ 3. AI Silicon Performance Characterization and Architectural Analysis • Design and execute performance studies covering a wide range of workloads, traffic patterns, and system configurations. • Analyze performance of communication fabrics, memory systems, and data movement paths under representative AI workloads. • Evaluate bandwidth utilization, latency characteristics, congestion behavior, traffic distribution, buffering efficiency, and resource utilization. • Characterize interactions across local memory, host memory, and remote memory domains. • Assess scalability of scale-up and scale-out architectures across increasingly larger deployment footprints. • Identify performance bottlenecks and quantify their impact on overall system throughput and efficiency. • Conduct architectural tradeoff studies to evaluate alternative design approaches. • Provide performance-driven recommendations that influence architecture and product decisions. ________________________________________ 4. Performance Data Generation, Analytics and Visualization • Develop frameworks and methodologies for large-scale performance data generation and analysis. • Create automated workflows for data collection, processing, correlation, and reporting. • Develop performance dashboards and visualization tools that simplify interpretation of complex performance data. • Define and track meaningful performance KPIs and architectural metrics. • Utilize Python-based analysis frameworks to process large datasets and generate actionable insights. • Enable efficient consumption of performance information by architects, designers, and engineering leadership. ________________________________________ 5. Cross-Functional Technical Leadership and Stakeholder Engagement • Partner closely with architecture teams, performance stimulus generation teams, silicon design teams, and product stakeholders. • Drive technical discussions related to performance methodology, architectural assumptions, workload behavior, scalability analysis, and bottleneck identification. • Review architectural proposals and provide performance-driven feedback. • Present performance studies, technical findings, and architectural recommendations to engineering leadership. • Influence product and architecture decisions through data-backed analysis and sound engineering judgment. • Act as a key technical bridge between architecture, modeling, and performance analysis organizations. ________________________________________ 6. Methodology Development and Team Growth • Drive improvements in modeling methodologies, simulation efficiency, and analysis workflows. • Identify opportunities for automation across modeling, validation, performance analysis, and reporting activities. • Establish best practices for model quality, performance characterization, and architectural analysis. • Contribute to technical mentoring and knowledge sharing across the team. • Support the development of junior engineers and future team growth initiatives. • Help cultivate a culture of technical excellence and continuous improvement.

Technical Experience • 15+ years of industry experience in performance modeling, AI silicon architecture, SoC architecture, computer architecture, performance engineering, or related domains. • Strong software development experience in C++. • Working proficiency in Python for automation, performance analysis, data processing, and visualization. • Hands-on experience with SystemC and Transaction-Level Modeling (TLM) methodologies. • Experience developing or validating performance models for AI accelerators, SoCs, CPUs, GPUs, networking products, or complex hardware systems. • Strong understanding of: o SoC architecture o Memory subsystem architecture o Memory controllers o Cache hierarchies o Data movement architectures o On-chip communication fabrics and NoC concepts o High-speed interconnects o Scale-up and scale-out communication architectures o Performance bottleneck analysis o Latency and bandwidth characterization • Experience performing architectural tradeoff analysis and performance characterization studies. • Experience working with large performance datasets and deriving meaningful engineering insights. title: AI SW Engineering Student
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

About the team
Scale the models everyone is talking about.
Today's models span hundreds of GPUs, and the network between them decides whether a training run takes a week or a month.

As AI models became larger and more complicated, a performant graph mode and efficient scaling solution became a key aspect of the SW solution.

Our team builds that layer. We own the Intel oneAPI Collective Communications Library (oneCCL) and develop the software for multiple generations of Intel AI GPUs, for training and inference.



What you'll do:

  • You'll be a member of the team, working on the library that moves data between GPUs in some of the largest AI training jobs running on Intel hardware.
  • Develop features in the core library: design and implement parts of the C++/SYCL code that run on the GPU, from the first design through code review to the release.
  • Push performance: profile communication across many GPUs, find the bottlenecks and make the fixes that cut the time it takes to train AI models.
  • Solve hard bugs: track down concurrency, synchronization and memory issues in a distributed system that runs across many GPUs at once.
  • Shape how the team builds software: improve the build system, CI pipelines and developer tooling the whole team depends on every day.
  • Learn to use AI tools as part of the development process.

What you'll get:

  • Hands-on work with code that runs in production and is open source.
  • A mentor from the team and regular one-on-one guidance.
  • Experience with high-performance computing and AI infrastructure, a fast-growing field.

Qualifications:

Required:

  • B.Sc. or M.Sc. student in Computer Science, Computer/Electrical Engineering or a related field.
  • Good working knowledge of C++from courses or personal projects.
  • Solid basics in data structures and algorithms.
  • Comfortable with, or eager to learn, working in Linux and on the command line.
  • Curious, willing to ask questions, and able to learn new things on your own.

Nice to have:

  • A course or project in parallel programming, operating systems or computer architecture.

You don't need prior industry experience. We care more about how you think and learn than about what you already know.

Work on Intel 14A and explore the engineering challenges behind leading-edge Gate-All-Around (GAA) transistor technology. Join Intel’s Technology Development Foundry Engineering team and contribute to advanced semiconductor process development at the intersection of process integration, device performance, yield, and product execution.

As an intern, you will own a focused technical project with practical engineering impact, supported by experienced technical mentors. What You Will Work On

title: Process and Equipment Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Process and Equipment Engineer specializing in Wafer Laser and Saw Singulation Technologies, you will serve as the technical owner responsible for driving the performance, capability, and stability of advanced wafer singulation processes within our high-volume semiconductor manufacturing environment. In this role, you will leverage your expertise in precision laser-material interaction, wafer dicing, laser ablation, and singulation technologies to solve complex process and equipment challenges, optimize manufacturing performance, and implement innovative solutions that enable next-generation semiconductor products.

Your hands-on contributions will directly impact factory yield, quality, equipment uptime, Manufacturing Availability (MA), cost competitiveness, and process robustness. You will play a critical role in supporting Intel's advanced packaging, NPI and wafer manufacturing roadmap through the deployment of cutting-edge laser and sawing technologies.

Business group:
As part of Intel Wafer Packaging Manufacturing (WPM), you will join a globally recognized organization at the forefront of semiconductor manufacturing and advanced packaging technologies. Our organization develops and deploys innovative wafer processing, laser manufacturing, and singulation solutions that enable Intel's next-generation computing platforms.
The Wafer Laser Ablation and Saw Engineering team plays a critical role in delivering high-yield, high-quality wafer singulation processes through the integration of advanced laser processing, precision sawing, automation, data analytics, and AI-driven manufacturing solutions. We continuously push the boundaries of wafer processing capability to meet increasingly demanding product requirements across advanced packaging and silicon technologies.
Working within a highly collaborative environment, you will partner with global factory networks, technology development teams, virtual factories, equipment suppliers, and manufacturing stakeholders to develop breakthrough solutions that improve yield, quality, cost, and manufacturing scalability. This role offers unique opportunities to influence future technology roadmaps while supporting Intel's mission to create world-changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

Key Responsibilities:
Process Optimization - Own and optimize laser ablation and wafer saw process parameters to achieve best-in-class yield, quality, and throughput.
Yield Improvement - Drive systematic defect reduction initiatives targeting burrs, chipping, cracking, kerf quality, and recast.
Equipment Engineering - Lead complex troubleshooting and reliability improvements for laser ablation, laser dicing, and wafer saw equipment.
Maintenance Strategy - Develop and execute preventive and corrective maintenance plans to maximize equipment uptime and MA.
Data Analytics - Utilize SPC, DOE, FMEA,JMP and advanced analytics to identify root causes of process variation and equipment failures.
Automation and AI Solutions - Develop and deploy Python/Co-pilot/Github/ Gemini- and AI-based solutions for defect monitoring, predictive maintenance, and process optimization.
Technology Development - Collaborate with TD teams to evaluate, develop, and qualify next-generation laser processing and singulation technologies.
New Product Introduction (NPI) - Support process qualification, technology transfer, and high-volume manufacturing ramp for new products.
Cross-Functional Collaboration - Partner with upstream and downstream process owners to improve end-to-end manufacturing performance.
Supplier Engagement - Work closely with equipment vendors to implement hardware upgrades, software enhancements, and productivity improvements.
Documentation and Standards - Develop and standardize SOPs, troubleshooting guides, BKMs, and engineering documentation.
Technical Leadership - Present technical findings, project updates, and business impact assessments to factory stakeholders and leadership teams.
Manufacturing Excellence - Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on yield, quality, cost reduction, and cycle-time optimization.
Safety and Compliance - Ensure compliance with Intel safety, quality, and environmental requirements while promoting a strong safety culture.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Materials Engineering, Physics, or a related engineering discipline.

• Fresh graduates with strong technical aptitude, problem-solving skills, and a passion for semiconductor manufacturing are encouraged to apply.

• 0-1 year experience in relevant industry.


Preferred Qualification:

• More than 2 years in relevant industry.

• Experience in semiconductor manufacturing, particularly in wafer singulation, laser ablation, laser dicing, stealth dicing, wafer saw, Die Preparation, or advanced packaging processes, will be an added advantage.

• Strong understanding of laser-material interaction, optics, motion control systems, vision alignment systems, and precision manufacturing technologies is highly desirable.

• Knowledge of Statistical Process Control (SPC), statistical data analysis, and structured problem-solving methodologies; experience with Design of Experiments (DOE), Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) will be an added advantage.

• Experience with data analytics, automation, and programming tools such as Python, JMP, SQL, Power BI, or AI-based manufacturing applications will be an added advantage.

• Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot technical challenges using a structured and data-driven approach.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to work independently and in a team-based environment.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams.

• Self-motivated, results-oriented, and passionate about continuous improvement, innovation, and cost reduction.

• Willingness to work in a cleanroom manufacturing environment and support factory operations as required.

title: Intel Foundry Product Yield Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.


Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel 


As a Yield Development Engineer, you will be at the forefront of advancing Intel's cutting-edge process technologies within our Logic Technology Development (LTD) organization. This pivotal role involves identifying root cause yield limiters and driving solutions that enhance manufacturability and yield across technology nodes. You will work within a dynamic, fast-paced environment to ensure the successful introduction of new products, process improvements, and robust methodologies to meet manufacturing goals. Your expertise will directly contribute to Intel's ability to deliver world-class semiconductor solutions and advance the future of computing.


About Intel Foundry


At Intel, the Foundry Technology Development (TD) unit is the driving force behind Moore's Law, enabling us to create groundbreaking technology that enriches lives globally. With over 15,000 dedicated employees, Foundry TD spearheads innovative research, develops next-generation processes and packaging technologies, and manages high-volume manufacturing in state-of-the-art facilities. Within Intel Foundry TD, our Logic Technology Development (LTD) organization is at the forefront of creating and refining each process technology node, paving the way for tomorrow's computing solutions.


Your responsibilities as a Product Yield Development Engineer will include but not be limited to:

  • Develop methods, processes, and systems to consolidate and analyze diverse big data sources for defect mode understanding and yield modeling.
  • Perform statistical analysis, create visualizations, and construct process development roadmaps that drive technology yield milestones.
  • Extract insights from structured and unstructured data using advanced statistics, machine learning, and coding techniques.
  • Organize, interpret, and structure insights from fab process, defect, and electrical data while identifying anomalies to drive process changes for yield enhancement.
  • Develop multivariate algorithms and tools to identify root cause yield limiters and recommend process changes for yield improvement.
  • Collaborate with design teams to resolve yield issues, ensuring manufacturability across process and product specifications before ramping production.
  • Execute new product introductions, enable design-technology co-optimization, and participate in design of experiments with factory task forces.
  • Develop measurement recipes for rapid feedback on product integrity and address issues impacting yield or product quality.
  • Create and harden systems capable of meeting operational needs for leading-edge logic nodes, working with equipment vendors and internal collaborators.
  • Develop AI/ML applications and computational tools to bridge the gap between design and manufacturing, improve design efficiency, and reduce debug time.
  • Document technical procedures, train colleagues, and debug equipment, software, and procedural failures in production environments when required.

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates Experience listed below would be obtained through a combination of your schoolwork, classes, research and/or relevant previous job and/or internship experiences.


Minimum qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in semiconductor science-related STEM degree in engineering, physical science, computer science, or related field with 2+ years of experience in advanced semiconductor devices and process flow; OR
  • Master’s degree in semiconductor science-related STEM degree in engineering, physical science, computer science, or related field with 4+ years of experience in advanced semiconductor devices and process flow.

Preferred qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience with data analysis systems and software tools
  • 2+ years of experience in yield projection with EOL signals and in line parameters
  • Project/program management experience with strong self-initiative and self-learning capabilities.
  • Proven track record of working across organizations through matrix structures to accomplish strategic objectives with conflicting priorities.

Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. title: Product Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

  • Drives and develops testability and manufacturability of integrated circuits from the component feasibility stage through production ramp.
  • Contributes to design, development, and validation of testability circuits, test flows, and methodologies for new products through evaluation, development, and debug of complex test methods.
  • Interfaces with process development, fab, factory, assembly, quality and reliability, and manufacturing groups to enable postsilicon HVM ramp.
  • Evaluates new designs on automatic test equipment (ATE) and works with the design, DFx, and product development teams to debug functionality and performance issues to root cause. Performs ATE device characterization, utilizes that data to define datasheet specifications and performs yield analysis.
  • Collaborates with designers to drive design for test/debug/manufacturing (DFT/DFD/DFM) features enabling efficient production testing of new products.
  • Develops and debugs complex software programs to convert design validation vectors and drive complex test equipment. Creates and tests validation and production test hardware solutions.
  • Tests, validates, modifies, and redesigns circuits to guarantee component margin to specification.
  • Analyzes and evaluates component specification versus performance to ensure optimal match of component requirements with production equipment capability with specific emphasis on yield analysis and bin split capability.
  • Ensures manufacturability over process and product design through thorough analysis of process and spec corners and works with design to resolve yield issues before manufacturing ramp.
  • Drives test time reduction through analysis of fallout data versus test time for various IPs to balance and drive overall product cost optimizations.
  • Analyzes early customer returns with emphasis on driving test hole closure activities.
  • Creates and applies concepts for optimizing component production relative to both quality and cost constraints.
  • Leads and drives manufacturing readiness from fab, assembly, and test factory to support engineering sample and customer sample generation (ES milestones), wafer start planning, product qual execution strategy and capacity analysis, and assembly and test site certification activities.
  • Works with fab, assembly, and test factory partners and planners to support production ramp.
  • May also manage execution of new product introductions in the fab, fab process targeting, product/process optimizations, and participate in factory task forces to bring product perspective and respond to product issues.
  • Optimizes product supply through data analysis of postsilicon binsplit, die level cherry pick (DLCP), and optimize sort/test content and yield downstream through data analysis.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications  

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with 0-1 years of hands-on experience in the domain, showcasing skills gained through internships, academic projects, coursework, or hands-on training.  
  • OR a Master’s degree in a relevant field with no prior professional experience.  
  • Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, C++, or PERL.  
  • Basic knowledge of data analysis tools like JMP, Power BI, SQL, and Excel.  
  • Understanding of electronics components and circuit analysis.  

Preferred Qualifications  

  • Experience with automated test equipment (ATE) and test program development.  
  • Strong problem-solving and prioritization skills with an independent and inquisitive mindset.  
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.  
  • A willingness to learn and passion for innovation in manufacturing engineering.  
  • Familiarity with machine learning pipelines or yield improvement practices is a plus.  

Be part of a dynamic and collaborative team working at the forefront of technology. Apply your skills to solve complex challenges and help shape the future of Intel’s products.

descriptionHtml:

As a CPU HVM Functional-Test Verification Engineer, you will be part of the DFT team focusing on validating DFT for manufacturing functional testing and delivering functional test content for the manufacturing of Intel's next generation CPU IP designs. title: Memory Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Role Overview
You will be partnering with and leveraging domain experts across various areas of technology development, EDA vendors and product design teams to develop and deliver high-quality industry-leading memory technology collaterals and to drive innovations that enable next generation high-performance, high-density, low-power embedded memory designs on Intel's advanced CMOS process technologies.


Business Group

The Advanced Design (AD) team is part of Intel’s larger Design Technology Platform (DTP) Organization and is focused on pathfinding and development of advanced memory technology.  These circuits enable best-in-class memory collateral, IP and innovative product design across all generations of Intel process technology.  At Intel, DTP is one of the key pillars enabling Intel to deliver winning products in the marketplace. Your work will directly enable Intel’s internal and external customers to get to the market faster with products that include high-performance, high-density, low-power memory at the leading edge of the technology curve and implemented in Intel’s advanced CMOS process technologies.  


In this position your responsibilities will include, but may not be limited to:


  • Define, develop, and optimize advanced memory bitcells, array architectures, and peripheral circuits.
  • Lead memory pathfinding and optimize power, performance, and area (PPA) through design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) and product design enablement.
  • Develop and validate memory libraries for PDK enablement across Intel's advanced process technologies.
  • Design memory arrays and IP, develop innovative memory circuits, and execute and validate test chips.

Your contributions will directly enable leading-edge products with high-performance, high-density, low-power memory implemented on Intel's advanced CMOS process technologies.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

  • BA degree with 3 years of experience or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related STEM field with 2+ years of experience OR a PhD with no experience.
  • Experience in customer circuit design, simulation, layout design and verification.
  • Hands-on experience with relevant industry EDA tools and flows for digital and/or analog design and verification, such as Cadence Virtuoso, Synopsys StarRC, and Synopsys HSPICE.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in memory bitcell and circuit design.
  • Experience with advanced CMOS process technologies and device physics.
  • Experience evaluating and balancing power, performance, and area trade-offs.
  • Experience designing, characterizing, and verifying custom memory circuits, such as SRAM, register files, and ROM.

title: Senior Foundry Automation Solutions Architect
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Transform the Future of Semiconductor Manufacturing - Intel is transforming its backend manufacturing network operations toward autonomous, lights-out manufacturing. We are building the next generation of factory automation platforms that enable intelligent, scalable, and highly efficient operations across Intel's global backend manufacturing network.

We are seeking a Senior Foundry Automation Solutions Architect to lead the architecture strategy and technology direction behind this transformation. In this highly visible role, you will define and deliver the software architectures that connect Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), equipment automation, robotics, material handling systems, edge computing, Industrial IoT, and AI-driven decision platforms into a unified factory ecosystem.

Working across engineering, factory operations, technology development, IT, and business leadership teams, you will translate strategic automation objectives into scalable, production-ready solutions that drive measurable improvements in factory performance at global scale.

Success in this role will be measured by tangible business outcomes, including reducing manual factory touchpoints to enable zero-touch operations, improving manufacturing efficiency and quality through the elimination of human-induced variability, increasing equipment utilization and throughput, reducing cycle times and operational bottlenecks, improving system availability and resilience, accelerating deployment of new automation capabilities, and establishing reusable architecture standards that can be scaled across Intel's manufacturing network.

This is a unique opportunity to define the architectural foundation for Intel's next generation of autonomous factories. The platforms, standards, and automation frameworks you create will directly influence the future of semiconductor manufacturing and help establish industry-leading operational excellence across Intel's global Assembly and Test operations.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Define architecture strategy, standards, and reference designs for factory automation platforms.
  • Lead the design of scalable, highly available, and mission-critical solutions spanning MES, AMHS, robotics, equipment automation, and Industrial IoT.
  • Drive technology evaluation and pathfinding, technical assessments, and adoption of emerging technologies including AI/ML, edge computing, and intelligent automation.
  • Establish interoperability frameworks, integration patterns, and communication standards across manufacturing systems.
  • Provide technical leadership and architectural governance across multiple programs and factory sites.
  • Partner with senior stakeholders to align technology investments with business priorities and manufacturing objectives.
  • Mentor engineers and architects while elevating architectural excellence across the organization.

Impact
Success in this role will be measured by:

  • Accelerating Intel's journey toward autonomous and lights-out manufacturing.
  • Reducing manual factory touchpoints and enabling zero-touch operations.
  • Improving equipment utilization, throughput, cycle time, quality, and operational resilience.
  • Accelerating deployment of new automation capabilities and technology transfers.
  • Establishing scalable architecture standards and reusable platforms across Intel's manufacturing network.
  • Enabling sustainable improvements in factory performance and operational excellence.

Qualifications:

We're looking for a senior technology leader who combines deep software architecture expertise with a passion for industrial automation and large-scale operational transformation.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of experience designing and delivering complex distributed software systems.
  • 5+ years in a Lead Architect, Principal Engineer, Solutions Architect, Systems Architect, or equivalent technical leadership role.
  • Expertise in distributed systems, event-driven architectures, microservices, messaging platforms, and highly available systems.
  • Experience with cloud-native, edge, or hybrid architectures for mission-critical environments.
  • Strong knowledge of industrial integration standards including SECS/GEM, GEM300, OPC-UA, MQTT, REST, and gRPC.
  • Proven ability to drive technical strategy and influence cross-functional and executive stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Semiconductor manufacturing, Assembly and Test, wafer fabrication, or advanced manufacturing automation experience.
  • Experience leading lights-out or autonomous factory initiatives.
  • Knowledge of MES, scheduling, dispatching, robotics, AMHS, AGV, or AMR solutions.
  • Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, k3s, Industrial IoT, and edge computing platforms.
  • Familiarity with Kafka, AI/ML-enabled automation, and OT cybersecurity.
  • Candidates from advanced manufacturing, robotics, logistics automation, and Industry 4.0 environments are encouraged to apply.

Join us in defining the architecture and technology foundation for Intel's next generation of autonomous factories.

In this job you are required to work with cross functional team. You are expected to lead a new site start up and logistics supplier integration.

title: Process Integration Development Engineer - TD Defect Metrology
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Embark with us on a journey of growth and transformation as we create exceptionally engineered technology and bring AI everywhere. As a valued team member, your adaptability and attention to detail will contribute to our drive for results and relentless pursuit of quality, ensuring we meet our customers' needs with precision.


Join us and build on our legacy of innovation and collaboration as we deliver world‑changing technology that improves the life of every person on the planet.


Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel


As a Process Integration Development Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in advancing semiconductor technology by designing, executing, and analyzing experiments to enhance process performance. Using cutting-edge materials and equipment, you will develop integrated solutions to meet quality, reliability, and manufacturability requirements, driving technology transfer to high-volume manufacturing. Your work will directly contribute to optimizing outputs and shaping Intel's future innovations.


Joining Intel Foundry's Logic Technology Development (LTD), you will be part of a team focused on driving advancements in silicon process technology. LTD is at the forefront of sustaining Moore's Law by enabling world-class semiconductor manufacturing. The group collaborates across engineering disciplines to develop processes that meet Intel's high standards for yield, performance, and reliability, ensuring the delivery of groundbreaking technology to our customers.


Your responsibilities may include but not limited to:


  • Plan and execute experiments to fully characterize processes throughout the development cycle and improve product performance.
  • Develop and qualify materials and equipment to meet reliability, cost, and manufacturability requirements.
  • Conduct feasibility studies and identify process solutions in collaboration with product and module engineering teams.
  • Leverage big data analysis to identify and resolve process design weaknesses or manufacturing tool issues.
  • Lead new product qualifications and ensure seamless technology transfers to high-volume manufacturing using the Copy Exactly methodology.
  • Collaborate with development teams and material suppliers to align processes with technology roadmaps.
  • Organize and present process solutions to engineering teams to address customer requests or resolve issues.

Qualifications:

Candidates must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. The experience listed below may be obtained through schoolwork, classes and project work, internships, military training, and/or work experience.


Minimum Qualifications:


  • Ph.D. in Computer Science, Physics, Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Optics, Chemistry, or a related field; OR
  • Master's degree in the aforementioned fields with 4+ years of engineering industry experience.
  • Experience in materials characterization techniques such as SEM, TEM, Spectroscopy or other metrology tools.
  • Experience with semiconductor processing fundamentals, including lithography, etching, polishing, chemical/physical reactions, or device physics.
  • Experience in statistical or data analysis tools like MATLAB, JMP, or Excel, and familiarity with design of experiments (DOE) principles.

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Proven experience in defect reduction or process integration within semiconductor manufacturing.
  • Knowledge of Statistical Process Control (SPC) methods or advanced process controls (APC).
  • Expertise in advanced transistor device structures and architectures, including fabrication processes.
  • Proficiency in scripting languages (e.g., Python, Perl) or programming languages (e.g., SQL, C++).
  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset to foster trust and partnerships across engineering teams.

Take advantage of this opportunity to join Intel and shape the future of engineering. Apply today to be part of a team that drives industry-leading innovation and transformation.

title: Dedicated Emergency Responder Team
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Role and Impact
As a Manufacturing Safety Technician, you will play a critical role in ensuring the safety and readiness of Intel's factory operations. You will be responsible for responding promptly to safety incidents and emergencies, conducting thorough investigations, and providing technical guidance on emergency response protocols. Your work will directly contribute to a safer, more efficient manufacturing environment, ensuring compliance with safety standards and fostering continuous improvement across the site.

Business group
Intel Foundry is at the forefront of innovation, enabling cutting-edge manufacturing and advancing Intel's mission to create world-changing technology. The team is dedicated to supporting factory operations by embedding safety and emergency response expertise across the site. Joining this group provides an opportunity to work in a collaborative environment committed to operational excellence and employee well-being.

Key Responsibilities
- Respond promptly to safety incidents, accidents, and alarms, including hazardous material leaks, odors, spills, and medical concerns.
- Investigate incidents to determine root causes and recommend corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
- Document all safety reports, incidents, and activities occurring during shifts, maintaining accurate and detailed records.
- Conduct regular site walkthroughs to identify potential hazards and ensure a physical presence across the factory.
- Collaborate with project teams to ensure safety compliance during equipment installations, startups, and retirements.
- Provide technical expertise on emergency response protocols and actively participate in planning safety initiatives.
- Lead, mentor, and coach shift safety and emergency response teams, ensuring alignment with safety goals and readiness for emergencies.
- Develop and deliver safety training sessions, drills, and scenario updates to team members as needed.
- Perform preventative maintenance and upgrades on safety equipment, supplies, and emergency resources to ensure optimal functionality.
- Monitor and maintain inventory levels of safety equipment and emergency supplies, ensuring their availability when needed.
- Partner with other departments to implement safety initiatives and drive continuous improvement measures.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in a relevant field with 2+ years of hands-on experience in safety, emergency response, or a related domain OR an Associate degree in a relevant field with 3-6 years of applicable experience.
- Proficiency in incident investigation procedures, root cause analysis, and safety documentation.
- Familiarity with safety standards, regulations, and protocols, including Hazardous Production Materials.
- Experience conducting safety audits, inspections, or walkthroughs in manufacturing environments.
- Technical aptitude for maintaining and performing preventative maintenance on safety equipment and supplies.

Preferred Qualifications
- Strong communication skills with the ability to lead and mentor teams effectively.
- Experience delivering safety training sessions, drills, or scenario updates.
- Demonstrated ability to collaborate across departments and drive safety initiatives.
- Familiarity with continuous improvement processes and safety-related project planning.
- Passion for fostering a safe workplace and contributing to team development.

title: Graduate Talent (CPU-SoC Silicon Design)
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

In this position, you will be involving in the training, design and development of next generation SOC/CPU for wide range of Intel products. Your responsibilities will include some of the following but not limited to:

  • Assist design unit owner in Register Transfer Level RTL model functional validation. Use CAD tool extensively to simulate logic behavior and circuit performance and direction of physical design for next generation, deep sub-micron embedded circuit solutions. Verify the circuit behavior against the original simulation model and first silicon.
  • Define VLSI Structural Design methodology and developing design flows. Implement structural physical designs, such as synthesis, floor planning, power-grid and clock tree designs, timing budgeting and closure, place and route, RC-extraction and integration. Such tasks may include: Circuit design of high speed clocking related circuits [phase-locked loop PLL, delay-locked loop DLL, bandgap] or high voltage input/output IO [double data rate DDR/LPDDR, General-purpose input/output GPIO, OPIO].
  • Responsible for Integration of Third party IPs -- Synthesis, functional and/or timing convergence, and pre and post-si debug of IPs developed by various external vendors as well as within the company. Handling of signals crossing power planes and clock domains, industry standard protocols including hardware and software details dealing with Memory LPDDR, storage eMMC, SATA, UFS, peripherals PCIe, USB, and MIPI interfaces in SOC devices. System integration dealing with Si/ Platform/ FW/ MW/ drivers/ OS/ Apps on Android Windows-based tablets and phones.

You must possess a Bachelor of Engineering degree or a Master of Science degree in Electronic, Electrical or Computer Engineering.

  • Familiarity with Very Large Scale Integration VLSI Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor CMOS logic circuit design
  • Well versed in UNIX, C programming and relevant Computer Aided Design CAD tools.

title: Product Quality and Reliability Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The Product Quality and Reliability Modeling Engineer develops reliability models and risk assessments that enable successful qualification and launch of advanced semiconductor products. Working across Product Quality & Reliability, Design, Process, Manufacturing, and Foundry teams, this role applies device physics, reliability engineering, statistical analysis, and data science to predict product reliability, identify risks, and drive data-driven decisions throughout the product lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute reliability models to assess product lifetime and qualification readiness.  
  • Evaluate failure mechanisms including EM, TDDB, BTI, HCI, thermal and package-related degradation.
  • Analyze qualification, characterization, and manufacturing data to quantify reliability risk.
  • Conduct reliability projections, scenario analysis, and risk assessments for new product features and technologies.
  • Drive cross-functional investigations and resolution of reliability concerns.
  • Improve modeling methodologies, automation, and predictive analytics capabilities.
  • Present reliability recommendations to technical and management stakeholders.

In this role, you will serve as a senior technical contributor responsible for designing, implementing, automating, and supporting enterprise-scale application delivery and load-balancing solutions. descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

The world is transforming - and so is Intel. Intel is a company of bold and curious inventors and problem solvers who create some of the most astounding technology advancements and experiences in the world. With a legacy of relentless innovation and a commitment to bring smart, connected devices to every person on Earth, our diverse and brilliant teams are continually searching for tomorrow's technology and revel in the challenge that changing the world for the better brings. We work every single day to design and manufacture silicon products that empower people's digital lives. Come join us and do something wonderful.


Business group

Intel Integrated Photonics Solutions (IPS), part of the Data Center Group, is a leader in silicon photonics integration. Our team drives innovation through advanced technology and scalable, high-volume manufacturing of silicon photonics products. We are committed to developing next-generation optical connectivity solutions that enable continued data center bandwidth growth through smaller form factors, co-packaged optics, and data rates scaling from 400G today to 3.2T and beyond.
 

The Role and Impact

We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Analog Design Engineer to join our growing team and help accelerate the development of industry-leading silicon photonics solutions. As a Senior Analog Design Engineer, you will contribute to the Silicon Photonics Solutions Group's mission of transforming data center connectivity and strengthening Intel's leadership in networking technologies.


In this role, you will be responsible for:

  • The architecture, design, implementation, and validation of high-speed analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits used in advanced optical interconnect products.
  • You will collaborate closely with cross-functional design teams to deliver innovative solutions from concept through production.
  • Define circuit architectures and develop designs that meet power, performance, and functionality requirements for next-generation optical interconnects.
  • Lead block-level design and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to deliver key integrated circuit components.
  • Architect, design, and validate high-speed, low-voltage, low-power analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits.
  • Work closely with digital design teams to ensure successful integration and product execution.

descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

This role requires regular onsite presence to support the successful development, ramp, and ongoing operation of a high-volume manufacturing or technology development fabrication facility. The position provides both tactical and strategic operational support, leveraging technical expertise to enable new product introductions (NPI), optimize factory performance, and sustain manufacturing operations.

Key Responsibilities

Manufacturing Operations & Process Improvement

  • Support new product introduction (NPI) builds and sustain manufacturing processes throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Define manufacturing requirements, evaluate manufacturing technologies, and develop manufacturing and supply chain plans to support production goals.
  • Analyze and improve existing manufacturing processes, identifying opportunities for optimization and correcting process deviations.
  • Inspect and assess machinery, equipment, and tooling performance, initiating corrective actions for identified issues.
  • Analyze key factory metrics and drive initiatives that improve overall operational performance, capacity, and factory health.

Data Analytics & Decision Support

  • Develop and implement manufacturing decision-support tools, methodologies, and operational standards.
  • Analyze data to identify system enhancements and optimization opportunities and drive implementation roadmaps.
  • Develop, enhance, and troubleshoot factory reporting systems to provide actionable operational insights.
  • Partner with automation teams to create business systems and processes that monitor and improve factory performance.

Stakeholder Collaboration & Operational Support

  • Collaborate with factory operations management, engineering, automation teams, and supply chain partners to align manufacturing strategies with operational goals.
  • Support Manufacturing Operations Managers and their teams in achieving output and performance objectives.
  • Work cross-functionally to resolve issues affecting factory operations, capacity, productivity, and overall manufacturing effectiveness.
  • Provide guidance to product, module, and supply chain engineering teams throughout equipment selection, design, qualification, and implementation.

Manufacturing Systems & Documentation

  • Develop and maintain manufacturing documentation supporting product design, configuration, process requirements, and build execution.
  • Define and drive requirements for automation station controllers and manufacturing systems supporting key product roadmaps.
  • Own and manage factory support equipment, including:
    • Command center workstations
    • Factory laptops
    • Small form factor manufacturing devices and compute elements (e.g., Intel NUCs)
    • Associated factory support equipment and infrastructure

Impact

This role serves as a critical link between manufacturing operations, engineering, automation, and supply chain organizations, ensuring efficient factory execution, continuous improvement, and scalable manufacturing solutions that support current and future product roadmaps.

Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Research, or a related engineering discipline, with at least 2 years of relevant professional experience; or a Master’s degree in one of these fields, with at least 1 year of relevant professional experience.

Experience listed above should be a combination of the following:

  • Experience in semiconductor manufacturing, foundry operations, industrial engineering, or operations research within a high-volume production environment.

- Strong communication and leadership skills with the ability to translate complex manufacturing and optimization challenges into clear operational actions, manage customer-facing delivery commitments, and influence cross-functional teams including Finance, Industrial Engineering, Global Supply Management, Process Engineering, and Automation at all levels of the organization.

title: Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Job Details:

Job Description: 

Intel is seeking a highly qualified candidate to join our ASIC design verification team in a dynamic and forward-thinking organization focused on next-generation semiconductor product development. Our team focuses on being nimble, adaptable, lean and efficient to drive cutting-edge, customer impacting technology development. We embrace innovative and efficient methodologies that drive at-scale product execution. Advance your career with cutting-edge verification techniques including coverage-driven verification, formal methods, and performance analysis. Lead custom SystemVerilog/UVM development, master industry-standard EDA tools, architect verification strategies for complex ASICs, and mentor emerging talent while independently driving verification closure. Join our fast-paced semiconductor team where your technical leadership shapes next-generation chip development through comprehensive methodologies and innovative verification solutions. Transform challenging projects into career-defining achievements. If you are passionate about building products faster and more efficiently than anyone else on the planet, we want you on our team.


Key Responsibilities:
• Define Project Specific Verification Strategy: Defines and implement scalable and reusable verification plans, test benches, and the verification environments for blocks, subsystems, and SoCs. Ensure meeting the required coverage levels and confirm to microarchitecture specifications.
• Lead Verification Execution: Create detailed test plans and drives technical reviews with design and architecture teams to validate these plans and proofs.
• Executes verification plan: Implement and run block/subsystem/cluster/soc simulation models to verify the design, analyze power and performance, and identify bugs.
• Investigate and Resolve Bugs: Replicates, root causes, and debugs issues in the pre-silicon environment. Finds and implements corrective measures to resolve failing tests.
• Collaborate Across Teams: Work closely with SoC architects, micro architects, full chip architects, RTL developers, post-silicon, and physical design teams to improve verification of complex architectural and microarchitectural features.
• Enhance Future Verification Methodologies: Continuously improves existing functional verification infrastructure and methodologies.
• Absorbs learnings: From post-silicon on the quality of validation done during pre-silicon development, updates test plan for missing coverages and proliferates to future products.
• Lead and mentor others: inspire and guide junior engineers, fostering their growth and development.

Your expertise will be instrumental in cultivating a collaborative and innovative environment where every team member thrives.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications: You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or in other relevant STEM related degree. • 6+ years of experience in ASIC/FPGA design verification • Strong understanding of object-oriented programming (OOP) principles and their application in SystemVerilog UVM or other verification methodologies. • Developing UVM and/or Formal based verification architectures and methodologies. • Experience with industry standard protocols (AMBA AXI/AXI-S/CHI and Low-speed communication protocols (UART, SPI, I2C/I3C)) • Hands-on experience with simulators (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium, or equivalent). • Familiarity with coverage-driven verification, constrained-random testing and strong debugging skills. • Experience with scripting languages. Preferred Qualifications: • Graduate/post-graduate degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or any STEM related degree with overall 8+ yrs. of experience. • Skilled in various validation concepts and debug techniques relevant to ASIC/FPGA domain. • Collaborative, able to communicate well with counter parts and stakeholders. Strong written and verbal communication skills. • Strong analytical ability and problem-solving skills. • Experience in defining testbench architecture, constrained random verification methodologies. • Experience in processor-based verification using C/C++ with UVM-based verification environments. • Define and execute validation of IPs and/or SOC from spec to tape-in including setting verification strategy, creating test bench and components, defining test plan, writing tests, debugging, coverage and analysis. • Low power experience (e.g., UPF). • Experience in AMBA, CXS stream, DDR, PCIe and/or Ethernet, UCIe protocols. • Experience in EDA tools and reusable testbench for subsystem and SoC that deploys 3rd party VIPs. • Experience with formal verification techniques and tools is an asset.
